props.name: dark
props.description: Force the dark color scheme.

props.name: light
props.description: Force the light color scheme.

props.name: scheme
props.description: Legacy value form of the scheme axis ("light" | "dark"), kept for back-compat and for config-driven code that already holds a `ColorScheme` value (a stored preference, an <html> hook). The boolean axis above wins when both are passed.

props.name: ssrScheme
props.description: The scheme the SERVER rendered, for SSR/SSG apps (Next.js and the like) whose client scheme can differ from it (a stored preference, the OS). Canvas resolves colors in JS and serializes them into the server HTML as literal inline styles, so when the hydration render disagrees with that HTML, React logs a mismatch and keeps the server's colors on any element that never re-renders again: components stay stuck in the server's scheme. With `ssrScheme` set, the provider renders it on the server AND for the hydration render (matching the server HTML exactly), then applies the requested scheme (the boolean axis or the legacy `scheme` prop) right after mount; that switch re-renders every consumer, which writes the real colors to the DOM. Pass the same value the server resolves (e.g. the next-themes `defaultTheme`). Omit in client-only apps and on native.

props.name: violet
props.description: Paint the accent violet (hue 285), the default.

props.name: cyan
props.description: Paint the accent cyan (hue 205).

props.name: mint
props.description: Paint the accent mint (hue 165).

props.name: rose
props.description: Paint the accent rose (hue 20).

props.name: amber
props.description: Paint the accent amber (hue 75).

props.name: ssrPalette
props.description: The palette the SERVER rendered, for SSR/SSG apps whose client palette can differ from it (a stored preference: `getPalette()` reads one on the web). The `ssrScheme` contract applied to the palette axis: the server render and the hydration render paint this palette, matching the server HTML exactly, and the requested one (`cyan`, `mint` and so on) applies right after mount. Omit in client-only apps and on native.

props.name: ssrBreakpoint
props.description: The breakpoint bucket the SERVER should assume, for SSR/SSG apps (the `ssrScheme` contract applied to the viewport axis). The server cannot measure a window, so `useBreakpoint`/`useResponsive`/`useFormFactor` resolve to the desktop `base` there by default; an app that knows it is serving a narrow client (UA hints) passes the bucket the server should render instead (e.g. "sm" for phones). The server render and the hydration render use it, then the real measured bucket re-renders every consumer right after hydration. Omit in client-only apps and on native.

props.name: glass
props.description: Request role-appropriate glass: stable content material and functional Liquid Glass where supported. Semantic tokens remain opaque.

props.name: solid
props.description: Request complete opaque surfaces without glass effects, even on iOS 26+.

props.name: surface
props.description: Legacy value form of the surface axis ("solid" | "glass"), kept for back-compat and for config-driven code that already holds a `Surface` value. The boolean axis above wins when both are passed.

props.name: tokens
props.description: Brand token overrides, merged over the active palette's base tokens so a consumer can rebrand the kit (e.g. `tokens={{ primary: "#7c3aed" }}`) without forking the token files. Pass a flat `Partial<ColorTokens>` to apply the same overrides to both schemes, or `{ light, dark }` to override each scheme separately. These are the SEMANTIC tokens only; the glass material carries its own fill (`glassByScheme`) and is never rewritten by a rebrand, so the two are independent. Pass a stable reference (a module constant or a memoized object); an inline literal re-creates the theme value on every render. Unlike `fonts`, a nested ThemeProvider does not inherit a parent's `tokens`: a nested provider is how a subtree shows its own palette or brand, so it paints its palette unbranded unless it is given overrides of its own. Pass the same constant again to carry a rebrand into a nested provider.

props.name: fonts
props.description: The typefaces the app registered, so the kit can paint its labels in the brand faces (`typeface.sans` is Instrument Sans, `typeface.display` Bricolage Grotesque, `typeface.mono` JetBrains Mono). Each entry is either one family name that carries every weight (a variable font, an OS-installed family) or a map from weight to the face registered for that weight (expo-google-fonts style: `{ "400": "InstrumentSans_400Regular", "500": "InstrumentSans_500Medium" }`). Pass it once, on the app's root provider: the faces are what the app loaded, not a per-subtree choice, so a nested ThemeProvider that omits `fonts` keeps the nearest parent provider's, and one that passes it uses its own map in place of the parent's (the roles are not merged; a stable empty map, `{}`, returns that subtree to the system face). Omit it on the root and the kit renders in the platform's system face, as it always has. Pass a stable reference (a module constant); an inline literal re-creates the theme value on every render.

groups.title: Scheme axis
groups.note: Scheme axis (pick one; omit both to follow the OS appearance). The color scheme spelled like every other Canvas axis: the prop name is the value. `dark` wins when both are passed.

groups.title: Palette axis
groups.note: Palette axis (pick one; omit for the default, violet). The accent hue, spelled like every other axis: the prop name is the value. It applies in both schemes. When more than one is passed the first in this order wins: cyan, mint, rose, amber, violet.

groups.title: Surface axis
groups.note: Surface axis (pick one; omit for the platform default: glass on iOS 26+, the native system material for that layer, solid elsewhere). The theming-level glass switch, spelled like every other Canvas axis; there is no per-component glass prop. `glass` wins when both are passed.

platformNotes.web:
Section panel with headline, body text, and one action. Used to surface a single decision or call-to-action.

The panel is the v4 hand-off's on every platform (no platform ships an action panel): an 18 px inset at the card corner on a hairline over the card fill, a 600 15 title over a 13 px muted description. The action is an outline Button; `destructive` washes the panel in the danger tint, edges it in the destructive colour and makes the action destructive; `inline` pins the action beside the copy, wrapping it underneath when the panel is narrow. Embedded `children` sit under the copy, and the Button then closes the panel on the right as the primary action that commits them.

components.name: ActionSheet
components.description: A modal sheet of contextual actions, the iOS action sheet idiom: a bottom sheet of choices summoned in response to a user action, over a dimmed scrim that glass on the web also blurs.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled (a `trigger` opens it).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fired when the open state changes (trigger press, scrim tap, Cancel, an action, back/escape).

props.name: trigger
props.description: Label for an optional trigger button. When set, the sheet renders the button and opens itself on press (uncontrolled). Omit when you drive `open` yourself.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional header title (a left-aligned primary-label heading on iOS, a short centered heading on web, left-aligned on Android).

props.name: message
props.description: Optional header message under the title.

props.name: actions
props.description: The action rows. Each runs its `onPress` then closes the sheet.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: The Cancel row label (default "Cancel").

props.name: embedded
props.description: Show the open sheet as a non-modal specimen inside its parent, for a catalogue or a showcase: the stack rests against the parent's bottom edge (the parent gives it its height) over the dim, with no Modal, no rise, no focus trap and no close on Escape, native back or a tap on the dim. Its rows still run their actions. Ignored with `trigger`, which always opens a live sheet.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition for the bottom-anchored stack, composed onto the stack container; not a restyle hook. (The device's bottom safe-area inset is applied automatically, so it clears the home indicator without a manual `paddingBottom`.)

platformNotes.web:
A modal sheet of contextual actions, the iOS action sheet idiom:
a bottom sheet
of choices summoned in response to a user action, over a dimmed scrim that glass
on the web also blurs.

It poses an optional title and message, lists a set of actions (any of which can
be destructive), and offers a Cancel. Selecting an action runs it and closes the
sheet; tapping the scrim or Cancel closes it without acting. Pass a `trigger`
label for a self-contained button that opens the sheet, or drive `open` /
`onOpenChange` yourself. For a small contextual menu anchored to a control,
reach for Dropdown or RowMenu instead.

On the web the sheet is two cards a little off the window's edges: a centered header
over full-width rows in the accent's ink (a destructive one in the error ink), each under
a hairline, and a separate Cancel card.
iOS keeps its Liquid Glass sheet with detached
capsules, and Android the Material 3 bottom sheet with a drag handle and list rows.

iOS accessibility escape and Android system back request cancellation without
running an action.
An open child overlay handles the request first. Disabled
actions do not disable cancellation, and a controlled owner can keep the sheet
open. The visible Cancel row remains available to assistive technology.

components.name: Alert
components.description: Inline notification banners: info, success, warning, and destructive, plus a full-width announcement bar. For a blocking confirmation prompt, see Alert Dialog.

props.name: title
props.description: Content.

props.name: description
props.description: Content.

props.name: icon
props.description: The leading glyph: an element (an `<Icon />`, tinted to the tone's color unless it sets its own, and sized to the banner's glyph) or a single text character. Omitted, the banner draws its tone's own glyph (an info circle on info and neutral, a check on success, an alert circle on warning, a cross on destructive); `null` draws none.

props.name: info
props.description: Tone (pick one; omit for the neutral default).

props.name: success
props.description: Tone (pick one; omit for the neutral default).

props.name: warning
props.description: Tone (pick one; omit for the neutral default).

props.name: destructive
props.description: The danger tone. This is the name the intent axis uses across the kit (Button, AlertDialog, and every chart) and the one the design hand-off uses here too.

props.name: announcement
props.description: The announcement bar: one line on the accent gradient (the accent running into the cyan series hue) in the accent's own ink, under its glow, with its `action` inline at the end. For page-wide news ("v4 is live"), not for a status. It is its own look, so it ignores the tone axis.

props.name: action
props.description: One action, as a label and a handler. On the announcement bar it sits inline at the end of the line, in the bar's ink; on the other looks it is a link Button in the actions region, before any `actions`.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Shows a trailing dismiss control. Pressing it hides the banner out of the box (uncontrolled); pass `dismissed` to own that state instead.

props.name: dismissed
props.description: Controlled dismissal: `true` hides the banner. Omit to let the Alert manage it.

props.name: defaultDismissed
props.description: Uncontrolled seed: start hidden. Rarely useful; defaults to false.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Fired when the dismiss control is pressed (both modes).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: actions
props.description: A footer action region rendered under the body. The Alert owns the layout: it separates the actions from the description above and lays the buttons out in a row, so a call site passes the buttons directly (`actions={<Button primary small>Upgrade plan</Button>}`) with no wrapper. Pass a fragment for more than one action.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Tone
groups.note: Tone (pick one; omit for the neutral default).

platformNotes.web:
Inline notification banners: info, success, warning, and destructive, plus a full-width announcement bar. For a blocking confirmation prompt, see Alert Dialog.

A banner fills the parent it is given, so a column of alerts is the same measure top to bottom and a banner over a form lines up with the fields; a Container step sets the measure when the layout calls for one.

A banner is a soft callout: the tone's wash under a 1px edge of the tone's color, the tone's own glyph in that color, a foreground title and a muted body, from `statusColors` (the helper Badge and every toned surface read). The neutral banner is the quiet muted surface with an info glyph in the muted ink. Pass `icon` to draw another glyph (an `<Icon />` takes the tone's color and the banner's 18px size), or `icon={null}` to draw none.

props.name: description
props.description: Content (strings).

props.name: trigger
props.description: Trigger button label. When set, the dialog renders the button and opens itself on press (uncontrolled). Omit when you drive `open` yourself.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: Action labels.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: Action labels.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled (the trigger opens it).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fired when the open state changes (trigger press, confirm, cancel).

props.name: withInput
props.description: Body: render a confirmation field that gates confirm. The user must type the `confirmText` token (default "DELETE") for the confirm action to enable; until it matches exactly, confirm is disabled and `handleConfirm` is a no-op. This is a real safety gate, not a decorative field.

props.name: confirmText
props.description: The token the confirmation field must match to enable confirm (default "DELETE"). Only used when `withInput` is set; drives the placeholder ("type DELETE to confirm"), the field's accessible name, and the gate.

props.description: Action handlers.

props.name: onCancel

props.name: overlay
props.description: Presents the confirm OVER the page instead of inline where it is mounted. The default is a contained overlay, which the docs catalogue needs to show one inside an example stage. An application asking to confirm a destructive action needs the opposite: inline, the scrim appears wherever the component happens to sit, the page behind stays scrollable and clickable, and the dialog still claims `aria-modal`. Teleports into the nearest `OverlayProvider`; with none in the tree it renders in place.

props.name: embedded
props.description: Show the open dialog as a non-modal specimen in the page, for a catalogue or a showcase: it keeps its look, its alertdialog role and its labelling, but does not take focus when it opens, trap Tab, return focus, claim `aria-modal`, or cancel on Escape or native back. Ignored with `trigger`, which always opens a live modal.

props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.description: Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook.

platformNotes.web:
Catalyst-style confirmation dialog: a centered panel over a dimmed backdrop, which glass on the web also blurs, with a title, description, optional body, and action buttons. Reserve it for decisions that must block the rest of the app.

On the web and Android the panel leads with a tone tile (a trash glyph on the
destructive wash, otherwise an info glyph on the accent's), then a display title over
its description, and closes on two equal buttons: a secondary Cancel and the primary or
destructive confirm.
On iOS it is the system alert: centered text over a two-cell action
row under a hairline, the confirm in the error ink when destructive.

Browser Escape and iOS accessibility escape cancel the dialog,
clear its
confirmation field and request `open=false`. The confirmation text gates only
the confirm action; cancellation remains available while confirm is disabled.
An open child overlay handles dismissal first. A controlled owner can refuse
closure without passing that request to a parent or calling `onConfirm`.

Add `embedded` to show an open alert dialog in a page as a specimen, the way a
catalogue or a showcase does: it keeps its look, its alertdialog role and its
labelling, but it is not modal. It does not take focus when it opens, trap Tab,
return focus, set `aria-modal`, or cancel on Escape or native back, so the page
around it keeps its scroll position and its keyboard order. `embedded` is ignored
with `trigger`, which always opens a live modal.

platformNotes.web:
The app's root frame and its scrolling screens. `AppFrame` mounts the safe-area context and the app-root overlay host, pads all four safe-area edges over the theme background, renders the app's top chrome in a banner region and lets its body (a router's Stack) fill the height left. `Page` is one screen inside it: the main region, a scroller with page gutters whose content is capped and centered at a step of the width scale.

Mount `AppFrame` once, inside `ThemeProvider`, at the root of the app. It is the app-root `OverlayProvider` itself, so menus, sheets and toasts render above the whole window and keep clear of the status bar, the Dynamic Island and the home indicator; do not mount a second root host around it. The safe-area context comes from `react-native-safe-area-context` when the app installs it (Expo Router apps already do); without it the frame keeps its layout and the insets resolve to 0.

Each screen renders a `Page`. Its content stacks at the loose rhythm and is capped at `widest` (1152) by default, the reading width of an app page on a desktop window; below the cap it fills the window between its gutters, which is all a phone is. A measure step (`xxxs` through `page`) narrows or widens it, `start` pins it to the leading edge, and `fluid` removes the cap. The page is also an overlay host of its own, so an anchored menu opened in it is framed by the page.

platformNotes.web:
Text input + dropdown: searchable single-select.

Pass `label` (and `required`) to name the field:
iOS and web render the label
above the field, while Android floats the Material 3 in-container label once the
list opens or a value fills the field. On Android the field grows with the
user's text size, and a label longer than the field truncates on one line clear
of the toggle while the field's accessible name stays the whole label.
The required
star is decorative: a screen reader hears the field as required,
from
`aria-required` on the web and from its name ("Assigned to, required") on iOS and
Android.
The field fills the parent it is given; a
step of its own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with `start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a
Container step sets its measure.

On web the field is the Canvas v4 search field: 40px tall (32 small, 48 large) on
the sunken fill behind the `field-border` hairline, a leading 16px search glyph, a
400 14px value (13 small) and a 15px chevrons-up-down 10px from its end. The
pointer darkens the edge to the subtle ink, and focus rings it in the accent with a
4px halo. The suggestions are a card 6px under the field with a 4px inset and 34px
rows; the typed letters are marked in each suggestion on the accent's soft wash, and
the chosen suggestion sits on the `muted` wash.
iOS ships no combo box, so it draws
the same field and card at the iOS corners.
Android keeps the Material 3 exposed
dropdown: the filled field with its active indicator and drop-down triangle, and the
Material menu whose active and chosen rows take the state layer.

In glass mode the suggestion list is a dense-layer glass card under the field (or
above it when it fits there); the field, its caret and its toggle stay in place,
and picking a suggestion commits the value at once. Solid mode paints the skin's
own list.

Arrow Down and Arrow Up open the list and highlight an option while focus stays in the text field. Navigation stops at the first and last matches. Home and End jump to those limits once an option is highlighted; otherwise they retain their text-editing behavior. Enter chooses the highlighted option, Escape closes the list without changing the query, and Tab closes it while moving focus. Typing resets the highlight. Confirming an input-method candidate does not select an option or submit a surrounding Form.

Use `value` with `onValueChange` to control the selection, and use `""` for a controlled empty value. The callback reports selections and clearing the field. `onSelect` remains a selection-only notification. The independent `query`/`onQueryChange` pair controls filtering; choosing an option resets the query to `""`.

The disclosure button has a real target of at least 24px on web, 44pt on iOS, and 48dp on Android.
The small iOS field keeps a 44pt height so its touch target fits inside the field; its typography remains compact.

An option can carry a short `detail` (a version, a platform, a count): pass
`{ label, detail }` objects in place of strings, and the detail sits at the row's end
in the 11px mono face in the subtle ink.
Android sets it in the row's type and muted ink.
The label is what the query matches and what `value` holds; the row is announced as
"label, detail".

components.name: Avatar
components.description: A photo when the account has one, falling back to one or two initials on an identity disc: the name resolves to one of ten hues (or `hue` picks one), and the disc is that hue's soft wash under initials in the same hue, so one person keeps one colour on every platform and stays distinct in a stack or list. The initials sit at weight 600, 38% of the disc, and their ink is held to 4.5:1 on the wash in both schemes.

props.name: account
props.description: Original Argus account control with a 32px orchid disc and compact role menu.

props.name: triggerLabel
props.description: Explicit name for the trigger.

props.name: menuLabel
props.description: Menu heading and accessible name, independent of the account's identity lines.

props.name: name
props.description: The account holder's full name: the pill's first line, the avatar's initials fallback and colour identity, and the menu header's title.

props.name: email
props.description: The secondary line under the name in the pill, and the menu header's description (typically the account's email address).

props.name: src
props.description: The account photo. Falls back to the initials exactly like `Avatar`.

props.name: initials
props.description: Ready-made initials for the avatar, used verbatim when there is no photo.

props.name: items
props.description: The menu rows, top to bottom. Same rows as `Dropdown` (icon, shortcut, destructive, disabled, separatorBefore).

props.name: compact
props.description: Avatar and chevron only, no name block: the topbar form of the pill.

props.name: alignStart
props.description: Hang the menu from the pill's LEADING edge instead of its trailing one.

props.name: alignEnd
props.description: The default, spelled out: the menu's trailing edge meets the pill's.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dimmed, non-opening pill: the menu never opens and the press is inert.

props.name: inline
props.description: Draw the menu open and in flow under the pill instead of floating it over the page, a specimen of the account menu (Dropdown's `inline`): the pill reads as open and its press is inert, a row still fires `onSelect`, and `open` / `onOpenChange` have no effect.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled (the pill opens/closes it).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fired when the open state changes (pill press, row select, dismissal).

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fired with the selected row and its index when a menu row is pressed.

platformNotes.web:
A photo when the account has one, falling back to one or two initials on an identity disc: the name resolves to one of ten hues (or `hue` picks one), and the disc is that hue's soft wash under initials in the same hue, so one person keeps one colour on every platform and stays distinct in a stack or list. The initials sit at weight 600, 38% of the disc, and their ink is held to 4.5:1 on the wash in both schemes.

Like a photo, the disc is identity content: it keeps its colours under glass, where only the neutral tile of an avatar with no name or initials takes the control material. `AvatarMenu` builds the signed-in account control on the same circle: one capsule trigger carrying the avatar, the name, and the email, opening the account menu under that same identity.

Argus identity sizes are available as `annotation` (16), `compact` (30), `account`
(32), `row` (36), `person` (38), `profile` (44), `detail` (52), `hero` (58),
`featured` (60), and `spotlight` (74), in that precedence order. These retain their
reference initials metrics, including the existing 9px annotation glyph.

`hue` selects a stage identity independently of its name. `whiteInk` preserves
white reference initials; `bold` uses the 700 weight. `sheen`, `mediumSheen`, and
`strongSheen` add the 2, 2.5 and 3px conic ring (strongest wins). `inverse` is the
translucent white identity disc, `orchid` the account gradient, and `glow` its
selected account ring. These reference discs keep the identity gradient. On the four
stock sizes, `glow` is a 2px gap in the page colour inside the accent's soft glow, and
`ring` stays the separator ring a stack draws between discs.

components.name: Badge
components.description: Two families on one Badge component, picked by boolean props. The metadata badge labels a schema, role, or tag: with no tone it is the accent's soft pill, and the tones give `default` the solid call-to-action pill, `secondary` the quiet surface pill, `outline` a hairline pill and `destructive` the soft red pill; add `mono` for token names. A status tone (`success`, `warning`, `error`, `info`, `neutral`) paints the pill in that tone's wash and ink and leads it with a dot. The status badge (`status`) has no pill: a dot in the tone's color, ringed in its wash, beside a muted label, for live state like active, pending, or failed.

props.name: status
props.description: Family: metadata badge (default) vs. status badge (with a dot).

props.name: soft
props.description: Soft intent fill with matching ink (every toned pill is soft; kept for the intent grammar).

props.name: neutralFill
props.description: Neutral border-colored fill.

props.description: Foreground ink on the quiet surface.

props.description: The small pill: 18 px tall, 11 px label.

props.name: tiny
props.description: The tiny pill: 18 px tall under a 10 px label on the pill's own 18 px line, at the regular weight even when solid (a navigation row's "New" tag beside its count).

props.name: count
props.description: A count at the small size with the heavier label.

props.name: navigationCount
props.description: Solid count used in navigation.

props.name: notification
props.description: Compact counter carried by a notification control.

props.name: reference
props.description: A linked reference key at the key corner, in the code face.

props.name: token
props.description: A code token chip: the 22 px pill with its 8 px inset under the small 11 px label in the code face, for a role, a state or an attribute name beside its term.

props.name: large
props.description: The large pill: 26 px tall.

props.name: marker
props.description: An anatomy figure's numbered marker: a 22 px disc on the accent with its number in the code face, set off from the stage by a ring of the stage's fill and a shadow (Component.dc.html line 220).

props.name: disc
props.description: A legend's numbered disc: the marker's 22 px disc with its number in the code face, in the tone axis's fill (the solid accent as `default`, the quiet surface as `secondary`) with no ring and no shadow (Component.dc.html line 222, the anatomy legend's part numbers).

props.name: tier
props.description: A tier pill (Atom, Molecule, Organism beside a page title): 24 px tall with a 10 px inset and a 500 11 px label on its own line (Component.dc.html line 139), tracked in caps with `uppercase` and in the code face with `mono`, as the page sets it.

props.name: band
props.description: A group band's pill (the props table's "pick one" beside an axis's title): 20 px tall with a 7 px inset and a 500 11 px label (Component.dc.html line 237), in the code face with `mono` as the page sets it, in the tone axis's fill (the accent's soft pill with none). It sits between `tier` and `small` in precedence.

props.name: tick
props.description: A ruler tick's pill (the Layout page's "this window" readout under its marker): 20 px tall with an 8 px inset and a 500 10 px label in the code face on the pill's own 20 px line, with no border and no tone dot. Usually with `contrast`. After `band` in precedence.

props.description: A numbered step mark (the Layout page's "try in this order" list): a 32 px square at the step mark's corner with its number 600 13 px in the code face, centred. In the tone axis's fill: `default` the solid accent with its glow, none the accent's soft wash, `secondary` the quiet surface inside the `field-border` edge in the second ink. Pass it as a MediaObject's `icon` with `bareIcon`. After `disc` in precedence.

props.description: The key cap's corner in place of the round pill's, on any size: the sizing legend's mode tags and the primitive names under a Grid (Layout.dc.html). The corner axis has this one member; `reference` and `step` keep their own corners.

props.name: dot
props.description: Show the intent dot without switching to the status family. With no children it is the bare 8 px dot in the tone's ink, with no pill (a marker beside text that names it).

props.description: Standalone 10px signal marker, retaining its status label.

On the tone axis after `default`; under glass the ink at the dense alpha, as the Tooltip bubble's, so its label keeps its contrast.

platformNotes.web:
Two families on one Badge component, picked by boolean props. The metadata badge labels a schema, role, or tag: with no tone it is the accent's soft pill, and the tones give `default` the solid call-to-action pill, `secondary` the quiet surface pill, `outline` a hairline pill and `destructive` the soft red pill; add `mono` for token names. A status tone (`success`, `warning`, `error`, `info`, `neutral`) paints the pill in that tone's wash and ink and leads it with a dot. The status badge (`status`) has no pill: a dot in the tone's color, ringed in its wash, beside a muted label, for live state like active, pending, or failed.

The tone colors come from `statusColors`, the helper every toned surface in the kit reads, so a warning badge and a warning alert are the same state, and every ink is the solved text role that keeps 4.5:1 on its wash.

`contrast` is the most prominent neutral: the scheme's ink (`foreground`) as the fill under the page colour as the label (under glass, the ink at the dense alpha, as the Tooltip bubble's). `dashed` is the placeholder outline: no fill inside a dashed `field-border` edge, the label in the second ink.

If more than one tone is passed, Badge resolves the highest-precedence one: `default` > `contrast` > `destructive` > `secondary` > `outline` > `dashed` for metadata (the accent's soft pill when none is passed), and `success` > `error` > `warning` > `info` > `neutral` for status (`neutral` when none is passed). The metadata tones win over a status tone's colors; the status tone's dot stays.

`cyan` and `mint` paint a metadata pill in a fixed series hue, the same whatever the palette (the hand-off's `--cyan` and `--mint`, the `chart-2` and `chart-3` tokens): the hue's 16% wash under its ink, solved to 4.5:1 on the wash, with no dot. They sit after the status tones in precedence (`success` > `warning` > `error` > `info` > `cyan` > `mint`), so a section can name three tiers mint, cyan and the accent and keep them apart under every palette.

Lay out a series of badges with `BadgeGroup`, a wrapping row that owns the gap (`tight` 4 / `compact` 6 / `snug` 8 / `cozy` 12, default `compact`, the hand-off's 6; the largest gap passed wins: `cozy` > `snug` > `compact` > `tight`) and centers its badges, so a call site never hand-rolls a flex row around them. Give it an `accessibilityLabel` (say, "Rachel Chen's roles") and it is announced as a named group that keeps its badges' text; without one it is a plain row.

The pill is 22 px tall with a 12 px label; `small` is 18 px with an 11 px label and `large` 26 px. `count` is the small pill with the heavier label, `navigationCount` the small solid count, and `reference` a linked key at the 6 px key corner in the code face, underlined, with an arrow when it has an `href`. `token` is a code token chip, the 22 px pill under the small 11 px label in the code face, for a role, a state or an attribute name listed beside its term; `tier` is a tier tag, a 24 px pill with a 10 px inset under an 11 px mono label in caps on its own line, the tag that names a component's tier beside its title, in whichever tone the tier takes. `tiny` is the 18 px pill under a 10 px label on its own line, at the regular weight even when `solid` (a navigation row's "New" tag). The metric precedence is `notification` > `marker` > `disc` > `step` > `reference` > `navigationCount` > `count` > `tier` > `band` > `tick` > `token` > `tiny` > `small`. `primary` and `action` take the accent's wash, `soft` names the soft wash every toned pill already has, `neutralFill` fills with the border color, `foreground` overrides the label ink, `dot` adds the leading dot without a status tone, and `inverse` and `solid` supply branded surfaces. `uppercase` tracks caps; `start` pins a badge in a host layout.

`notification` is a destructive count: a 20 px pill with a 600 11 px label, soft by default and solid with `solid`, set off from the page by a ring of the background; `action` adds a halo of the destructive wash. Button carries its own count when passed a `count`.

`signal` is the original standalone 10px status marker. It uses the existing
status-tone precedence and announces its supplied status label.

`marker` is an anatomy figure's numbered disc: a 22 px pill with no inset, its number 600 11 px in the code face on the accent (the solid call-to-action fill under its ink), set off from the stage by a 3 px ring of the stage well's fill (`surface-sunken`) and a drop shadow, the way the component page's Anatomy section numbers a specimen's parts. It wins over the other metrics but `notification`.

`disc` is the same 22 px numbered disc in a legend: the marker's disc and 600 11 px code-face number, in the tone axis's fill (`default` the solid accent for a part the figure draws, `secondary` the quiet surface for one it does not) with no ring and no shadow, the way the Anatomy legend numbers its rows. It sits below `marker` in precedence and above the pills.

`tier` is the tier pill beside a page title (Atom, Molecule, Organism): 24 px tall with a 10 px inset and a 500 11 px label on its own line, tracked in caps with `uppercase` and in the code face with `mono`, in the tone axis's fill. It sits above `small` in precedence.

`band` is a group band's pill, the "pick one" beside an axis's title in a props table: 20 px tall with a 7 px inset, no border, and a 500 11 px label, in the code face with `mono`, in the tone axis's fill (the accent's soft pill with none). It sits between `tier` and `small` in precedence; like `tick`, it never leads with a tone's dot.

`tick` is a ruler tick's readout: 20 px tall with an 8 px inset, no border and a 500 10 px label in the code face on the pill's own 20 px line, usually `contrast` (the Layout page's "this window" pill under its marker).

`step` is a numbered step mark: a 32 px square at the 10 px step corner with its number 600 13 px in the code face, centred, in the tone axis's fill: `default` the solid accent with the accent's glow beneath, none the accent's soft wash, `secondary` the quiet surface inside the `field-border` edge in the second ink. Pass it as a MediaObject's `icon` with `bareIcon` to number a list of steps.

`keyCorners` sets any pill at the key cap's 6 px corner in place of the round one (the corner axis has this one member); `reference` and `step` keep their own corners.

platformNotes.web:
Ranked label and value rows: each row is a proportional tone wash behind a truncating label, with a right-aligned mono value and an optional delta.

Bars size against the largest row by default (the ranking idiom); `share` sizes them against the sum of the rows and appends percent readouts (the composition idiom). Rows become drill-in buttons with `onPressItem`. For comparing magnitudes on a shared axis without deltas or shares, reach for the bar `Chart` and its `horizontal` mode instead.

components.name: Board
components.description: A data-driven kanban board: columns scroll horizontally, each column is a drop zone in a sunken well headed by its label and item count, and every card carries a drag grip, an optional trailing badge, a two-line description, a free-form chips slot, and an optional kebab menu.

props.name: plain
props.description: Unframed work lanes with custom domain cards.

props.name: pageScroll
props.description: Let the surrounding page own horizontal overflow instead of an inner scroller.

props.name: draggable
props.description: Enable drag handles and drop targets in plain lanes.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Temporarily prevent moves, for example while the consumer saves a drop.

props.name: renderItem
props.type: ((item: BoardItem, controls: { dragHandle: ReactNode; }) => ReactNode) | undefined
props.description: Custom plain card; place the supplied dragHandle alongside its domain actions.

props.name: bleed
props.description: Extend the scroller through its parent's horizontal inset.

props.name: columns
props.description: The columns (lanes), left to right.

props.name: items
props.description: CONTROLLED list; order within a column is array order filtered by `columnId`. The kit never mutates it: apply each `onMove` yourself (`applyBoardMove` is the standard reducer). Omit it (optionally passing `defaultItems`) for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultItems
props.description: Initial list for UNCONTROLLED use; Board then applies each move internally.

props.name: onItemsChange
props.description: Fired with the would-be next list after a drop, in both modes.

props.name: onMove
props.description: Fired on every completed drop with the computed move (source, target, index, neighbors).

props.name: onPressItem
props.description: Makes each card body pressable and reports the pressed item.

props.name: onSelectItemMenu
props.type: ((item: BoardItem, menuItem: RowMenuItem, menuIndex: number) => void) | undefined
props.description: Fired when a row of a card's kebab menu (`item.menu`) is selected.

props.name: columnWidth
props.description: Column width in px (default 300).

props.name: compact
props.description: Density axis (pass none for the default density).

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Message shown in an empty column (default "No items").

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only (width/flex), never a restyle hook.

groups.title: Density axis
groups.note: Density axis (pass none for the default density).

platformNotes.web:
A data-driven kanban board: columns scroll horizontally, each column is a drop zone in a sunken well headed by its label and item count, and every card carries a drag grip, an optional trailing badge, a two-line description, a free-form chips slot, and an optional kebab menu.

Dragging is the kit's own drag-and-drop family,
so it runs on iOS, Android, and the web from one code path
and stays keyboard- and screen-reader-operable: press Space on a grip to grab, the arrow keys to move between positions and columns, Space to drop, Escape to cancel. The list stays controlled: a drop reports a `BoardMove` (source, target, insertion index, and the new neighbor ids) through `onMove`, and `applyBoardMove` is the standard reducer to apply it. Pass `defaultItems` instead of `items` for uncontrolled use, where the board applies each move itself.

For an action-driven work board, `plain` drops the lane wells and keeps the lane
headers and dashed empty slots. `renderItem` supplies the domain card with its
own controls. Add `draggable` to enable drag grips and drop targets while retaining
the plain layout. A custom `renderItem` receives `{ dragHandle }` as its second
argument; place that supplied grip in the card's header. `disabled` prevents moves
while a consumer saves a change. `bleed`
extends horizontal scrolling through the owning container's inset.
Plain lanes share the Board's measured width equally, with a 168px minimum per
lane. Narrow containers scroll horizontally; long card text stays within its lane.

Add `pageScroll` when the surrounding page or content pane owns horizontal scrolling.
The Board then renders an overflow-visible lane row without an inner scrollport.
Plain lanes still fill the available content width equally down to their 168px
minimum; standard lanes keep their configured width. The surrounding scroll area
must allow horizontal overflow and keyboard scrolling. Card actions and drag grips
retain their keyboard behavior. Omit `pageScroll` to keep the default local scroller.

components.name: Button
components.description: Six intents × three sizes (plus the icon square) × disabled / focus / hover states. Always semantic: the intent communicates what the button does (default = the primary action, destructive = irreversible, ghost = chrome).

props.name: iconLeft
props.description: An icon element rendered before the label (e.g. a lucide or Canvas `Icon`). It renders directly (not wrapped in the label `Text`, which cannot host an SVG), spaced from the label by the skin's gap. Pass `iconLeft` alone with the `icon` size prop for an icon-only square button. The caller sizes the icon; a Canvas `Icon` with no tone of its own takes the button's label ink (the primary's contrast ink on a primary button, the muted ink on a quiet one, dimmed with the label while disabled), and an explicit tone keeps it.

props.name: iconRight
props.description: An icon element rendered after the label (e.g. a trailing chevron/arrow).

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessibility label, required for an icon-only button (no text to read).

props.name: href
props.description: Renders the button as a REAL link on the web: react-native-web gives the root Pressable an `<a href>`, so middle-click, cmd-click, open-in-new-tab, and crawlers all see the destination, and assistive tech hears a link. Native platforms have no anchors and ignore it, so pair `href` with an `onPress` that runs the same navigation through the host's router. While `disabled` or `loading` the anchor is suppressed, exactly like `onPress`.

props.name: hrefAttrs
props.type: { target?: "_blank" | "_self"; rel?: string; download?: boolean | string; } | undefined
props.description: Anchor attributes forwarded with `href` on the web (react-native-web's `hrefAttrs`): `target`, `rel`, `download`. Ignored without `href`, and everywhere natively.

platformNotes.web:
Six intents × three sizes (plus the icon square) × disabled / focus / hover states. Always semantic: the intent communicates what the button does (default = the primary action, destructive = irreversible, ghost = chrome).

On the web a button is 32, 40 or 48 tall (`small`, default, `large`) with the 10 px control corner, a 500-weight label at 13, 14 or 16 px, and an 8 px gap beside its icons. The call to action fills with the accent, `destructive` with the status red, both under a lit top edge; `secondary` is the quiet well with a boundary, `outline` the boundary alone, `ghost` and `link` bare (the link underlined). A filled button brightens and rises 1 px under the pointer over 150 ms and settles back when it leaves; the other looks take the well's wash at once. A press scales the button to 96% and darkens it, unless `steadyPress`. A disabled button fades to 40%; a loading one keeps its full look while its spinner runs. A disabled or loading button stays put, and Reduce Motion makes the lift instant.
On iOS the button is the 50 pt capsule with a semibold 17 pt label, on Android the 40 dp Material 3 stadium, both in the same colours.

Pass `ref` to access the interactive Pressable, including link buttons. Use `useRef<ComponentRef<typeof Button>>(null)` from React, or `useRef<View>(null)` with React Native's `View` type. Object and callback refs are supported and detach on unmount. Calling `ref.current?.focus()` or `.blur()` delegates to the host without activating the control. Browser focus is supported; native focus depends on the platform and React Native version, and is separate from accessibility focus.

`softHover` dims a link to 85% on hover in place of the wash. Inverse actions use
a translucent white hover wash over a branded surface.

Utility icon actions use `icon` with `compactIcon` (28), `mediumIcon` (32), or
`largeIcon` (34). `wideIcon` gives the compact box two extra pixels of
horizontal room; `circle` rounds it fully. Pair with `ghost` for a plain surface,
`outline` for a boundary, or `ghost inset` for a quiet fill. `steadyPress` keeps
the resting look while pressed, and `count` carries a notification badge over the
upper trailing corner. The button still owns its accessible name, hover wash, and
native touch-target extension.

Use `inlineLink link small` for an inline text action: an underlined 13-pixel
label with no box, read as a link and washed on hover. The default size is 14
pixels; `large` is 16. `extraBold`, `foreground`, and `inverse` set its weight and
ink. `external` opens `href` through the system browser on every platform, while
keeping its browser link semantics.

`plainLink` is a plain accent text action with no box and no underline, still read
as a button: a panel's Reset, a table's show-all row. On the web it is a 500 13 px
label in the accent text ink (12 px with `small`) that brightens to the foreground ink
under the pointer; natively it is the platform's own tint-coloured text button. Among
the bodies, `inlineLink` wins over `plainLink` when both are passed.

`scopeTrigger ghost steadyPress` is a bare 32 px menu trigger with a 600-weight
14px label; `filterTrigger ghost steadyPress` the same with a muted 13px label. Both
take the well's wash on hover. Supply the trailing chevron through `iconRight`, and
announce the menu with `expanded` and `haspopup`.

`identityAction` is a 28 px hairline pill around a leading avatar and its name;
`referenceLink` an underlined monospace key in the link ink; `inlineIcon` an unboxed
22 px icon action; `themeChoice` a 32 px pill around the theme's colour disc, a
`<Swatch tiny ring circle decorative>` passed through `iconLeft`, whose `selected` state is the
accent edge with a soft accent halo. `pageLink` is a page header's link, a 34 px hairline box
around a muted 13 px label (a page's section, its source); add `mono` when the label is a
path, which sets it in the 400 12 px mono face. `jumpLink` is a page's jump to one of its sections, a 28 px
hairline pill around a muted 500 12 px label. Both header links brighten their label to the
full ink and take the `secondary` wash under the pointer.

props.name: items

props.name: attached
props.description: Buttons joined in one hairline box on the raised fill, divided by full-height rules, the selected one on the raised step (an alignment or a view picker drawn as buttons rather than a track and thumb). It selects as `segmented` does and takes `active`, `defaultActive` and `block`.

props.name: decrementIcon
props.description: The stepper's decrement end, in place of its built-in glyph (a `zoomOut` Icon for a zoom control). The stepper kind only.

props.name: incrementIcon
props.description: The stepper's increment end, in place of its built-in glyph (a `zoomIn` Icon).

props.description: Related actions shown in the split kind's chevron dropdown.

props.name: compact
props.description: Density of the segmented row: the segments keep their size's height and take the small label on a 12 px inset (the hand-off component page's platform switch, a default-height track of 12 px labels). On the web only: a platform that ships the control keeps its one density. The split, stepper and spaced kinds ignore it.

props.name: rounded
props.description: A capsule segmented track with equal cells and a sliding selection thumb.

props.name: iconsOnly
props.description: Segmented/spaced only: each segment renders its `icon` alone and the item's `label` becomes the segment's ACCESSIBLE name (an icon-only view or form-factor switcher). An item without an icon keeps its visible label, with a dev-only warning. Split and stepper ignore it (dev-only warning).

props.name: steadyPress
props.description: Keep segmented and spaced cells at their resting opacity during a press.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the segmented row (the `tablist`), announcing what the group switches (e.g. "Preview form factor"). Segmented kind only: spaced peers are independent buttons with no group role.

props.name: block
props.description: Stretch the group to the container width, the segments sharing the space equally. An orthogonal layout modifier for the segmented and spaced kinds; split and stepper ignore it (their cells are fixed-width chrome) with a dev-only warning. A measure step (`sm`, `lg`, …) does the same up to that width of the scale.

platformNotes.web:
Segmented controls, split buttons, attached groups.

On the web the segmented control is the v4 hand-off's: the options sit in a rounded track on the raised fill, and the selected one rides a flat card thumb with a small shadow, the rest in the muted ink. It is 30, 36 or 44 px tall at the small, default and large sizes. The split button is the green call-to-action pill with its chevron half, and the stepper and the spaced peers are hairline pills the height of a Button beside them.

Pass `rounded` for a capsule segmented track with equal cells and one sliding selection thumb. The small capsule is 32 px tall, as in the docs appearance picker. Its spring transition follows Reduce Motion.

components.name: Card
components.description: A content surface, used three ways: a stat card (a single metric, a big number and a delta), a section card (a labeled surface with an optional eyebrow, header and footer), and the generic card that brings its own structure. It is the Canvas v4 panel: the card fill under a hairline at the card corner (16 px on the web, 12 natively), the small shadow at rest and the large one `raised`; `flat` drops the shadow and steps the fill up a surface, `sunken` drops the shadow and sinks the fill to the well beneath the page (`surface-sunken`, the hand-off's `--bg2` tiles, stages and panels set into a card) under the hairline, and `outlined` drops the shadow and keeps the card fill under the hairline (the hand-off's page cards; a platform whose card control draws an outline instead of a shadow draws both the same), and `heroShadow` is the medium shadow (the hand-off's `--sh-md`, its section hero's stage), between the resting card and the raised one. Precedence is `raised`, `flat`, `sunken`, `outlined`, `heroShadow`. On Android `sunken` is the Material 3 filled card: the well's fill with no outline. A pressable card lifts 2 px on hover and takes the raised shadow. `selected` draws the primary border with a ring of the accent's soft wash around it.

props.name: padded
props.description: Padding (orthogonal booleans). A card with raw children is padded by default, and the data-driven string path (no children) pads through its self-padding sections instead, so neither prop moves the surface inset there. `flush` strips the raw-children inset (edge-to-edge content, or composing the self-padding CardHeader/CardContent); `padded` is the explicit form of the padded-by-default.

platformNotes.web:
A content surface, used three ways: a stat card (a single metric, a big number and a delta), a section card (a labeled surface with an optional eyebrow, header and footer), and the generic card that brings its own structure. It is the Canvas v4 panel: the card fill under a hairline at the card corner (16 px on the web, 12 natively), the small shadow at rest and the large one `raised`; `flat` drops the shadow and steps the fill up a surface, `sunken` drops the shadow and sinks the fill to the well beneath the page (`surface-sunken`, the hand-off's `--bg2` tiles, stages and panels set into a card) under the hairline, and `outlined` drops the shadow and keeps the card fill under the hairline (the hand-off's page cards; a platform whose card control draws an outline instead of a shadow draws both the same), and `heroShadow` is the medium shadow (the hand-off's `--sh-md`, its section hero's stage), between the resting card and the raised one. Precedence is `raised`, `flat`, `sunken`, `outlined`, `heroShadow`.
On Android `sunken` is the Material 3 filled card: the well's fill with no outline.
A pressable card lifts 2 px on hover and takes the raised shadow. `selected` draws the primary border with a ring of the accent's soft wash around it.

Corners (pick one; the smaller step wins): the card corner by default, `smallCorners` for the tile corner (12), and the three steps the hand-off's component page frames with, `calloutCorners` (14: a note under a table, a compact link tile), `largeCorners` (18: a card framing a section of a page) and `stageCorners` (20: a staging frame, a figure and its legend), and the two its section pages frame with, `showcaseCorners` (20: a section page's showcase card) and `heroCorners` (24: the section hero's stage). The web skin draws each from its row; the native skins keep their own card corner on every step but the tile.

components.name: Carousel
components.description: A horizontally paged slide viewer: swipe (or use the prev/next arrows and the dot indicators) to move one slide at a time.

props.name: items
props.description: The slides, left to right.

props.name: index
props.description: Controlled current slide. Pair with `onIndexChange`. Omit for uncontrolled.

props.name: defaultIndex
props.description: Initial current slide for the uncontrolled case (read once; default 0).

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Called with the next current index whenever the slide changes.

props.name: loop
props.description: Wrap from the last slide to the first (and first to last) on arrow nav.

props.name: showArrows
props.description: Show the prev/next chevron buttons beside the slides. Default is platform-adaptive: on for web, off for iOS + Android (swipe idioms); pass `true` to opt in.

props.name: showDots
props.description: Show the centered dot indicators below the slides. Default is platform-adaptive: on for web + iOS (UIPageControl), off for Android M3.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

platformNotes.web:
A horizontally paged slide viewer: swipe (or use the prev/next arrows and the
dot indicators) to move one slide at a time.

Paging snaps to the viewport width, the current slide drives the dots, and the
arrows step the index (clamped, or wrapped when `loop`). Slides hold any
content; pass an `items` array of `{ key, content }`.

Each slide is itself the card: it paints the surface, rounds the corners and
clips its content to them. So pass the slide's content, not a Card. A plain
string renders in the slide's own type, inset from its edge; any other node
fills the slide inside its 1px edge, so a picture is masked to the slide's
shape. A
Card nested inside frames the slide
twice, and on Android the Material 3
item's 28dp corners cut the Card's own 12dp edge.

The prev and next arrows sit beside the slides, never over them, so nothing
near a slide's edge is hidden behind an arrow; the slides narrow by the two
arrow gutters instead.

Every slide is mounted from the first frame and stays mounted, so a slide's own
state (a field's text, a playing video) survives the carousel measuring its
viewport, on the first layout and whenever a hidden carousel is shown again.
Until it has measured, the current slide fills the viewport on its own. A
carousel does not window its slides, so a long gallery loads every slide's
content up front.

On web, Tab visits the carousel in the order it reads: the previous arrow, the
slide viewport, the next arrow, then the slide picker (an arrow disabled at the
end of a non-looping carousel is skipped). Tab reaches the viewport while its
slides overflow it, and the focused viewport draws the theme's focus ring around
the slide. Left and Right move between
slides, while Home and End reach the first and last. Controls inside a slide
keep their own keyboard behavior. The named slide-picker buttons report the
current slide and its position in the set; activating the current slide does
nothing.
Picker targets measure at least 24px on web, 44pt on iOS, and 48dp on
Android, independently of the small painted dots.

The active dot follows the committed slide (a dot press, the arrows, the
keyboard, a controlled `index`, a finished swipe) in both surface modes; the
strip is absent with one slide,
with `showDots={false}`, and by default on
Android.

components.name: Chart
components.description: A single- or multi-series bar chart: vertical columns (or horizontal rows) sized against the axis max, with per-category values and labels.

props.name: data
props.description: The bars to render, in order (single-series mode).

props.name: labels
props.description: Category labels along the x axis (grouped mode, with `series`).

props.name: series
props.description: Multiple series rendered as grouped columns per category, colored by the chart-1..8 tokens (or a series' own `success`/`destructive` tone).

props.name: stacked
props.description: Stack the grouped series within one column per category (composition) instead of clustering them side by side.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional heading shown above the plot.

props.name: max
props.description: Axis maximum. Defaults to the largest value in the data (the largest category TOTAL when `stacked`).

props.name: success
props.description: Tone (pick one; default is the primary fill). Single-series only.

props.name: destructive
props.description: Tone (pick one; default is the primary fill). Single-series only.

props.name: horizontal
props.description: Orientation (default is a vertical column chart). Single-series only.

props.name: compact
props.description: Density (default is the standard plot size).

props.name: plain
props.description: Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats).

props.name: hideLegend
props.description: Hide the series legend (grouped mode shows one by default).

props.name: selected
props.description: Press-to-inspect: the selected category index (controlled). Pass null for none. Vertical charts only.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: Press-to-inspect: the initially selected category (uncontrolled).

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fired when a press selects a category (or clears it with null).

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats the value axis, the inspected value and the accessible values (data formatting, not styling).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Tone
groups.note: Tone (pick one; default is the primary fill). Single-series only.

groups.title: Orientation
groups.note: Orientation (default is a vertical column chart). Single-series only.

groups.title: Density
groups.note: Density (default is the standard plot size).

props.description: Save the zero-based current question index; omit questionIndex for local navigation state.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable question forms while other application work is in progress.

props.name: pending
props.description: A reply is being prepared; no artificial message is added to the data.

props.name: pendingIcon
props.description: Application-supplied provider mark for a reply that has not started streaming.

props.name: terminal
props.description: Flat, compact monospace terminal transcript.

props.name: style
props.description: Parent composition only. Supply a bounded height, or a bounded flex parent.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Focus the message input on mount.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Receives the trimmed draft. The app owns clearing the draft and starting transport.

props.name: sendDisabled
props.description: Block only sending, keeping the draft, attachments, and message choices interactive.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Optional application input limit; enforced by the native text field.

props.name: onAttach
props.description: Show an attachment control; the app owns its file picker and upload service.

props.name: attaching
props.description: File selection or upload is in progress; prevents attaching or sending again.

props.name: footer
props.description: Anchored actions or help below the composer, outside the scrolling thread.

props.name: children
props.description: Untrusted Markdown source. HTML, URLs and images remain inert text.

props.name: compact
props.description: Denser document typography using Canvas's body reading scale.

props.name: terminal
props.description: Compact monospace transcript, with flat horizontally scrolling tables.

platformNotes.web:
A controlled assistant conversation with independently scrolling messages, clear author and provider identities, and an anchored multiline composer. The parent supplies the bounds; Chat fills the available height without choosing a fixed height of its own.

Messages remain application-owned `ChatMessageData`: keep each `id` stable while updating `content` during streaming. `pending` shows a three-dot thinking indicator until an explicitly `streaming` message arrives; pass `pendingIcon` to identify its provider. Streaming replies retain their own Responding indicator. Both animations stop when their state ends and stay still under Reduce Motion. `providerIcon` accepts an application-supplied provider logo beside the author; label the image or icon with the provider name for assistive technology. `provider` remains an optional supplementary text label such as the transport name. `error` adds a visible failure label; `notice` preserves delivery or fallback information. `footer` anchors connection, review, or other actions below the composer and outside the scrollport.

The conversation reads like a desktop assistant: one centered column at most 768 points wide, assistant replies as plain text across it, the person's own turns as a neutral bubble on the trailing side without an author line (an explicit `author` or provider still shows), and the composer as one raised, rounded box below with a round add button and a round send button.

Set `activity` on a message for work the assistant did rather than said, such as a command, a tool call or a process log. It shows as one muted line, its `author` then its `notice`, and expands to its markdown `content` when pressed.

Pass `actions` on any message for app-owned choices beneath its content: each has a stable `id`, a literal `label`, and optional `primary`. Chat, ChatThread, and ChatMessage call `onAction(messageId, actionId)` when chosen. Choices wrap at narrow widths and use each platform’s Button. `disabled`, `pending`, any streaming message in the thread, or an absent callback prevents activation. The app owns saving the choice, setting busy state while it is accepted, duplicate prevention, and removing resolved or historical actions. Actions do not send a composer draft or submit question answers.

Assistant content supports paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, fenced code, bold, emphasis, and inline code through React Native text. HTML, images, and links stay literal text and never load or execute remote content. `plain` renders all source punctuation literally; user messages are always plain text. This is a small safe markdown subset rather than a complete CommonMark renderer.

`ChatThread` follows new content while the reader is within 48 points of the bottom. Scrolling up to read older messages pauses following; returning to the bottom resumes it. Message updates, streaming text, question-height changes, and viewport resizing coalesce into a tail adjustment after layout settles. Scrolling is immediate and never animated, so it does not add motion when text streams or Reduce Motion is enabled. The overflowing thread is keyboard focusable with a visible focus frame. The native app or owning Dialog handles safe areas and keyboard avoidance.

`ChatComposer` keeps Enter available for newlines. Its explicit Send control receives the trimmed draft through `onSend`; empty, disabled, pending, or uploading sends are blocked. An attached file permits an empty text draft. `sendDisabled` blocks only Send while leaving drafts, attachment controls, and message choices interactive; use it when a saved choice must be made before another freeform message. Pending replies leave the draft editable. The app owns draft clearing, transport, cancellation, persistence, and retry behavior.

Pass `terminal` to Chat or its standalone pieces for a flat, left-aligned monospace transcript. Messages use `❯` for the user and `●` for the assistant beside their author, preserving provider text and current delivery state. No user bubble or conversation card is added. The bare composer places `❯` and its multiline editor between two full-width hairlines, with an explicit rectangular Send action. Hardware Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts a newline. IME composition and native soft-keyboard Enter retain their normal text-entry behavior. Sending returns focus to the editor; `autoFocus` optionally focuses it on mount. The app still owns clearing the draft, delivery, and preventing duplicate requests. Pending replies keep the draft editable and block sending.

`Markdown terminal` preserves the same safe document grammar with 13px monospace text, compact spacing, and semantic headings. Tables remain aligned table rows in a horizontal scrollport instead of becoming stacked cards. Fenced code and tabs remain literal whitespace. `Textarea terminal` supplies the prompt's bare monospace metrics and implies `embedded`; existing Textarea defaults remain unchanged.

Set `onAttach` to show the accessible paperclip action. The app owns file picking and uploading, passes composer `attachments`, and removes a staged file through `onRemoveAttachment(id)`. A `ChatAttachmentData` has an `id`, `name`, optional `uploading` or `error` flags, and optional `notice` text. Uploading and failed files block sending; remove a failed file or replace it after retrying. `attaching` also blocks attaching and sending while the app opens a picker or uploads. Saved message attachments use the same metadata; `onOpenAttachment(attachment)` on Chat, ChatThread, or ChatMessage delegates opening or downloading to the app. Canvas never requests, uploads, or opens file URLs itself.

An assistant message can include `questions`: each `ChatQuestionData` has a stable `id`, `title`, optional `multiple`, and `options` with an `id`, `label`, and optional `description`. Supply controlled `ChatQuestionAnswerData` entries in `questionAnswers` containing `questionId`, `optionId` for a single choice or `optionIds` for multiple choices, and optional `customText`. Set `multiple` on the question for checkboxes; a custom answer can be combined with regular choices. A single-choice question also offers Select multiple at the bottom-right of its action row: switching it on records `multiple: true` in its answer and uses `optionIds`, preserving the original question metadata. The switch retains existing selections and custom text. Switching it off returns to the first selected choice, or clears an empty draft. Every question offers Write my own answer under the reserved `__custom` option id, limited to 1000 characters.

The active form shows one question with a counter derived from the actual question count. Selecting an ordinary radio saves and advances before the last question. Custom text stays on the current question and uses Next; a blank custom answer cannot advance. Back is a neutral outline button that preserves saved selections and text. Revisited valid single choices offer Next. Checkboxes use Submit to advance; Submit appears only for multiple-choice questions and the last question. The last question always requires explicit Submit before the complete batch is sent, and every question must have a real answer. An incomplete earlier answer returns the reader to the first unresolved question instead of submitting. Submitted custom text is trimmed.

Chat, ChatThread, and ChatMessage expose `onQuestionAnswerChange(messageId, answers)`, `onQuestionIndexChange(messageId, index)`, and `onSubmitQuestionAnswers(messageId, answers)`. Record answer changes in message data and pass the zero-based `questionIndex` to control navigation, including saved continuation after reload. Omitting `questionIndex` uses local navigation state. The position is clamped to the actual list. The final callback receives fresh answers for the whole batch, including the current answer; set `questionsSubmitted` after accepting it. Repeated activations are guarded while navigation or submission settles. A busy state that ends without a saved receipt permits retry. The app owns persistence, transport, and duplicate prevention across requests.

Both answer callbacks and an enabled form are required for interaction. `disabled`, `pending`, and active streaming lock the current question. Use `questionsDisabled` for an inactive earlier batch: it shows every original question and option read-only, without navigation actions. `questionsSubmitted` shows saved answers with an Answers sent receipt. Multiple-choice receipts include every selected label and custom text; an answer-mode override is identified as Multiple answers selected by you. Question labels and descriptions remain literal text; RadioGroup supplies arrow navigation and accessible group names. The counter is announced as Question X of N in a polite live region; navigation moves focus there through the kit's shared browser and native accessibility focus mechanism.

The current question is framed by the existing compact, flat selected Card: a soft theme tint and primary border distinguish its counter, answers and actions from the surrounding conversation. Saved receipts and inactive question history remain unframed. The Card is visual only, so answer controls retain their own accessible roles and focus behavior.

`Markdown` reuses Chat's safe grammar and renderer for standalone documents. It preserves heading levels one through six, emphasis, inline and fenced code, quotes, ordered and unordered lists, nested indentation, static checked/unchecked task lists, horizontal rules, and pipe tables.
Tables use Canvas DataTable's container-responsive stacked layout on narrow surfaces, retaining every column on iOS too.
Checklists are read-only Canvas selection controls; reading a document never changes its source. HTML, links and image syntax remain inert text: no source is executed and no remote image is requested. `MarkdownProps` accepts the source as children, an optional accessibility label and test ID; `compact` uses dense document typography. The parent supplies width.

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: Multi-select option, single yes/no, grouped lists.

props.name: children
props.description: Label text (the option's title) shown beside the box.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional muted secondary line rendered under the label, for the common title-plus-description option (a notification setting, a consent row). Supplying it builds the stacked title/description layout inside the control, so the caller never hand-composes a Row + Column + two Typography nodes and the whole row stays tappable.

props.name: checked
props.description: Controlled checked state; omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Initial state for uncontrolled use (a bare <Checkbox /> is interactive).

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Mixed state: some-but-not-all selected. Shown as a dash, not a tick. Takes visual precedence over `checked`. Implies `selection`: a mixed state belongs to a list's select-all, and a switch has none.

props.name: selection
props.description: A checkbox that selects an item in a list or a bulk selection (a table's rows, a list in edit mode, a select-all), rather than one on/off setting. The web draws the checkbox, iOS the edit-mode selection circle, Android the Material 3 checkbox. Without it a Checkbox is one setting, which iOS and Android render as their switch (role `switch`), so a settings row reads the way each platform writes it.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fired with the next checked value when the row is pressed (both modes). Web keyboard activation supports Space on release and Enter.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Alias of onChange, for parity with RN's value-style callbacks.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name for a LABEL-LESS checkbox (one with no `children`, e.g. a row selector in a table). With a visible label the label itself is the name; without one this is what a screen reader announces.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the pressable row.

props.name: small
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the base box).

props.name: large
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the base box).

props.name: disabled
props.description: State.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the interactive checkbox row, including its label. Typed as a React Native View. On web, React Native Web exposes its DOM host; focus() and blur() move browser focus. Native host behavior depends on the platform and React Native version. Calling focus() does not activate the control or call accessibility focus APIs.

groups.title: Size
groups.note: Size (pick one; default is the base box).

platformNotes.web:
Multi-select option, single yes/no, grouped lists.

One job, a platform's own control: a Checkbox that is one setting (a yes/no, a consent, an opt-in)
renders the platform's switch on iOS and Android, where a single setting is a switch (Material 3 on phones included), and stays a checkbox on the web; its role follows what renders (`switch` there, `checkbox` here).
A Checkbox that selects items in a list, a table's rows or a "select all" parent takes `selection`:
the web keeps the checkbox, Android the Material 3 checkbox, and iOS draws the edit-mode selection circle.
`indeterminate` implies `selection`, since a mixed state belongs to a "select all" parent and a switch has none. In glass mode the box keeps its solid look on every platform: it is a small mark inside content, not a surface, so it draws with no pane and no rim, a checked box in its solid brand fill under its check and an empty box with its solid outline.

Pass `ref` to access the interactive checkbox row, including its label. Use `useRef<ComponentRef<typeof Checkbox>>(null)` from React, or `useRef<View>(null)` with React Native's `View` type. Object and callback refs are supported and detach on unmount. Calling `ref.current?.focus()` or `.blur()` delegates to the host without activating the control. Browser focus is supported; native focus depends on the platform and React Native version, and is separate from accessibility focus.

On the web, Space activates the focused control on key release, and Enter also activates it. Holding Space does not repeat the change. Moving focus away, disabling the control, or composing text cancels a pending Space press.

On the web, Space activates the focused control on key release, and Enter also activates it. Holding Space does not repeat the change. Moving focus away, disabling the control, or composing text cancels a pending Space press.
