components.name: Chip
components.description: An interactive pill for filter chips, tags, and selectable tokens. It carries an optional leading icon and a label, becomes tappable with `onPress`, and grows a trailing "×" remove button with `onRemove`.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen chip's value (CONTROLLED). Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial chosen value for uncontrolled use (a bare group selects on press).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fired with the newly chosen chip's value.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable every chip in the group.

props.name: option
props.description: Draw every chip as an `option` chip (Chip's compact settings pick), 4 px apart: the pick-one sets of a settings panel.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's name, rendered as a heading above the chips and announced as the radiogroup's accessible name. The group owns this label anatomy; never hand-compose a heading Text beside a bare group.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional muted supporting line rendered under the label.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: The group's accessible name when the page already shows its heading elsewhere (no visible label is rendered). `label` wins when both are passed.

props.name: children
props.description: The `<Chip value="…">` options that make up the set.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the group container.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only (flex within a parent), never a restyle hook.

props.name: children
props.description: The chip label.

props.name: count
props.description: A dimmed trailing count, set in the mono face.

props.name: start
props.description: Pin a chip within an app-owned host layout.

props.name: icon
props.description: A leading element (e.g. an `<Icon />` or a small `<Avatar />`). An `<Icon />` is auto-tinted to the chip's label color unless it sets its own color.

props.name: trailing
props.description: A trailing element (e.g. a chevron for a menu trigger). Rendered after the label.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Makes the whole chip tappable (e.g. toggling a filter). Called with the press event, which a ChipGroup option's Space key does not have, so an `href` chip that routes on the client calls `event?.preventDefault()` here.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the chip a LINK to this destination (a route or a URL): on the web react-native-web renders the chip as an `<a href>`, so middle-click, cmd-click and open-in-new-tab work and assistive tech hears a link; it takes the link chip's hover (the accent ink inside an accent edge) in place of the brightening. props.name: hrefAttrs
props.type: { target?: "_blank" | "_self"; rel?: string; download?: boolean | string; } | undefined
props.description: Anchor attributes forwarded with `href` on the web (react-native-web's `hrefAttrs`): `target`, `rel`, `download`. Ignored without `href`, and everywhere natively.

props.name: onRemove

props.name: selectable

platformNotes.web:
An interactive pill for filter chips, tags, and selectable tokens. It carries an
optional leading icon and a label, becomes tappable with `onPress`, and grows a
trailing "×" remove button with `onRemove`.

A Chip is a LOW-emphasis tag, not a call to action: the neutral chip is a 28 px
outlined pill (the raised neutral fill inside a hairline, its label at weight
500). A status chip is its soft pill (the status wash under the status ink, the
recipe Alert and the other toned surfaces share); a palette hue is that hue's
16% wash inside the same hue at 30%, under a deep ink in the hue that holds
4.5:1 on the wash. A selectable chip rests as the bare pill in the field border,
and once selected it is the accent's soft wash in the accent ink, inside an
accent edge and leading with a check.
On Android the chip is Material 3's: a 32dp outlined
container at the 8dp chip corner, its selected filter chip tonal with an 18dp
check and no outline.
The chip owns that whole look, so no call site
hand-composes a `borderRadius` + `backgroundColor` + padding Pressable.

Two orthogonal axes drive the look:

- **Color** (pick one; default the neutral tag). A semantic status (`success`,
  `warning`, `destructive`, `info`, `neutral`) or a free-form palette hue (`red`,
  `orange`, `amber`, `yellow`, `lime`, `green`, `emerald`, `teal`, `cyan`, `sky`,
  `blue`, `indigo`, `violet`, `fuchsia`, `purple`, `pink`, `rose`, `gray`). Status
  names read the theme's status colors (`statusColors`), so a success chip matches a
  success Badge and Alert; `info` is the primary color. Precedence when more than one
  is set: status names first, then hues in the order above.
- **Emphasis**. `outline` drops the fill for the field-border edge around the
  color's ink; `primary` is the solid accent;
`secondary` is the higher raised
  fill with no edge (on Android, the filled chip beside the bare outlined
  container that is its idle chip).
`neutral` is the muted tag with no edge;
  `gray` is the same muted fill and ink inside the chip's own edge. `outline` composes with any color,
  e.g. `<Chip blue outline>`. Precedence: a color wins over `primary`, and
  `outline` wins over `primary`'s fill.

`count` adds a dimmed trailing count in the mono face. A hovering pointer
brightens the chip on the web. `start` pins a chip when its host layout does not
publish a Canvas sizing context.

`steadyPress` retains the resting opacity during a press, while selection,
hover feedback and the native ripple keep working.

`href` makes the chip a link to a route or a URL: a real anchor on the web (so
middle-click and open-in-new-tab work and assistive tech hears a link), with
`hrefAttrs` forwarding `target`, `rel` and `download`. Native platforms have no
anchors, so pair `href` with an `onPress` that navigates through the app's router; it
receives the press event, so a web app routing on the client calls
`event?.preventDefault()` there. A hovering pointer turns a link chip's ink and edge to
the accent instead of brightening it. A link is not a toggle: `href` is ignored on a
selectable chip or a ChipGroup option.

`small` gives passive metadata tags a 24 px container and 11 px label where the skin supports it. Platform-native chips and the option, token and link looks keep their own dimensions.

components.name: CodeBlock
components.description: Syntax-highlighted code display with clipboard copy, horizontal scrolling, line emphasis, diff rendering, collapsible folding, and tabbed alternatives.

props.name: code
props.description: The code to render. Newlines are preserved (RN Text honors "\n").

props.name: filename
props.description: Optional filename label shown in a header bar above the surface. Honored by the plain and numbered variants (and the terminal chrome label); the inline pill has no header. When both are set, `filename` takes the header label and `language` renders as a trailing badge.

props.name: language
props.description: The snippet's language. Drives syntax highlighting (ts/tsx/js/jsx, json, bash/sh, css, html, python — anything else renders monochrome) and the header/terminal label when no `filename` is given.

props.name: transcript
props.description: Bare execution output: selectable, wrapped monochrome text with no card, header or expander. Takes precedence over terminal, numbered and inline; other display modifiers are ignored.

props.name: compact
props.description: Density (pick one; default is the comfortable ramp).

props.name: playground
props.description: The hand-off component page's JSX card (Component.dc.html lines 171 to 174, the playground's output): the block at the card corner, its header a 40 px bar on the card fill, 16 in and 8 out, with its Copy a 28 px hairline button, and the code 16 above and below, 18 in, at the default 13 / 1.7 ramp. `compact` wins when both are passed.

props.name: snippet
props.description: The hand-off component page's own snippet (Component.dc.html line 283, the Usage section's block under its paragraph): the code-card corner, with the code 16 above and below and 18 in at the default 13 / 1.7 ramp. `compact` and `playground` win over it.

props.name: guide
props.description: The hand-off component page's card snippet (Component.dc.html line 288, the block in a Usage guidance card): the card-snippet corner, with the code 12 above and below and 14 in at 12 / 1.65. Every other density wins over it.

props.name: copy
props.description: Show a copy affordance (header-hosted when a header/chrome exists, else pinned top-right). On the `inline` variant the whole pill becomes the copy button: a raised mono chip with a trailing copy glyph that turns to a check once copied (an import line a reader takes away).

props.name: wrap
props.description: Soft-wrap long lines instead of scrolling them horizontally. An overflowing unwrapped block is a keyboard tab stop; arrow keys use the platform's normal scrolling.

props.name: diff
props.description: Render the code as a unified diff: the first column of every line is the marker ("+" added, "-" removed, anything else context). Added/removed rows tint green/red, markers stay out of the selection, and the copy chip yields the post-change code (context + added lines, markers stripped).

props.name: attached
props.description: Square the top edge (no top radius/border) to sit flush under an adjoining bar.

props.name: headerless
props.description: Draw no header bar: `language` still drives the highlighting, but neither it nor a `filename` labels the block, and `copy` floats over the code's top-right corner. For a snippet whose context already names it (a docs page's usage block). Plain and numbered variants; a `tabs` strip still needs its header, and the terminal keeps its chrome.

props.name: unbadged
props.description: Keep the header bar but draw no trailing language badge beside the copy chip: `language` still drives the highlighting, for a header whose `filename` already names the language (the hand-off's playground bar, Component.dc.html lines 171 to 174, is "JSX · <Interface>" and a Copy button only). Nothing changes when there is no `filename`, since the language is then the header's label, not a badge.

props.name: highlightLines
props.description: Emphasize lines: entries are 1-based line numbers or "start-end" ranges (e.g. `[2, "5-7"]`). Numbers refer to the displayed numbering, so they respect `startLine`. Plain and numbered variants only.

props.name: startLine
props.description: First displayed line number for the numbered variant (default 1).

props.name: collapsible
props.description: Fold long blocks behind a "Show all" expander (plain + numbered variants).

props.name: collapsedLines
props.description: How many lines a collapsed block shows (default 8).

props.name: expanded
props.description: Controlled expanded state for `collapsible`.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.description: Uncontrolled initial expanded state (default false).

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Called when the expander toggles (fires in both modes).

props.name: tabs
props.description: Labeled code alternatives rendered as a tab strip in the header (or the terminal chrome) — the classic npm/yarn/bun switcher. Each tab supplies its own code and optional language/filename.

props.name: active
props.description: Controlled active tab index.

props.name: defaultActive
props.description: Uncontrolled initial tab index (default 0).

props.name: onTabChange
props.description: Called with the next tab index when a tab is selected (fires in both modes).

props.name: prompt
props.description: The terminal prompt marker (default "$"). Lines starting with it render as commands.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Called when the copy affordance is pressed, with the copied text. The chip also writes the clipboard itself (navigator.clipboard on web, the optional expo-clipboard peer on native), so this is for side effects, not plumbing.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Variant
groups.note: Variant (pick one; default is the plain block).

groups.title: Density
groups.note: Density (pick one; default is the comfortable ramp).

over the code's corner. Long lines scroll horizontally instead of truncating, and

hairline at a 14 px corner, a 36 px header of 12 px mono labels, 13 / 1.7 code, line

or jsx snippet takes the hand-off's component-page highlighter, which paints four
things and nothing else: a Capitalised tag name in the accent (the brackets and slash
neutral), an attribute name before its `=` in cyan, a string literal in mint and a
comment in the subtle ink; a bare boolean attribute, a keyword, a number and the
children text stay in the code ink, so `<Button>Save changes</Button>` reads as one

whose whole surface is one copy button, with a trailing copy glyph that turns to

verbatim, announces itself as "Copy" followed by the code, sets the code in one
ink (no syntax colours), and on the web its hairline turns to the accent under the

components.name: Collapsible
components.description: A single disclosure: one header (its `title`, or a custom `trigger`, plus a chevron that rotates when open) over one collapsible content panel.

props.name: title
props.description: The default trigger label text.

props.name: description
props.description: The muted secondary line under the title in the default trigger anatomy (ignored when a custom `trigger` is given, which owns its own anatomy).

props.name: trigger
props.description: A custom trigger node; if provided, it renders as the pressable's content instead of the `title` text (the chevron still renders alongside).

props.name: card
props.description: Card surface: wraps the disclosure in an outlined card container with inset header and content (web/Android). On iOS the default Collapsible already renders as the inset-grouped card, so `card` is a no-op there.

props.name: reference
props.description: The reference-sheet card (a component page's sub-component props): the card corner on a hairline over the card fill, a 46 px toggle with the title in 600 14 and the `description` inline after it in the mono meta ink, and the content flush to the card's edges, for a `reference attached` DataTable (web/Android). On iOS the default Collapsible already renders as the inset-grouped card, so `reference` changes nothing there.

props.name: children
props.description: The collapsible content. A string renders in the skin's content type; a ReactNode renders as-is.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`. Omit for uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next open state whenever the header toggles.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state for the uncontrolled case (read once, default false).

props.name: disabled
props.description: A disabled header does not toggle and reads dimmed.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

platformNotes.web:
A single disclosure: one header (its `title`, or a custom `trigger`, plus a chevron that rotates when open) over one collapsible content panel.

Closed by default; pass `defaultOpen` to start open. Open state is controlled (`open` + `onOpenChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultOpen`). A `description` adds a muted secondary line under the title;
`card` wraps the disclosure in an outlined card surface on web and Android (on iOS the default look already is the inset-grouped card, so `card` is a no-op there).
For a set of related, peer sections, reach for an Accordion (a group of these); Collapsible is the standalone primitive.

components.name: Command
components.description: Cmd+K search: navigation, actions, recent items.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Prompt shown in the empty search input.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible purpose for the search input and result list. Defaults to the search placeholder. Supply this when the placeholder does not explain the task.

props.name: query
props.description: The text typed into the search input (CONTROLLED). Filters the rows to the labels matching it (case-insensitive). Omit and use `defaultQuery` for uncontrolled use: a bare Command is searchable out of the box.

props.name: defaultQuery
props.description: Initial query for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.description: Fired with the new query on each keystroke (both modes).

props.name: groups
props.description: Grouped result rows.

props.name: filtered
props.description: Groups are already filtered and ranked by the owner; preserve their order and contents.

props.name: embedded
props.description: Fill the parent and inherit its surface, for composition inside a Dialog or Drawer. Ignored with trigger.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Focus the inline search field after mounting, allowing the containing overlay to capture its opener first.

props.name: onKeyPress
props.description: Input keyboard handler, called before built-in navigation. preventDefault cancels built-in handling.

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description: Content shown when there are no result rows, including an empty query.

props.name: active
props.description: Flat index of the highlighted row (CONTROLLED), counted across the visible (query-matching) rows. Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultActive
props.description: Initial highlighted row for uncontrolled use (hovering a row moves it, typing resets it to the first match).

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled (the search trigger toggles it).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Render the palette open initially for uncontrolled use (selecting a row closes it).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fired when the open state changes.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Render a collapsed full-width search trigger above the palette (a search glyph + "Search..." + a trailing kbd cap). The palette card still renders inline below the trigger (gated by `open`), mirroring how Dropdown shows its trigger plus the open menu in the docs.

props.name: footer
props.description: Append a footer hint bar below the list (↑ ↓ to navigate, ↵ to select, esc to close).

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the chosen item and its flat index (within the visible, query-matching rows) when a row is pressed.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element; the scrolling results list gets `${testID}-results`.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook.

platformNotes.web:
Cmd+K search: navigation, actions, recent items.

The search row is a real input: typing filters the grouped rows to the matching
labels, and a query that matches nothing shows a muted "No results" row.

On every platform the palette is the v4 card: 520 wide at an 18-pixel corner, a 48-pixel
search row with an `esc` cap over a hairline,
mono eyebrows over 38-pixel rows (44 on
iOS, 48 on Android) with quiet icons
and mono shortcuts, the accent's soft wash under the
active row, and an optional footer of mono hints.
Neither iOS nor Android ships a
command palette, so both take this look in their own face.

In glass mode the triggered palette is a functional-layer glass card under the
search bar, with its own search field; the search editor keeps focus while typing
filters the rows. Solid mode paints the skin's own palette.

The search placeholder names the input and its result list. Supply `accessibilityLabel` when a more specific purpose is needed. `defaultActive={-1}` starts without a highlighted result: Enter selects nothing until navigation or hovering chooses a row. Either arrow key starts at the first result from this state. Controlled indices above the visible result count clamp to the last match; negative, fractional and non-finite indices leave no active result.

Use `filtered` when a search service or index supplies ranked groups; Command keeps
those rows and their order instead of filtering their labels again. An item's
`description` supplies its secondary text. `emptyMessage` provides both the initial
prompt and the no-match message.

Use `embedded` inside a `Dialog` or `Drawer` to inherit its surface and fill its
bounds. It has no effect when `trigger` is set. Long results scroll within the
palette. `autoFocus` focuses the inline field after the containing overlay captures
its opener, so closing restores the original control. `onKeyPress` runs before
built-in navigation; call `preventDefault()` to handle an application shortcut.

components.name: Container
components.description: The bounds provider. A Canvas component never dictates its own width: `Container` conforms to its parent (full width, no cap) by default, and a named step of the shared width scale (`xxxs` 192 through `page` 1280) caps and centers it, so the reading measure of a form, an article, or a card stack is a step you can name instead of a width invented at the call site.

platformNotes.web:
The bounds provider. A Canvas component never dictates its own width:
`Container` conforms to its parent (full width, no cap) by default, and a named
step of the shared width scale (`xxxs` 192 through `page` 1280) caps and centers
it, so the reading measure of a form, an article, or a card stack is a step you
can name instead of a width invented at the call site.

A component fills the parent it is given (a field, a card, a table) or hugs its
content (a button, a badge), and the nearest layout container provides the
bounds. `Container` is the layout container whose job is a MEASURE, and by
default the parent is the conformance factor. A cap is fluid: inside anything
narrower than the step the container simply fills its parent, which is all a
phone screen is. `start` pins a capped box to the leading edge instead of
centering it, and `padTight` / `pad` / `padLoose` add horizontal gutters from
Row and Column's own padding scale.

components.name: DashboardGrid
components.description: A 12-column widget board for overview screens. Each widget declares a span in twelfths, and the grid measures its OWN width (never the window) to pick a tier: a wide container honors every span, a narrower one reflows widgets to their `narrowSpan`, and a phone-sized one stacks them full width.

props.name: items
props.description: The widgets to lay out, and the canonical collection prop. Their array order is the fallback order: any widget whose id is missing from the active order is appended, so adding one to a release never breaks a saved layout.

props.name: order
props.description: CONTROLLED widget order, as ids. The primary path: the consuming app owns the array and persists it through its own API, applying each `onOrderChange`. Ids the widget list does not hold are ignored, and widgets missing from it are appended, so a stored order survives a release that adds or drops a widget.

props.name: defaultOrder
props.description: Initial order for UNCONTROLLED use; the grid then applies each drop itself. Defaults to the `items` array order.

props.name: onOrderChange
props.description: Fired with the full, reconciled next order after every drop that changes it, in BOTH the controlled and the uncontrolled mode.

props.name: unlocked
props.description: Customize mode: cells gain the edit affordance and a drag grip, and the board becomes reorderable. The grid never flips this itself; the app owns the "Done" / "Customize" control. Locked (the default) the drag provider is not mounted at all.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: Web-only convenience for the UNCONTROLLED path: seed the initial order from browser storage under this key and write each drop back to it. Ignored when `order` is passed (the controlled order owns persistence). On native there is no storage, so the order is session-only there; `clearStoredDashboardOrder` forgets a saved layout. A server-rendered board renders `defaultOrder` first and adopts the saved layout in the commit right after hydration, so React always hydrates against the markup the server actually sent.

props.name: compact
props.description: Density axis (pass none for the default density).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook.

groups.title: Density axis
groups.note: Density axis (pass none for the default density).

platformNotes.web:

A widget's `title` is its accessible name rather than a header the grid paints: customize mode uses it to name the widget's drag grip and its drop zone.

components.name: DataTable
components.description: A data table rendered from column and row data, with sorting, row selection, pagination, and the loading and empty states built in.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns: a header label per column, or a `DataTableColumn` descriptor for per-column alignment (`numeric`/`centered`), a fixed `width`, and sorting (`sortable`, `sortValue`). Strings and descriptors mix freely. Treat the array and descriptors as immutable: replace both when a column changes.

props.name: rows
props.description: Row data: an array of rows, each an array of cells (one per column). A cell is a string (rendered in the default cell type) or any ReactNode for a custom cell, such as a link, a `Badge`, or a monospace name (rendered directly). Treat this data as immutable: replace the outer array and each changed row when data changes, so cached sorting and pagination update correctly.

props.name: groups
props.description: Group the rows under titled bands (the props table's "Intent", "Size" and "State" groups): each group draws a band spanning every column, its label, an optional adornment and an optional count on the sunken fill, then its own rows. Given `groups`, the table's rows are the groups' rows in order and `rows` is ignored; every row index a callback reports (`onRowPress`, `onRowEdit`, `rowKey` and the rest) counts through them in that order. Sorting reorders rows within their group and never moves a group; paging pages the rows, and each page draws the band of every group it shows. A group with no rows draws no band.

props.name: striped
props.description: Tint every other data row for easier horizontal scanning.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Draw the table's frame on the firmer field boundary rather than the hairline.

props.name: attached
props.description: The table sits flush inside a frame its parent draws (a `flush` Card, a bordered panel that clips to its corners), so it draws no frame of its own. Without it a standalone table frames itself (on the web and Android, a hairline at the table corner over the card fill), which is the standalone look.

props.name: stacks
props.description: Responsive: when the table's own CONTAINER is at or below `stackBreakpoint` (default `sm` = 640), each row lays its cells out top to bottom at the full width instead of side by side, so long text reads at the width of the table rather than a column's share of it. The first cell leads the row as its title; every later cell carries its column label above its value. The header row is drawn only while it holds a control (a sortable column, or the box that selects every row), as a band of its labels that wraps; the selection box and the row actions stay at the row's leading and trailing edges. A stacked table never pans, and on iOS it stacks instead of collapsing to its first column. Container-measured with a viewport seed for the first frame, like Row `stacks`; crossing the breakpoint changes the layout only.

props.name: stackBreakpoint
props.description: The breakpoint at and below which `stacks` stacks the rows (default `"sm"`). Only meaningful with `stacks` (DEV warns without it).

props.name: compact
props.description: Tighter vertical padding on header and data cells.

props.name: comfortable
props.description: Looser vertical padding on header and data cells.

props.name: reference
props.description: The reference sheet (a component page's props table): the column headings as the page's small uppercase mono label on a header row with no fill of its own, 12 px above and below whatever the density; rows 10 px above and below with a rule above each; the columns 16 px apart and 16 px in from the frame's sides; and the frame at the panel corner on the `border` hairline over the card fill, so `bordered` only firms the hairline and `attached` still drops the frame. On iOS the table keeps its own look and this changes nothing.

props.name: bare
props.description: The bare hairline table: no frame and no fill, a `field-border` rule under the headings (the reference sheet's mono uppercase label) and a `border` rule under every row, the first column flush with the table's start, each cell keeping 12 px clear at its end inside its column's width, and 12 px above and below whatever the density. `reference` wins over it. On iOS the table keeps its own look and this changes nothing.

props.name: matrix
props.description: The specimen matrix (a section page's states grid): no frame, no fill and no rules, the headings as the page's small uppercase mono label in the third ink, the cells unpadded, the rows 12 px apart and the columns 20 px apart. Pair it with `fit` columns for the hand-off's content-sized tracks. `reference` and `bare` win over it. On iOS the table keeps its own look and this changes nothing.

props.name: alignTop
props.description: Align every cell to the top of its row rather than its middle, so a row whose description wraps keeps its name, type and default beside the description's first line. The selection box and the row actions center on that first line, as they do in a stacked row.

props.name: footer
props.description: A row drawn inside the table's frame under the last row (and under the pagination bar when `paginated`): 44 px tall with its content centered, for a "Show all" control or a note. A hairline separates it from what sits above it: the one the last row draws already, or its own where nothing above it draws one.

props.name: sortable
props.description: Make every column sortable: pressing a header cycles ascending, descending, off. A column descriptor opts back out with `sortable: false`. Sorting is self-managed out of the box; control it via `sort`/`onSortChange`.

props.name: sort
props.description: Controlled sort state (`null` = unsorted). Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultSort
props.description: Initial sort for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: Fired with the next sort (or `null` when cleared) on header press.

props.name: selectable
props.description: Row selection: a leading checkbox column with a select-all header checkbox (indeterminate on a partial selection). Selection is keyed by `rowKey` (the row's original index when omitted) and self-managed out of the box; control it via `selectedKeys`/`onSelectionChange`. When no `onRowPress` is set, pressing anywhere on a row toggles it.

props.name: selectedKeys
props.description: Controlled selected row keys. Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultSelectedKeys
props.description: Initial selected row keys for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onSelectionChange
props.description: Fired with the next selected keys when a row or the select-all is toggled.

props.name: paginated
props.description: Page the rows through a built-in footer (the kit Pagination): a "Showing X-Y of N" range with Prev/Next, plus the selection count when `selectable`. Sorting applies before paging. Self-managed out of the box; control the page via `page`/`onPageChange`.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Rows per page (CONTROLLED; default 10, or the first of `pageSizes`).

props.name: defaultPageSize
props.description: Initial rows per page for uncontrolled use.

props.name: pageSizes
props.description: Selectable rows-per-page values. Supplying them upgrades the footer to the Pagination `withSize` variant (a "Rows per page" selector).

props.name: onPageSizeChange
props.description: Fired with the next rows-per-page value when the footer selector changes it.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page, 1-based (CONTROLLED). Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultPage
props.description: Initial page for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Fired with the next 1-based page when the footer pagination navigates.

props.name: loading
props.description: Loading state: the body renders pulsing skeleton placeholder rows (one per would-be row on the page) instead of data.

props.name: emptyMessage
props.description: What to render, centered under the header, when `rows` is empty (and not `loading`). A string gets the muted caption type; any ReactNode renders as given (an `EmptyState`, a retry Button). Omitted = just the header row, as before.

props.name: onRowPress
props.description: When set, each data row is pressable, reporting the row data and its index in `rows`. A press anywhere on the row acts; the keyboard and screen-reader path is a button inside the row's FIRST column, named from the row's plain text cells (or, when it has none, by that cell's own content). The row itself stays a `row`, so keep your own controls out of the first column here: a control there would nest inside the activator.

props.name: onRowEdit
props.description: Row editing: passing this adds a trailing actions column with a pencil button per row. Pressing the pencil opens the row's edit mode (its string cells become fields with a trailing Save/Cancel pair) and fires this with the row's original index in `rows`. Save reports the edited cells through `onRowCommit`; Cancel (or Escape in a field) closes without committing.

props.name: onRowDelete
props.description: Row deletion: passing this adds a delete (bin) button to the trailing actions column. Delete is second-press confirm: the first press ARMS it (the bin turns destructive and its accessible name says confirm), a second press within the confirm window fires this with the row's original index, and pressing anywhere else in the table (or the window lapsing) disarms.

props.name: inlineEdit
props.description: Let string cells be edited in place: pressing one swaps it to a field. Enter or blur commits through `onCellCommit`; Escape restores the cell. Custom ReactNode cells (badges, links) are not editable.

props.name: onCellCommit
props.type: ((rowIndex: number, colIndex: number, next: string) => void) | undefined
props.description: Fired when an `inlineEdit` cell commits (Enter or blur) with a changed value: the row's original index in `rows`, the column index, and the next text. Data stays yours: re-render with updated `rows` to keep the edit.

props.name: onRowCommit
props.description: Fired when a pencil-opened row edit is saved: the row's original index in `rows` and the full cells array with the edited strings in place (custom ReactNode cells pass through unchanged).

props.name: virtualized
props.description: Render the data rows through a windowed `FlatList` instead of mounting every row up front, for large tables. The header row stays fixed above it. Give the table a bounded height (via `style`, e.g. `{ maxHeight: 400 }`) so the body can scroll; without one it warns and renders eagerly. Default mounts all rows.

props.name: rowKey
props.type: ((row: ReactNode[], index: number) => string | number) | undefined
props.description: Stable key for a row, derived from the row data and its index in `rows`. Selection is keyed by it, and it keeps React row identity stable when rows reorder (sorting, live data) and a cell is a stateful custom ReactNode. When omitted, rows key off their original array index (safe for string/number cells and stateless custom cells; selection then tracks row POSITIONS, so supply a real key when the data itself can be reordered, inserted, or deleted). Keep this function pure; replace its identity when external data changes how keys are derived, so the cached selection summary updates.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Density
groups.note: Density (pick one; default is the regular row height).

platformNotes.web:
A data table rendered from column and row data, with sorting, row selection,
pagination, and the loading and empty states built in.

Columns are plain header labels or descriptors (`{ label, numeric, width,
sortable, ... }`) for per-column alignment, fixed widths, and sorting; compose a
toolbar above when the screen needs one. Density tweaks affect padding live.
Pass `onRowEdit` / `onRowDelete` for a trailing actions column: the pencil opens
the row's string cells as fields with Save/Cancel (committing via
`onRowCommit`), and Delete asks for a confirming second press before it fires.
`inlineEdit` skips the pencil and lets a string cell be pressed straight into a
field, committing via `onCellCommit`. `onRowPress` makes the whole row act on
press and puts the keyboard and screen-reader path on a button in the row's
first column, so keep your own controls out of that column when you use it. Data
stays yours either way: the table reports intent and re-renders whatever rows it
is handed back.

Treat `rows` and `columns` as immutable inputs. When editing data, replace the outer `rows` array and each changed row, as the examples below do. When changing a column, replace its descriptor and the `columns` array. Keep unchanged arrays and callbacks stable for large tables: Canvas caches sorting, paging, and selection summaries so typing a draft or opening a row action does not process the whole data set again. `sortValue` and `rowKey` must be pure functions of their inputs. If either closes over changing external data, supply a new callback identity; for `sortValue`, also replace its column descriptor and the `columns` array. A saved edit appears in sorted order when the updated `rows` arrive.

On narrow web and Android layouts, the columns still share the table width and
wrap their text, each keeping a 110 px minimum (a column with a fixed `width`
keeps that width), and they pan horizontally only when those minimums exceed
the table width. A long cell wraps inside its column rather than widening the
table. The overflowing scrollport is a keyboard tab stop, so the
platform's arrow keys can reveal the remaining columns, and while it has keyboard
focus the table's surface draws the theme's focus ring. A table that fits adds
no scrolling tab stop, and on Android it takes no sideways drag either, so a tap
that drifts sideways still presses its row and a swipe that starts across it
scrolls the page (while TalkBack explores by touch the scroller stays enabled, so
the exploring finger reaches every cell). On an iPhone-width table iOS shows only
the first column instead, as SwiftUI Table does. A table that passes `stacks`
does neither: at that width each row stacks its cells (see Stacked below).
On the web and Android, and for a table that stacks on any platform, crossing
that width changes the layout only: rows, custom cells, an open editor with its
text and focus, and a windowed body's scroll position stay as they are when a
window is resized across it or a phone measures the table on its first frame.
The iOS first-column layout is the exception: below that width the columns
after the first leave the table, with any editor or custom cell in them, and
mount again when it widens.

A `virtualized` table's body scrolls its rows under the fixed header. On the
web, while those rows overflow, the body is a keyboard tab stop of its own
(after the column scroller when a narrow table pans, and before the rows'
controls when they have any), the keyboard can scroll it, and while it has
keyboard focus the table's surface draws the same focus ring. The body is the
table's row group, so the rows it renders stay inside the table for a screen
reader rather than behind an unnamed focusable node.

components.name: DepthChart
components.description: The order-book view: cumulative bid and ask step areas mirrored around the spread, bids in the success tone and asks in destructive, on a numeric price axis.

props.name: bids
props.description: Bid levels (any order; sorted internally).

props.name: asks
props.description: Ask levels (any order; sorted internally).

props.name: title
props.description: Optional heading shown above the plot.

props.name: compact
props.description: Density (omit for the default plot size).

props.name: plain
props.description: Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats).

props.name: hideLegend
props.description: Furniture visibility.

props.name: hideGrid
props.description: Furniture visibility.

props.name: hideAxes
props.description: Furniture visibility.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats tick labels and accessible values (data formatting, not styling).

props.name: spread
props.description: The spread's label ("spread 0.12%"): drawn as a dashed guide midway between the best bid and the best ask, with this label in a pill at its top. Omit for no guide.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

props.name: overlay
props.description: Presents the dialog OVER the page instead of inline where it is mounted. The default is a contained overlay: a scrim with its own height, sitting in normal flow, which is what the docs catalogue needs to show a dialog inside an example stage. An application confirming a destructive action needs the opposite, and the inline form is actively wrong there: it appends a scrim wherever the component happens to sit, leaves the page behind scrollable and clickable, and still claims `aria-modal`. With `overlay`, the dialog teleports into the nearest `OverlayProvider` and fills it, so `aria-modal` becomes true rather than aspirational. Mount an `OverlayProvider` at the app root for this to cover the screen.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Cancel when the backdrop is pressed. Off by default, including destructive dialogs.

props.name: embedded
props.description: Show the open dialog as a non-modal specimen in the page, for a catalogue or a showcase: it keeps its look, its dialog role and its labelling, but does not take focus when it opens, trap Tab, return focus, claim `aria-modal`, or cancel on Escape, native back or a backdrop press. Ignored with `trigger`, which always opens a live modal.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: The dialog's accessible name, for the case where `children` supply the panel body. Children REPLACE the built-in title/description, so there is no element left for `aria-labelledby` to point at, and the dialog would otherwise be announced with no name at all. That is merely poor for a `dialog` and invalid for the `alertdialog` a destructive confirm renders.

platformNotes.web:
A modal dialog: a centered panel over a dimmed backdrop, which glass on the web also blurs, with a title, an optional description, a body for real content like a form, and right-aligned actions. Use it for a focused task that warrants interrupting the page; reach for the Alert Dialog for a terse yes/no confirmation.

On light glass, the description and currency prefix use the stronger foreground color. For custom body content, use the default `Typography` foreground for message copy over the dimmed background.

Browser Escape and iOS accessibility escape cancel the foremost open child
overlay before the dialog.
Cancelling the dialog calls `onCancel` and requests
`open=false`, including destructive dialogs and dialogs with custom children.
A controlled owner may keep it open; that request never confirms an action.

Pass `dismissible` to let a backdrop press follow the same cancel policy. It is
off by default, so existing dialogs and destructive confirmations keep their
current outside-press behavior. The scrim is excluded from keyboard navigation.

Use `form overlay dismissible` for the original Argus application dialog: a
persistent title and optional `description`, a close action, and scrolling body
and `footer` content. `panelWidth` bounds the form (560 pixels by default), and
the viewport keeps a twenty-pixel safe-area inset. The web treatment preserves
Argus’s 28-pixel content inset, 17-pixel title, rounded card, shadow, and lightly
frosted dim. A form with no trigger contributes no layout wrapper to its caller.
Nested menus receive Escape before the dialog; focus stays in the open modal.

For a conversation or other workspace with its own scroll region, use
`form workspace overlay`. The dialog measures a safe-area-bounded viewport
height; its header and optional `footer` stay fixed while `children` fill the
remaining space. Put the workspace's scrollable content inside `children` and
keep its composer or other controls as siblings of that scroll region. The
workspace body does not add an outer scrollport. `workspaceHeader` adds content
below the title and description in the fixed header, such as a step indicator.
This mode is intended for an overlay form; ordinary forms keep their existing
scrolling body.

Add `compact` to a workspace when short content should determine the panel's
height: `form workspace compact overlay`. The panel hugs the conversation and
composer, then grows up to the same safe-area-bounded viewport maximum. A long
conversation scrolls inside its own thread while the header, composer, and dialog
footer remain visible. The default workspace still fills its available height;
`compact` has no effect without `form workspace`.

Add `embedded` to show an open dialog in a page as a specimen, the way a catalogue
or a showcase does: it keeps its look, its dialog role and its labelling, but it is
not modal. It does not take focus when it opens, trap Tab, return focus, set
`aria-modal`, or cancel on Escape, native back or a backdrop press, so the page
around it keeps its scroll position and its keyboard order. `embedded` is ignored
with `trigger`, which always opens a live modal.

platformNotes.web:
A reusable drag-and-drop context: wrap a surface in a `DragDropProvider`, mark droppable regions with `DropZone`, and make items draggable with `Draggable` plus a `DragHandle` grip.

Items lift into a floating ghost and reorder within or across zones, position-aware.
It runs on iOS, Android, and the web from one PanResponder + Animated code path,
and the grip is keyboard- and screen-reader-operable: press Space to grab, the arrow keys to move, Space to drop, Escape to cancel.

The reading direction is respected throughout. In a right-to-left locale a `horizontal` zone lays its items out right to left, so the first position is the rightmost one, the drop indicator meets the row's right edge, and the two horizontal arrows swap roles (Left Arrow moves forward, Right Arrow back, per the WAI-ARIA practices). Vertical lists and the up/down arrows read the same way in both directions.

components.name: Drawer
components.description: A full-screen panel that slides in from an edge: a navigation drawer, a mobile menu, or a bottom action sheet. Built on React Native's Modal, so it floats over the whole app on iOS, Android, and the web, over a dimmed scrim that glass on the web also blurs. For a small contextual menu, reach for Dropdown or RowMenu instead.

props.name: footer
props.description: Pinned actions below the independently scrolling body.

props.name: navigation
props.description: Navigation body: no content inset or inter-item gap; fills the available height.

props.description: Solid, rounded execution sidebar inset from the viewport. Overrides edge and plain; width remains configurable.

props.name: plain
props.description: Square web side panel and the original lightly frosted application dim.

props.name: instant

props.name: embedded
props.description: Show the open drawer as a non-modal specimen inside its parent, for a catalogue or a showcase: the panel docks against its edge of the parent (which gives it its height) over the dim, with no Modal, no slide, no focus trap, and no close on Escape, native back or a tap on the dim. It keeps its labelling as a named region. Ignored with `trigger`, which always opens a live drawer.

props.name: open

props.name: onOpenChange

props.name: right

props.name: bottom
props.description: A sheet spanning the width, rising from the bottom.

props.name: top

props.name: width
props.description: Width of a side drawer in px (default 300). Ignored for the bottom/top sheet.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the modal surface. Required when the drawer has no trigger whose label can name it.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style

platformNotes.web:
A full-screen panel that slides in from an edge: a navigation drawer, a mobile menu, or a bottom action sheet. Built on React Native's Modal,
so it floats over the whole app on iOS, Android, and the web,
over a dimmed scrim that glass on the web also blurs. For a small contextual menu, reach for Dropdown or RowMenu instead.

Drawer provides an overlay host inside its own window. Dropdown, Select, and other anchored children render above the panel without being clipped by its corners; no additional OverlayProvider is needed inside the drawer. A tap outside an open child menu dismisses that menu, and Escape dismisses the child before the drawer. Nested drawers each keep their overlays in their own window.

On iOS, VoiceOver's accessibility escape gesture requests dismissal of the
foremost open child before the drawer.
Android system back uses the same child
ownership.
A controlled child that stays open continues to own later requests;
one request never falls through to its parent. The scrim remains a pointer
target, and the built-in trigger opens the drawer. Sidebar drill-down navigation
has its own back behavior; accessibility escape dismisses the overlay rather
than navigating a sidebar level. Focus restoration remains platform-dependent.

Give a controlled drawer an `accessibilityLabel` when it has no built-in
`trigger`. A drawer with a trigger uses the trigger label as its modal name.

`header` and `footer` pin content around an independently scrolling body. Its
application inset is 20 pixels vertically and 24 horizontally, with 22 between
children. `navigation` gives that body no inset or gap and fills its height.
`plain` preserves the original square Argus side panel and lightly frosted dim on
web; native skins retain their platform panel. `instant` presents and dismisses
without a slide or fade. Existing drawers retain their animated default.

components.name: Dropdown
components.description: Floating menus triggered by a button: actions, options, navigation.

props.name: anchorRef
props.description: Use an existing trigger without adding a trigger or layout wrapper.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Explicit accessible name for the menu.

props.name: compact
props.description: Exact compact web application menu frame and row metrics.

props.name: steadyPress
props.description: Preserve resting row fill and opacity during a press.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Width of the floating menu, clamped inside the overlay outlet.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Height cap for the compact menu's scrolling contents.

props.name: note
props.description: Muted footnote separated from menu commands by a hairline.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Label for the default outline trigger button. Omit when supplying a custom trigger via `children`.

props.name: children
props.description: A custom trigger rendered in place of the default outline button, e.g. an avatar account chip. It is wrapped in a Pressable that toggles the menu; the menu itself still comes from `items`.

props.name: triggerLabel
props.description: The accessible name for a CUSTOM trigger (`children`). Without it the button is named from its own contents, which runs the trigger's text together into one unpunctuated string ("Rachel Chenrachel@example.com") and repeats any label a nested control already carries. Ignored by the default `trigger` button, which is named by its own text.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional muted section heading rendered above the rows (e.g. "Actions").

props.name: title
props.description: Identity header title, rendered in the popover foreground ABOVE everything else in the menu (an account name over its email, say). Pair it with `description`; passing neither omits the header block entirely.

props.name: description
props.description: Identity header second line, muted, under `title`.

props.name: items
props.description: The menu rows, top to bottom.

props.name: alignEnd
props.description: Align the menu's TRAILING edge with the trigger's trailing edge instead of the leading edge (the default). For a trigger parked at the end of a bar, where a leading-aligned menu would run off the surface. Logical, so a right-to-left locale mirrors it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dimmed, inert trigger: the menu never opens and the press is a no-op.

props.name: inline
props.description: Draw the menu open and in flow under the trigger instead of floating it over the page: a specimen of the menu for a docs page or an empty state. The trigger reads as expanded and the press is inert, a row still fires `onSelect`, and nothing dismisses the card, so `open` and `onOpenChange` have no effect. `alignEnd` lines the card up with the trigger's trailing edge, as it does for the floating card.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled (the trigger opens/closes it).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fired when the open state changes (trigger press, select, etc.).

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fired with the selected item and its index when a row is pressed.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook.

platformNotes.web:
Floating menus triggered by a button: actions, options, navigation.

On the web the menu is the v4 panel: a card with a hairline and a soft shadow, 36-pixel
rows with quiet icons that take a raised wash under the pointer at once, a mono uppercase
eyebrow over a section, mono shortcuts in their own column, destructive rows in the
destructive ink, and a disabled row in the muted ink rather than faded.
iOS and Android keep their platform
menus (the iOS pull-down menu, the Material 3 menu) in the theme's colours.

In glass mode the menu is a dense-layer glass card under its trigger (or above it
when it fits there); the trigger keeps its place, its press and its accessible
name and state, and a selection commits and closes the menu the moment a row is
pressed. AvatarMenu and the collapsed Navbar menu are built on Dropdown. Solid
mode paints the skin's own menu.

`compact` tightens the web rows to 30 pixels and lets the menu scroll inside
`maxHeight`; with `steadyPress` a press does not tint the row. Selected rows take the
action ink.
Items can carry a stored `value`, `detail`, `description`, `selected` state, and a
`sectionBefore` heading. `keepOpen` leaves refresh-style commands open. A `note`
adds a muted footer. `menuWidth` and `maxHeight` bound the scrolling menu.
Pass `anchorRef` to use an existing trigger without adding another control or
layout wrapper; `accessibilityLabel` names the menu independently of its heading.
Checked choices use browser menu-radio semantics and the native radio trait.

components.name: Emblem
components.description: A tinted rounded square (or circle) that holds a single `Icon` or a short monogram, the recurring "icon on a soft background" used in cards, media objects, empty states, and feeds. Emblem owns the surface and the icon color: pick a tone and it tints the square and paints the glyph to match, so a call site never hand-composes `borderRadius` + `backgroundColor` to build an icon background.

props.name: children
props.description: A single `<Icon />` element; Emblem tints it to match the tone.

props.name: label
props.description: A monogram letter (or two) instead of an icon, painted in the tone color.

props.name: primary
props.description: Tone (pick one; default `muted`). Sets the tinted surface and the icon color. Precedence: primary > destructive > success > warning > cyan > secondary > muted.

props.name: destructive
props.description: Tone (pick one; default `muted`). Sets the tinted surface and the icon color. Precedence: primary > destructive > success > warning > cyan > secondary > muted.

props.name: success
props.description: Tone (pick one; default `muted`). Sets the tinted surface and the icon color. Precedence: primary > destructive > success > warning > cyan > secondary > muted.

props.name: warning
props.description: Tone (pick one; default `muted`). Sets the tinted surface and the icon color. Precedence: primary > destructive > success > warning > cyan > secondary > muted.

props.name: cyan
props.description: The fixed cyan hue (the hand-off's `--cyan`, the `chart-2` series): its wash and ring mixed from it, the glyph in the hue's ink, solved to 4.5:1 per scheme (Typography's `cyan`).

props.name: secondary
props.description: The solid neutral tile: the `secondary` fill inside the `border` hairline, the glyph in the second ink (`muted-foreground`), with no lit top edge (the hand-off's neutral tile).

props.name: small
props.description: Size (pick one; default medium).

props.name: large
props.description: Size (pick one; default medium).

props.name: circle
props.description: Circle instead of the default rounded square.

props.name: soft
props.description: The plain soft tile: the tone's own soft wash (`primary-soft`, `destructive-soft`, ...) with no ring and no lit top edge, at the soft tile's own corner. The tone tile a dialog draws over its title (the v4 hand-off's AlertDialog renderer, `--ion-soft` / `--bad-soft`). Composes with the tone and size axes.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: For layout composition only (not styling): the tint, radius, and size come from props.

groups.title: Tone
groups.note: Tone (pick one; default `muted`). Sets the tinted surface and the icon color. Precedence: primary > destructive > success > warning > cyan > secondary > muted.

groups.title: Size
groups.note: Size (pick one; default medium).

components.name: EmptyState
components.description: Centered, calm, never blame the user. Always tell them what could be here, and ideally how to get there.

props.name: icon
props.description: The glyph shown in the disc: a monochrome `<Icon />` element (cloned with the tone's tint and the disc's glyph size, so it follows `success`/default like the disc wash does; a semantic color boolean on the element still wins) or an emoji/character string.

props.name: title
props.description: Short, neutral headline naming the empty result.

props.name: description
props.description: One reassuring line, ideally pointing at the next step.

props.name: actionLabel
props.description: When set, renders a secondary action button below the description (small when `compact`).

props.name: onAction
props.description: Called when the action button is pressed.

props.name: success
props.description: Tone axis (pick one; default keeps the disc muted).

props.name: bordered
props.description: Container axis: wrap the column in a bordered card.

props.name: elevated
props.description: A shaded card: the `card` fill under the medium shade.

props.name: compact
props.description: Density axis: tightens the padding, rhythm, tile and title.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Tone axis
groups.note: Tone axis (pick one; default keeps the disc muted).

groups.title: Container axis
groups.note: Container axis: wrap the column in a bordered card.

groups.title: Density axis
groups.note: Density axis: tightens the padding, rhythm, tile and title.

platformNotes.web:
Centered, calm, never blame the user. Always tell them what could be here, and ideally how to get there.

The column is padded 40 by 24 at an 18px corner with a 12px rhythm: a 52px glyph tile in
the accent's soft wash, a 19px display-face title, a muted 14px description capped at
320px, and a secondary action. `bordered` draws a dashed edge, `elevated` lifts it onto a
shaded card, and `compact` tightens the padding, rhythm, tile and title for a table cell.

components.name: Feed
components.description: Vertical activity streams with icons and timestamps. Used for audit logs, change history, and notification lists.

props.name: items
props.description: Events to render, top to bottom.

props.name: activity
props.description: Lead axis (pick one; default is the connector node + vertical line).

props.name: trace
props.description: Lead axis (pick one; default is the connector node + vertical line).

props.name: connector
props.description: Lead axis (pick one; default is the connector node + vertical line).

props.name: avatar
props.description: Lead axis (pick one; default is the connector node + vertical line).

props.name: compact
props.description: Density modifier: tightens the row padding and connector spacing.

props.name: onItemPress
props.description: When set, each event row is pressable, reporting the row index.

props.name: label
props.description: The feed's accessible name (e.g. "Recent activity"): a screen reader announces it with the list of events. A `virtualized` feed needs one: on the web its scroller is a keyboard stop while the events overflow, and Chromium names an unnamed stop from the text of every event it has rendered.

props.name: virtualized
props.description: Render the rows through a windowed `FlatList` instead of mounting every row up front, for large lists. Give the list a bounded height (via `style`, e.g. `{ maxHeight: 400 }`) so it can scroll; without one it warns and renders eagerly anyway. Default (omitted) mounts all rows, unchanged. On the web, while the rows overflow, the windowed list is a keyboard tab stop the keyboard can scroll, and the feed's card draws the focus ring while it has keyboard focus.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Lead axis
groups.note: Lead axis (pick one; default is the connector node + vertical line).

groups.title: Density modifier
groups.note: Density modifier: tightens the row padding and connector spacing.

platformNotes.web:
Vertical activity streams with icons and timestamps. Used for audit logs, change history, and notification lists.

The events are a list, as in Tailwind UI, and each event is one of its items: a
screen reader announces the list with its number of events and moves through it
event by event. A pressable event is a button inside its item. The `label` prop
names the list (for example "Recent activity").

A `virtualized` feed with a bounded height scrolls its events in a list of its
own. On the web, while those events overflow, that list is a keyboard tab stop
(before the rows themselves when `onItemPress` makes them buttons), the
keyboard can scroll it, and while it has keyboard focus the feed's card draws
the theme's focus ring. Only the events near its viewport are mounted, and each
says where it sits in the whole feed, so a screen reader still counts every
event. Give a windowed feed a `label`: focused, a list with no name is named in
Chromium from the text of every event it has rendered, so the kit warns in
development when it has none.

`activity` provides the original Argus time gutter, sentence, and dividing rule.
`trace` provides a colored marker, optional halo, optional numeric time gutter,
and inline category label. These unframed rows inherit their owning panel. Pass
rich `content`, marker `color` and `halo`, and optional `kind` on each item.

components.name: Field
components.description: A form row: a label, the control, and one message line under it. Field exists for the part no control owns on its own: every field family already owns its label, but nothing else in the kit renders helper or error text, so that message is what Field adds.

props.name: label
props.description: Row label. When the lone child is a field-family control (Input, Textarea, Select, Autocomplete) that carries no `label` of its own, the label and `required` are DELEGATED into that control so each platform places them per its own contract. Any other control keeps the static label above.

props.name: helper
props.description: Muted hint under the control. Replaced by `error` when that is set.

props.name: error
props.description: Error text. Setting it puts the row in the error state: the message turns destructive and replaces `helper` in place, so the row never changes height and nothing below it jumps.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the label with a destructive asterisk (decorative, never in an accessible name). A delegated control takes `required` and announces itself as required; over any other control, the label says it in its own name on iOS and Android ("Notifications, required").

props.name: children
props.description: The control.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

props.name: xxxs
props.description: Measure (pick one; omit to take the parent's bounds). Caps the component at a step of the width scale, centered in its column; `start` pins it to the leading edge.

props.name: xxs
props.description: Measure (pick one; omit to take the parent's bounds). Caps the component at a step of the width scale, centered in its column; `start` pins it to the leading edge.

platformNotes.web:
A form row: a label, the control, and one message line under it. Field exists
for the part no control owns on its own: every field family already owns its
label, but nothing else in the kit renders helper or error text, so that message
is what Field adds.

When the row wraps a single field-family control that has no label of its own,
Field hands the label down to it rather than drawing one alongside,
so each
platform still places it its own way: a static title above on web and iOS, the
floating in-container label on Android, and `required` goes down with it.
Over
any other control (a Switch, a group) Field draws the label above with its star,
and on iOS and Android the label says "required" in its own name.
Set `error` and it replaces `helper` in
the same slot, so the row never changes height and nothing below it jumps; on the
web an error leads with a small alert glyph.

platformNotes.web:
Stitch your own fields inside it; Form adds the stacked or two-column rhythm, titled sections, the submit and cancel actions row, and Enter to submit.

The actions row sits under a hairline rule, a ghost cancel before the primary submit; each FormSection closes with the same rule. A `disabled` form dims as a whole and disables its actions.

`twoColumn` lays the rows out in exactly two equal columns 16px apart, however wide the form: the fields fill their columns left to right, an odd last field keeps its half, and a FormSection takes the whole row, after which the next field starts a new one. The form measures itself, and at 512px or narrower (the `lg` width step) the rows stack in one full-width column instead.

`FormSection aside` sets the section's heading in a rail beside its rows, the layout of a
settings page: the rail at the `xs` width step (320px), 48px from the rows, a 20px title
over a 14px description, the rows 18px apart, 28px above and below the rows and a rule
closing the section. The section measures itself, and at 512px or narrower (the `lg`
width step) the rail stacks over the rows. A form whose last row is an aside section
drops the actions row's rule (the section's closes the rows). `hints` puts leading
content in the actions row, before the buttons (the keyboard hints "↵ to save"), and the
row then spreads the two to its ends.

platformNotes.web:
Stage-by-stage conversion bars: one centered row per stage, labelled on the left and valued on the right.

The stages stack as a column of rows, each a ramp-colored bar centered in its track at the stage's share of the first stage's value, so the column tapers as the funnel drops off. The stage's label sits at the start of the row and its value, in the mono face, at the end; `share` shows every stage's percent of the first stage in the value slot instead. Each stage's accessible name carries its percent of the previous stage (of the first stage with `share`). Press a stage to select it (the others dim).

platformNotes.web:
A world map with a bubble per place, its area proportional to its count, over coastlines and country borders precomputed at build time. Optionally zoomable, merging crowded places into one bubble that splits as you zoom in.

The land silhouette and the shared country borders are two paths precomputed from Natural Earth 1:50m (no runtime fetch, no map dependency, no tiles), and each point is a circle at its projected coordinate whose AREA is proportional to its count, so doubling the count doubles the disc rather than its width.

Add `zoomable` and the wheel zooms about the pointer, two fingers pinch, a drag pans, and places too close together to draw separately merge into one bubble carrying their summed count, splitting into their members as you zoom in.

Single-identity encoding, so there is no tone axis and no legend. Press a bubble to flag its label and count (the others dim); the accessible name carries the biggest places with their values, because a screen reader user cannot see bubbles.

`detailed` frames the geography and outlines every place separately, keeping all places visible while an inline readout identifies the selected city. Zoom, pan and keyboard controls remain available.

platformNotes.web:
The container-measured auto-fit tile grid. `minTileWidth` sets the floor
(default 240): the grid fits as many equal-width columns of at least that width
as its own measured container allows, and re-fits as the container changes, so
the same grid renders three-up on a desktop, two-up on a tablet, and a single
column on a phone with no breakpoint at the call site.

`columns` caps the count at the desktop number, the gap scale is Row and
Column's own (`flush` / `tight` / `snug` / `cozy` / `relaxed` / `loose`), and a
`GridItem` child with `wide` spans two cells. The grid spans its parent's full
width (it is a FILL component, so it needs no wrapper to reach the edges), and
its tiles are equal-height as well as equal-width: every cell stretches to the
height of the row it wrapped onto, and a `Card` in a cell grows to fill it, so a
row of cards shares a flush bottom edge however unevenly their content runs (CSS
Grid's `align-items: stretch`). A field or a hug component keeps its own height.
Equal-width tiles belong here; content-sized rows that should stack at narrow
widths belong to `Row stacks`.

`flow` preserves natural card heights and the original Argus one-pixel allowance
when fitting columns. `GridItem full` spans a whole row; `raised` and `front` keep
banner and lifted-card shadows above adjacent cells. `rowsCozy` and `rowsSection`
set the vertical rhythm to 12 or 26 independently of the horizontal gap.

The shared gap scale also includes `comfortable` (10), `roomy` (14), `generous`
(22), `panel` (28), `apart` (32), `ample` (40, the step under a section page's hero) and
`broad` (48), preserving the original application layout measurements,
and Row and Column's widest step, `chapter` (64), which wins over every other step.

components.name: GridList
components.description: Tiled card grids for people directories, item collections, and image galleries.

props.name: items
props.description: The tiles to render, one card per entry.

props.name: cols3
props.description: Columns (pick one; default is three-up).

props.name: cols2
props.description: Columns (pick one; default is three-up).

props.name: gallery
props.description: Gallery mode: render each tile as a borderless thumbnail (a square color block from `item.color`, with a left-aligned filename and size below). Avatars, badges, and actions are not shown in this mode. Omit for the default people/card tile.

props.name: compact
props.description: Density modifier: tighter gap and tile padding.

props.name: onPressItem
props.description: Make each tile a tappable target (open a detail, select a tile). When set, every tile renders as a Pressable with a button role and a pressed affordance, so a tappable grid needs no hand-rolled Pressable.

props.name: label
props.description: The grid's accessible name (e.g. "Team members"): a screen reader announces it with the list of tiles. A `virtualized` grid needs one: on the web its scroller is a keyboard stop while the tiles overflow, and Chromium names an unnamed stop from the text of every tile it has rendered.

props.name: virtualized
props.description: Render the tiles through a windowed `FlatList` instead of mounting every tile up front, for large grids. Give the grid a bounded height (via `style`, e.g. `{ maxHeight: 480 }`) so it can scroll; without one it warns and renders eagerly anyway. Default (omitted) mounts all tiles, unchanged. On the web, while the tiles overflow, the windowed grid is a keyboard tab stop the keyboard can scroll, and it draws the focus ring around itself while it has keyboard focus.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Columns
groups.note: Columns (pick one; default is three-up).

groups.title: Density modifier
groups.note: Density modifier: tighter gap and tile padding.

platformNotes.web:
Tiled card grids for people directories, item collections, and image galleries.

The tiles are a list, as in Tailwind UI, and each tile is one of its items: a
screen reader announces the list with its number of tiles and moves through it
tile by tile. A tappable tile is a button inside its item.
The `label` prop names the list (for example "Team members").

A `virtualized` grid with a bounded height scrolls its tiles on its own. On the
web, while those tiles overflow, the grid is a keyboard tab stop (before the
tiles themselves when `onPressItem` or tile actions make them buttons), the
keyboard can scroll it, and while it has keyboard focus the grid, which has no
card around it, draws the theme's focus ring around itself. Only the tiles near
its viewport are mounted, and each says where it sits in the whole grid, so a
screen reader still counts every tile. Give a windowed grid a `label`: focused,
a list with no name is named in Chromium from the text of every tile it has
rendered, so the kit warns in development when it has none.

components.name: Heatmap
components.description: Density cells whose fill encodes each value, in seven-row columns inside the chart frame, titled by `label` (or `caption`) and closed by a less-to-more legend; `plain` strips the frame for nesting inside a card. Pass `calendar` for a GitHub-style contribution graph: each cell is a day, and a press or hover inspects its count and date. The calendar layout IS the kit's activity calendar, so a contribution graph needs no separate component.

props.name: values
props.description: The cells: intensities 0–1, or `{ value, count?, date?, label? }` for inspectable data.

props.name: label
props.description: What the grid measures (e.g. "Contribution activity"); leads the accessible name.

props.name: calendar
props.description: GitHub-style: the cells are days, each inspectable for its count and date.

props.name: detailed
props.description: Unframed contribution calendar with the authored month, weekday and level styling.

props.name: caption
props.description: A summary line above the grid (e.g. "248 contributions in the last year"); shown in place of `label`.

props.name: plain
props.description: Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats).

props.name: hideLegend
props.description: Hide the less-to-more legend row.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: For sizing/composition only.

components.name: Histogram
components.description: An auto-binned frequency distribution: pass raw sample `values` and the chart bins them into nice-edged uniform buckets (Sturges' rule by default, `bins` to override) and draws contiguous bars on a numeric axis.
