components.name: Icon
components.description: Lucide-style outline. 1.75 stroke width, rounded caps. The stroke defaults to the theme foreground token and tracks light and dark automatically; pick other hues with the semantic color booleans (`primary`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`, `muted`, `subtle`; that order is the precedence). `muted` is the third ink (`subtle-foreground`) and `subtle` the second (`muted-foreground`), the names Typography gives the same two inks. Inside a control that owns a label ink (a Button's `iconLeft` and `iconRight` slots) a glyph with no tone takes that ink instead, the way the hand-off's icons inherit `currentColor`: the primary's contrast ink on a primary button, the muted ink on a quiet one. The precedence is the explicit tone, then the host's ink, then the foreground, so a toned glyph keeps its tone anywhere.

props.name: disclosure
props.description: Rotate the glyph as an Argus disclosure indicator.

props.name: expanded
props.description: Open state of a disclosure indicator.

props.name: heavyStroke
props.description: Strong action/link stroke from the Argus reference.

props.name: boldStroke
props.description: Standard emphasized metadata stroke.

props.name: mediumStroke
props.description: The medium toolbar stroke.

props.name: regularStroke
props.description: The fine navigation stroke.

props.name: primary
props.description: Color axis: pass one (default foreground). First match wins.

props.name: primaryForeground
props.description: Contrast color for a glyph on a primary surface (e.g. a primary button).

props.name: success
props.description: Positive/green status (matches Alert's success tone, scheme-aware).

props.name: warning
props.description: Caution/amber status (the warning token, scheme-aware; matches Alert/Toast warning).

props.name: muted
props.description: The third ink (`subtle-foreground`, the hand-off's `--tx3`): a glyph that recedes.

props.name: subtle
props.description: The second ink (`muted-foreground`, the hand-off's `--tx2`), as Typography's `subtle`.

props.name: cell
props.description: The glyph centred in a square cell that fills its parent (a Grid tile of a glyph gallery) at a 10 px corner. On the web a hovered cell takes the accent's soft wash and its glyph the accent ink.

props.name: size
props.description: Single-glyph size in px (default 24).

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name for a MEANINGFUL standalone icon (one that conveys information not repeated in adjacent text, e.g. an icon-only button's glyph). Marks the glyph `role="img"` with this label on web and native.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Mark a DECORATIVE/ornamental glyph (one paired with a text label, a separator chevron, an empty-state illustration) so assistive tech skips it. Hides it via aria-hidden on web and importantForAccessibility on native.

groups.title: Color axis
groups.note: Color axis: pass one (default foreground). First match wins.

groups.title: Single-glyph size in px
groups.note: Single-glyph size in px (default 24).

platformNotes.web: Lucide-style outline. 1.75 stroke width, rounded caps. The stroke defaults to the theme foreground token and tracks light and dark automatically; pick other hues with the semantic color booleans (`primary`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`, `muted`, `subtle`; that order is the precedence). `muted` is the third ink (`subtle-foreground`) and `subtle` the second (`muted-foreground`), the names Typography gives the same two inks. Inside a control that owns a label ink (a Button's `iconLeft` and `iconRight` slots) a glyph with no tone takes that ink instead, the way the hand-off's icons inherit `currentColor`: the primary's contrast ink on a primary button, the muted ink on a quiet one. The precedence is the explicit tone, then the host's ink, then the foreground, so a toned glyph keeps its tone anywhere.

components.name: Image
components.description: Displays a local or remote image. Set the `source` (`{ uri }`) and a size, then choose how it fills its box with a fit prop: `cover` (the default) fills the box and crops the overflow, while `contain` fits the whole image inside and letterboxes the spare space.

props.name: source
props.description: The image to display: a remote `{ uri }`, or a bundled asset from `require(...)`.

props.name: contain
props.description: Fit: fit the whole image inside the box, letterboxing the spare space (pick one).

props.name: cover
props.description: Fit: fill the box, cropping any overflow. The default when no fit is set (pick one).

props.name: stretch
props.description: Fit: fill the box by distorting the aspect ratio (pick one).

props.name: center
props.description: Fit: center at intrinsic size, scaling down only when larger than the box (pick one).

props.name: repeat
props.description: Fit: tile the image at its intrinsic size to fill the box (pick one).

props.name: none
props.description: Fit: show at intrinsic size with no scaling (pick one).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the image box (px, or a percent string like `"100%"`). Images have no intrinsic layout size.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the image box (px, or a percent string).

props.name: radius
props.description: Corner radius from the kit's radius scale (pick one): none, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl, full.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition only (aspectRatio, layout within a parent). Size comes from `width` / `height`, rounding from `radius`.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the image, the same name `alt` gives (and it wins when both are set). On iOS and Android React Native makes an image its own accessibility element for `alt` (or `accessible`), so prefer `alt` for an image that stands on its own.

props.name: alt
props.description: The image's alt text: a named image is announced as an image with this name on every platform (the web's , the image role natively). With no name here or in `accessibilityLabel` the image is decorative, and assistive tech skips it.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the underlying image.

props.name: accessible
props.description: When true, indicates that the view is an accessibility element. By default, all the touchable elements are accessible.

props.name: accessibilityActions
props.type: readonly Readonly<{ name: AccessibilityActionName | string; label?: string | undefined; }>[] | undefined
props.description: Provides an array of custom actions available for accessibility.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Alias for accessibilityLabel https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#accessibilitylabel https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34424

props.name: blurRadius
props.description: blurRadius: the blur radius of the blur filter added to the image

props.name: accessibilityRole
props.description: Accessibility Role tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the type of element that is focused on.

props.name: capInsets
props.description: When the image is resized, the corners of the size specified by capInsets will stay a fixed size, but the center content and borders of the image will be stretched. This is useful for creating resizable rounded buttons, shadows, and other resizable assets. More info on Apple documentation

props.name: accessibilityState
props.description: Accessibility State tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the state of the element currently focused on.

props.name: onProgress
props.description: Invoked on download progress with {nativeEvent: {loaded, total}}

props.name: aria-busy
props.description: alias for accessibilityState see https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitystate

props.name: onPartialLoad
props.description: Invoked when a partial load of the image is complete. The definition of what constitutes a "partial load" is loader specific though this is meant for progressive JPEG loads.

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: An accessibility hint helps users understand what will happen when they perform an action on the accessibility element when that result is not obvious from the accessibility label.

props.name: accessibilityValue
props.description: Represents the current value of a component. It can be a textual description of a component's value, or for range-based components, such as sliders and progress bars, it contains range information (minimum, current, and maximum).

props.name: onAccessibilityAction
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs an accessibility custom action.

props.name: importantForAccessibility
props.description: [Android] Controlling if a view fires accessibility events and if it is reported to accessibility services.

props.name: resizeMethod
props.description: The mechanism that should be used to resize the image when the image's dimensions differ from the image view's dimensions. Defaults to `auto`. - `auto`: Use heuristics to pick between `resize` and `scale`. - `resize`: A software operation which changes the encoded image in memory before it gets decoded. This should be used instead of `scale` when the image is much larger than the view. - `scale`: The image gets drawn downscaled or upscaled. Compared to `resize`, `scale` is faster (usually hardware accelerated) and produces higher quality images. This should be used if the image is smaller than the view. It should also be used if the image is slightly bigger than the view. - `none`: No sampling is performed and the image is displayed in its full resolution. This should only be used in rare circumstances because it is considered unsafe as Android will throw a runtime exception when trying to render images that consume too much memory. More details about `resize` and `scale` can be found at http://frescolib.org/docs/resizing-rotating.html.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description: A value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within this accessibility element are hidden.

props.name: fadeDuration
props.description: Duration of fade in animation in ms. Defaults to 300

props.name: role
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services to treat UI component like a specific role.

props.name: id
props.description: Used to reference react managed images from native code.

props.name: onLayout
props.description: onLayout function Invoked on mount and layout changes with {nativeEvent: { layout: {x, y, width, height} }}.

props.name: onError
props.description: Invoked on load error with {nativeEvent: {error}}

props.name: onLoad
props.description: Invoked when load completes successfully { source: { uri, height, width } }.

props.name: onLoadEnd
props.description: Invoked when load either succeeds or fails

props.name: onLoadStart
props.description: Invoked on load start

props.name: accessibilityLabelledBy
props.description: Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props, the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props, the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: accessibilityLiveRegion
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: src
props.description: A string representing the resource identifier for the image. Similar to src from HTML. See https://reactnative.dev/docs/image#src

props.name: srcSet
props.description: Similar to srcset from HTML. See https://reactnative.dev/docs/image#srcset

props.name: aria-live
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: loadingIndicatorSource

props.name: nativeID

props.name: defaultSource
props.description: A static image to display while downloading the final image off the network.

props.name: screenReaderFocusable
props.description: Enables the view to be screen reader focusable, not keyboard focusable.

props.name: accessibilityElementsHidden
props.description: A Boolean value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within this accessibility element are hidden to the screen reader.

props.name: crossOrigin
props.description: Adds the CORS related header to the request. Similar to crossorigin from HTML. See https://reactnative.dev/docs/image#crossorigin

props.name: accessibilityViewIsModal
props.description: A Boolean value indicating whether VoiceOver should ignore the elements within views that are siblings of the receiver.

props.name: tintColor
props.description: Changes the color of all the non-transparent pixels to the tintColor. See https://reactnative.dev/docs/image#tintcolor

props.name: onAccessibilityEscape
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the escape gesture (scrub with two fingers).

props.name: referrerPolicy
props.description: A string indicating which referrer to use when fetching the resource. Similar to referrerpolicy from HTML. See https://reactnative.dev/docs/image#referrerpolicy

props.name: onAccessibilityTap
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs accessibility tap gesture.

props.name: onMagicTap
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the magic tap gesture.

props.name: accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors
props.description: https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityignoresinvertcolorsios

props.name: accessibilityLanguage
props.description: By using the accessibilityLanguage property, the screen reader will understand which language to use while reading the element's label, value and hint. props.name: accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer
props.description: A Boolean value that indicates whether or not to show the item in the large content viewer. Available on iOS 13.0+ https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityshowslargecontentviewer

props.name: accessibilityLargeContentTitle

props.name: accessibilityRespondsToUserInteraction
props.description: Blocks the user from interacting with the component through keyboard while still allowing screen reader to interact with it if this View is still accessible.

groups.title: Fit
groups.note: Fit (pick one; default `cover`). Chooses how the image is sized to fill its box. When more than one is set, first match wins in the order below.

platformNotes.web:
Displays a local or remote image. Set the `source` (`{ uri }`) and a size, then choose how it fills its box with a fit prop: `cover` (the default) fills the box and crops the overflow, while `contain` fits the whole image inside and letterboxes the spare space.

`stretch`, `center`, `repeat`, and `none` cover the rarer fits. `repeat` tiles a bundled asset (or a `{ uri, width, height }` source) at its point size on every platform, drawing the density variant that matches the screen (`grain@2x.png` on a 2x screen) into each tile; a box with no size of its own is one tile. A remote image with no stated size keeps React Native's own repeat. Remote images load over the network; bundle local assets with `require`. Name an image that carries content with `alt`, and it is announced as an image with that name on every platform; an image with no name is decorative, and assistive tech skips it. The v4 hand-off rounds a standalone photo at 12 (`radius="xl"`); Image draws no corner of its own, so a photo inside a Card or a Video keeps its host's corner. For a circular identity photo with an initials fallback, reach for `<Avatar src="…" name="…" />` rather than rounding a bare Image.

components.name: Input
components.description: The Input component is a React Native text field with semantic boolean props (`error`, `small`, `large`, `compact`, `disabled`), plus prefix/suffix addons, overlaid icons (`leadingIcon` / `trailingIcon` with any Canvas glyph as `icon`), a `passwordToggle` eye for a `secureTextEntry` value, a `clearable` clear button, and a `shortcut` keycap. Input is single-line; for multi-line entry use the dedicated Textarea.

props.name: value
props.description: Current text value (controlled). Omit and use `defaultValue` for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onChangeText
props.description: Called with the new text on each keystroke.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder shown while the field is empty.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's persistent label. Its placement is platform-adaptive: iOS and web render it ABOVE the field (the static title the Field/Form composers produce today); Android renders the Material 3 in-container FLOATING label (centered like a placeholder at rest, floating to the top once the field is focused or filled). The label is the field's programmatic name (wired via both accessibilityLabel and aria-labelledby), so a placeholder is no longer needed for the accessible name.

props.name: search
props.description: A toolbar search field with a magnifier and a tracked uppercase empty prompt on web.

props.name: eyebrow
props.description: Dense uppercase eyebrow label where the skin offers it.

props.name: systemFocus
props.description: Preserve the system focus outline on a framed field.

props.name: soft
props.description: Use the brand’s softer entry-well fill where the skin provides it.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field as required: appends a destructive "*" to the label (decorative, never in the accessible name) and announces the field as required, through aria-required on the web and with the word in its name ("Full name, required") on iOS and Android. The star takes effect only alongside `label`.

props.name: error
props.description: State (orthogonal). `error` (alias `invalid`) flags a validation problem.

props.name: invalid
props.description: State (orthogonal). `error` (alias `invalid`) flags a validation problem.

props.name: disabled
props.description: State (orthogonal). `error` (alias `invalid`) flags a validation problem.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Read-only: shows the value but blocks editing without the dimmed look.

props.name: small
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the medium field).

props.name: large
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the medium field).

props.name: compact
props.description: A compact outlined well: 40 high with a 14px value by default; small is 32/13, large is 48/16. Keeps the platform's field corner and places labels above.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Leading addon content (e.g. "https://", "$", an icon glyph).

props.name: suffix
props.description: Trailing addon content (e.g. "@canvas.dev", "USD", "Copy").

props.name: leadingIcon
props.description: Render `icon` as a passive glyph inside the left of the field.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: Render `icon` as a passive glyph inside the right of the field.

props.name: icon
props.description: Glyph name for leadingIcon/trailingIcon: any Canvas glyph (e.g. "search", "mail", "lock", "phone", "calendar", "creditCard").

props.name: action
props.description: Render the suffix as a pressable action button rather than a passive label.

props.name: onActionPress
props.description: Called when the action suffix is pressed (action only).

props.name: passwordToggle
props.description: A trailing eye button that reveals and re-masks a `secureTextEntry` value (the password field's show/hide toggle). The field starts masked; the button is announced as "Show password" / "Hide password". Takes effect only with `secureTextEntry`.

props.name: clearable
props.description: A trailing clear button (a circled x) that empties the field, shown while the field holds text (the search field's clear affordance). Works in both the controlled and the uncontrolled mode: it clears the native field and reports "" through `onChangeText`.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: A keyboard shortcut hint at the field's end: a compact flat keycap (`<Kbd small flat>`, the 20 px `tiny` cap on a `small` field) after the value and any inline suffix, before the trailing glyphs, the hint a search field shows for the key that focuses it (`shortcut="⌘K"`). Pass the keys as Kbd's `keys` takes them: `"⌘K"` is one cap, `"⌘ K"` two. A hint only: bind the key yourself.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the field when there is no programmatically-associated visible label. Maps to accessibilityLabel + the aria-label web alias on the underlying TextInput, so a Form/Field control is announced with its name.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: ID of the visible label element that names this field (its `nativeID`). react-native-web forwards aria-labelledby to the DOM input; prefer this over accessibilityLabel when a visible <Text> label is present so the label and field are programmatically linked.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: ID of the helper/error text that describes this field (its `nativeID`), so a screen reader reads the hint after the field name.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

props.name: textContentType
props.description: Give the keyboard and the system information about the expected semantic meaning for the content that users enter. To disable autofill, set textContentType to `none`. props.name: autoCapitalize
props.description: Can tell TextInput to automatically capitalize certain characters. characters: all characters, words: first letter of each word sentences: first letter of each sentence (default) none: don't auto capitalize anything https://reactnative.dev/docs/textinput#autocapitalize

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: Specifies autocomplete hints for the system, so it can provide autofill. On Android, the system will always attempt to offer autofill by using heuristics to identify the type of content. To disable autocomplete, set autoComplete to off. The following values work across platforms: - `additional-name` - `address-line1` - `address-line2` - `cc-number` - `country` - `current-password` - `email` - `family-name` - `given-name` - `honorific-prefix` - `honorific-suffix` - `name` - `new-password` - `off` - `one-time-code` - `postal-code` - `street-address` - `tel` - `username` The following values work on iOS only: - `nickname` - `organization` - `organization-title` - `url` The following values work on Android only: - `birthdate-day` - `birthdate-full` - `birthdate-month` - `birthdate-year` - `cc-csc` - `cc-exp` - `cc-exp-day` - `cc-exp-month` - `cc-exp-year` - `2fa-app-otp` - `email-otp` - `flight-confirmation-code` - `flight-number` - `gender` - `gift-card-number` - `gift-card-pin` - `loyalty-account-number` - `name-family` - `name-given` - `name-middle` - `name-middle-initial` - `name-prefix` - `name-suffix` - `password` - `password-new` - `postal-address` - `postal-address-country` - `postal-address-dependent-locality` - `postal-address-extended` - `postal-address-extended-postal-code` - `postal-address-locality` - `postal-address-region` - `postal-address-unit` - `promo-code` - `sms-otp` - `tel-country-code` - `tel-national` - `tel-device` - `upi-vpa` - `wifi-password` - `username-new`

props.name: autoCorrect
props.description: If false, disables auto-correct. The default value is true.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: If true, focuses the input on componentDidMount. The default value is false.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Provides an initial value that will change when the user starts typing. Useful for simple use-cases where you don't want to deal with listening to events and updating the value prop to keep the controlled state in sync.

props.name: keyboardType
props.description: enum("default", 'numeric', 'email-address', "ascii-capable", 'numbers-and-punctuation', 'url', 'number-pad', 'phone-pad', 'name-phone-pad', 'decimal-pad', 'twitter', 'web-search', 'visible-password') Determines which keyboard to open, e.g.numeric. The following values work across platforms: - default - numeric - email-address - phone-pad The following values work on iOS: - ascii-capable - numbers-and-punctuation - url - number-pad - name-phone-pad - decimal-pad - twitter - web-search The following values work on Android: - visible-password

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Works like the inputmode attribute in HTML, it determines which keyboard to open, e.g. numeric and has precedence over keyboardType.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Limits the maximum number of characters that can be entered. Use this instead of implementing the logic in JS to avoid flicker.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input is blurred Note: If you are trying to find the last value of TextInput, you can use the `onEndEditing` event, which is fired upon completion of editing.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input is focused

props.name: onSubmitEditing
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's submit button is pressed.

props.name: onKeyPress
props.description: Callback that is called when a key is pressed. This will be called with `{ nativeEvent: { key: keyValue } }` where keyValue is 'Enter' or 'Backspace' for respective keys and the typed-in character otherwise including ' ' for space. Fires before onChange callbacks. Note: on Android only the inputs from soft keyboard are handled, not the hardware keyboard inputs.

props.name: returnKeyType
props.description: enum('default', 'go', 'google', 'join', 'next', 'route', 'search', 'send', 'yahoo', 'done', 'emergency-call') Determines how the return key should look.

props.name: secureTextEntry
props.description: If true, the text input obscures the text entered so that sensitive text like passwords stay secure. The default value is false.

props.name: testID
props.description: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the underlying React Native host. Supports object refs and callback refs; native methods follow the platform's behavior.

props.name: xxxs
props.description: Measure (pick one; omit to take the parent's bounds). Caps the component at a step of the width scale, centered in its column; `start` pins it to the leading edge.

groups.title: State
groups.note: State (orthogonal). `error` (alias `invalid`) flags a validation problem.

groups.title: Size
groups.note: Size (pick one; default is the medium field).

groups.title: Addons
groups.note: Addons. Passing any of these switches the field to the grouped layout: a single control where a leading prefix and/or trailing suffix share one outer border with the field (squared joined edges, 1px inner separators), so they read as one piece rather than detached. Addons are plain strings, so no icon library is required at this layer.

groups.title: Overlaid glyph mode
groups.note: Overlaid glyph mode. Unlike prefix/suffix (a bordered addon box), these float a real Lucide glyph INSIDE the field with no separator, and pad the text away from it (pl-9 / pr-9). `icon` names which glyph (see ICON_BOOL).

groups.title: Measure
groups.note: Measure (pick one; omit to take the parent's bounds). Caps the component at a step of the width scale, centered in its column; `start` pins it to the leading edge.

platformNotes.web:
The Input component is a React Native text field with semantic boolean props
(`error`, `small`, `large`, `compact`, `disabled`), plus prefix/suffix addons, overlaid
icons (`leadingIcon` / `trailingIcon` with any Canvas glyph as `icon`), a
`passwordToggle` eye for a `secureTextEntry` value, a `clearable` clear
button, and a `shortcut` keycap. Input is single-line; for multi-line entry use the
dedicated Textarea.

On the web the eye shows what pressing it does: the open eye while the value is masked,
the struck-through eye once it is revealed. A field held
focused by an `InteractionOverride` (a docs specimen) draws the web's 1.5px accent caret,
blinking once a second, just after its value, since no real caret shows there.

`shortcut` shows a keyboard shortcut hint at the field's end, the key that focuses a
search field: a compact flat keycap (`<Kbd small flat>`, the 22 px cap; `tiny`, the 20 px
cap, on a `small` field) after the value and any inline suffix and before the trailing
glyphs, 8 px from the field's end and 10 px from the value (8 on a small field). It takes
the keys as Kbd's `keys` does: `"⌘K"` is one cap, `"⌘ K"` two. It is a hint only; bind
the key yourself.

Pass `label` (and `required`) to name the field:
iOS and web render the label
above the control, while Android floats the Material 3 in-container label. On
Android the field grows with the user's text size so the floated label never
meets the value, and a label longer than the field truncates on one line inside
it while the field's accessible name stays the whole label.
The required star is
decorative: a screen reader hears the field as required,
from `aria-required` on
the web and from its name ("Full name, required") on iOS and Android.
A field fills the parent it is given; a step of its own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with
`start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a Container step sets its measure.
Select and the search field share its look, and Field and Form compose that
label with helper and error text.
On iOS the field is the native text field in
Canvas's colors: a card-colored box with a hairline, a muted title above, a glyph
that tints with focus and error, and in solid mode an error wash. Under glass a
wash would cost the field's ink its contrast over the material, so the iOS field
takes none (the web's field a trace in dark only), and the error border, the tinted
glyph and a Field's message carry the state.
A prefix or suffix addon's fill is held to
the same bar: under glass it is only as dense as keeps its text at 4.5:1 over the field,
so in the browser's light palettes and on the iOS field in dark it is a faint trace.

Inside an overlay, Escape follows the overlay's cancellation policy. A supplied
`onKeyPress` runs first and can call `preventDefault()` to handle Escape locally.
Cancelling an IME candidate keeps the overlay open.

On web, the field is a sunken well: 40 pixels tall (32 small, 48 large) at the
10-pixel field corner, a hairline edge, a 12-pixel inset, a regular 14-pixel value
(13 small) and a medium 13-pixel muted label above. The edge darkens under the
pointer, takes the accent with a soft accent halo on focus, and turns red with a
red halo for an error; a read-only field is a dashed edge on no fill, and a
disabled one dims. A prefix sits in a muted box behind a divider, a passive
suffix is inline monospace text before the clear button (a small raised disc with
an x), and an action suffix is a button box at the end.

On iOS the clear button is the system's gray disc with an x, inside the boxed
suffix segment, and the action suffix's label is a semibold 15-point brand label.
On Android the suffix is inline text before the circled-x clear glyph, an errored
field shows a red alert glyph at its end (in place of a clear or eye button), and
a read-only field drops its fill under a dashed frame with a subtle underline.

`eyebrow` uses the original dense uppercase web field label, preserving its
9.5/12.35 metrics and tracking. Other platform label treatments retain their skin.

`soft` uses the brand’s entry-well fill where the skin provides it.
`systemFocus` preserves the platform’s system focus outline. An explicit
`accessibilityLabel` takes precedence over the visible label’s accessible name.

Pass `search` for the toolbar search: a magnifier, a borderless editor, and a
uppercase prompt while empty on web. The prompt names the editor unless
`accessibilityLabel` or `label` supplies its purpose.
iOS draws its search field
(a 36-point muted well) and Android the Material 3 search bar (a 56-dp muted
stadium).
`systemFocus` preserves the system
focus outline for the borderless editor.

pointer, takes the accent with a soft accent halo on focus, and turns red with a
red halo for an error; a read-only field is a dashed edge on no fill, and a
disabled one dims. A prefix sits in a muted box behind a divider, a passive
suffix is inline monospace text before the clear button (a small raised disc with
an x), and an action suffix is a button box at the end.

On iOS the clear button is the system's gray disc with an x, inside the boxed
suffix segment, and the action suffix's label is a semibold 15-point brand label.

`eyebrow` uses the original dense uppercase web field label, preserving its
9.5/12.35 metrics and tracking. Other platform label treatments retain their skin.

`soft` uses the brand’s entry-well fill where the skin provides it.
`systemFocus` preserves the platform’s system focus outline. An explicit
`accessibilityLabel` takes precedence over the visible label’s accessible name.

Pass `search` for the toolbar search: a magnifier, a borderless editor, and a
uppercase prompt while empty on web. The prompt names the editor unless
`accessibilityLabel` or `label` supplies its purpose.
iOS draws its search field (a 36-point muted well).
`systemFocus` preserves the system
focus outline for the borderless editor.
platformNotes.android:
The Input component is a React Native text field with semantic boolean props
(`error`, `small`, `large`, `compact`, `disabled`), plus prefix/suffix addons, overlaid
icons (`leadingIcon` / `trailingIcon` with any Canvas glyph as `icon`), a
`passwordToggle` eye for a `secureTextEntry` value, a `clearable` clear
button, and a `shortcut` keycap. Input is single-line; for multi-line entry use the
dedicated Textarea.

On the web the eye shows what pressing it does: the open eye while the value is masked,
the struck-through eye once it is revealed. A field held
focused by an `InteractionOverride` (a docs specimen) draws the web's 1.5px accent caret,
blinking once a second, just after its value, since no real caret shows there.

`shortcut` shows a keyboard shortcut hint at the field's end, the key that focuses a
search field: a compact flat keycap (`<Kbd small flat>`, the 22 px cap; `tiny`, the 20 px
cap, on a `small` field) after the value and any inline suffix and before the trailing
glyphs, 8 px from the field's end and 10 px from the value (8 on a small field). It takes
the keys as Kbd's `keys` does: `"⌘K"` is one cap, `"⌘ K"` two. It is a hint only; bind
the key yourself.

Pass `label` (and `required`) to name the field:
Android floats the Material 3 in-container label. The field grows with the user's text size so the floated label never meets the value, and a label longer than the field truncates on one line inside it while the field's accessible name stays the whole label.
The required star is
decorative: a screen reader hears the field as required,
from its name ("Full name, required").
A field fills the parent it is given; a step of its own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with
`start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a Container step sets its measure.
Select and the search field share its look, and Field and Form compose that
label with helper and error text.
A prefix or suffix addon's fill is held to
the same bar: under glass it is only as dense as keeps its text at 4.5:1 over the field,
so in a light palette it is a faint trace.

Inside an overlay, Escape follows the overlay's cancellation policy. A supplied
`onKeyPress` runs first and can call `preventDefault()` to handle Escape locally.
Cancelling an IME candidate keeps the overlay open.

On web, the field is a sunken well: 40 pixels tall (32 small, 48 large) at the
10-pixel field corner, a hairline edge, a 12-pixel inset, a regular 14-pixel value
(13 small) and a medium 13-pixel muted label above. The edge darkens under the
pointer, takes the accent with a soft accent halo on focus, and turns red with a
red halo for an error; a read-only field is a dashed edge on no fill, and a
disabled one dims. A prefix sits in a muted box behind a divider, a passive
suffix is inline monospace text before the clear button (a small raised disc with
an x), and an action suffix is a button box at the end.

On Android the suffix is inline text before the circled-x clear glyph, an errored
field shows a red alert glyph at its end (in place of a clear or eye button), and
a read-only field drops its fill under a dashed frame with a subtle underline.

`eyebrow` uses the original dense uppercase web field label, preserving its
9.5/12.35 metrics and tracking. Other platform label treatments retain their skin.

`soft` uses the brand’s entry-well fill where the skin provides it.
`systemFocus` preserves the platform’s system focus outline. An explicit
`accessibilityLabel` takes precedence over the visible label’s accessible name.

Pass `search` for the toolbar search: a magnifier, a borderless editor, and a
uppercase prompt while empty on web. The prompt names the editor unless
`accessibilityLabel` or `label` supplies its purpose.
Android draws the Material 3 search bar (a 56-dp muted stadium).
`systemFocus` preserves the system
focus outline for the borderless editor.

components.name: InputOTP
components.description: A segmented one-time-code field: `length` cells display the typed characters while one underlying text input captures the keystrokes, so native SMS autofill, the one-time-code keyboard suggestion, and paste all flow into a single value.

props.name: length
props.description: Number of segment cells (and the max code length). Default 6.

props.name: value
props.description: Current code (controlled). Only the typed characters, e.g. "123". Omit for uncontrolled use; a bare <InputOTP /> is typeable out of the box.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Starting code for the uncontrolled field. Defaults to empty.

props.name: onChangeText
props.description: Called with the new code (cleaned, sliced to `length`) on each change (both modes).

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Fired once when the code reaches `length` digits.

props.name: groups
props.description: Split the run into groups of this many cells, separated by a dash: `length={6}` with `groups={3}` reads 123-456. Omit for one unbroken run.

props.name: alphanumeric
props.description: Accept letters as well as digits, and ask for the text keyboard instead of the number pad. Off by default: a one-time code is digits only.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Focus the field on mount.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable input and dim the cells.

props.name: masked
props.description: Render a bullet (●) instead of the character, for passcode entry.

props.name: small
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the medium cell).

props.name: large
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the medium cell).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the underlying React Native host. Supports object refs and callback refs; native methods follow the platform's behavior.

groups.title: Size
groups.note: Size (pick one; default is the medium cell).

platformNotes.web:
A segmented one-time-code field: `length` cells display the typed characters while one underlying text input captures the keystrokes, so native SMS autofill, the one-time-code keyboard suggestion, and paste all flow into a single value.

Because that one input spans the whole row, the caret is pinned to the end of the code: tap any cell and the next character still lands in the first unfilled one, so a keystroke can never drop into the middle of a partly-entered code. It works controlled (`value` + `onChangeText`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`, or a bare `<InputOTP />` that is typeable out of the box); `onComplete` fires once the code reaches `length` characters. Style and shape it with semantic props: `groups` splits the run into dash-separated chunks, `alphanumeric` accepts letters as well as digits, and `small`, `large`, `masked`, `disabled` and `autoFocus` do what they say.

components.name: Kbd
components.description: Keyboard shortcut indicator: a raised 24 px key cap with a mono label. `keys` composes a whole shortcut, one cap per key; `sequence` says "then" between the caps of keys pressed one after another. A shortcut reads as one accessible name ("⌘+K", "G then C"). `comfortable` pads the cap 3 px above and below its label and 8 px at the sides (25 px tall) for a key set beside what it does, as a reference's keyboard table lists it; omit it for the 24 px cap with 6 px sides.

props.name: children
props.description: A single key label, rendered as one cap. Ignored when `keys` is set.

props.name: keys
props.description: A multi-key shortcut (a combo, pressed together), rendered as one cap per key. Pass a whitespace-separated string (`"⌘ K"`) or an array (`["⌘", "K"]`). A single entry renders one cap, identical to passing that key as `children`. When set, `keys` takes precedence over `children`.

props.name: sequence
props.description: Render a key SEQUENCE (press one, then the next): the caps are separated by "then". Only affects the `keys` form.

props.name: comfortable
props.description: The comfortable cap: padded 3 px above and below its label and 8 px at the sides (25 px tall), the key the hand-off's component page sets beside a key's effect. Omit for the 24 px cap with 6 px sides.

props.name: small
props.description: The compact 22 px cap: 6 px sides on the small key corner, a 500 11 px label on a 20 px line (the hint a search field or a command palette shows, `<Kbd small flat>`). Size precedence: `small` > `tiny`; a size step wins over `comfortable`.

props.name: tiny
props.description: The compact 20 px cap: 5 px sides on the tiny key corner, a 500 10 px label on an 18 px line.

props.name: flat
props.description: The hint cap's edge: one pixel all round (no raised 2 px bottom) and the label in the secondary ink, the keycap a field or a menu shows beside what it opens.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

components.name: LineChart
components.description: Categorical-x series lines with nice y ticks, gridlines, and a legend for multiple series.

props.name: dots
props.description: Mark each datum with a dot.

props.name: baseline
props.description: Reference value (e.g. previous close) drawn as a dashed line. A single series with no explicit tone auto-tones success/destructive by whether its last value sits above or below the baseline - the trading-app gain/loss idiom.

props.name: fade
props.description: Soft gradient fade under the lead (first) series' line (the price-chart look).

props.name: labels
props.description: Category labels along the x axis, one per data column.

props.name: series
props.description: The series to plot; colors follow the chart-1..8 tokens in fixed order, or a series' own `success`/`destructive` tone.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional heading shown above the plot.

props.name: max
props.description: Y-axis maximum override. Defaults to a nice bound above the data max.

props.name: min
props.description: Y-axis minimum override. Defaults to 0 (or the data min when negative).

props.name: success
props.description: Tone (single-series only; pick one; default is the primary fill).

props.name: destructive
props.description: Tone (single-series only; pick one; default is the primary fill).

props.name: curved
props.description: Curve (omit for straight segments).

props.name: compact
props.description: Density (omit for the default plot size).

props.name: plain
props.description: Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats).

props.name: hideLegend
props.description: Furniture visibility.

props.name: hideGrid
props.description: Furniture visibility.

props.name: hideAxes
props.description: Furniture visibility.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats tick labels and accessible values (data formatting, not styling).

props.name: selected
props.description: Scrub-to-inspect: the selected category index (controlled). Pass null for none.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: Scrub-to-inspect: the initially selected category (uncontrolled).

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fired when a press/scrub selects a category (or clears it with null).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Tone
groups.note: Tone (single-series only; pick one; default is the primary fill).

groups.title: Curve
groups.note: Curve (omit for straight segments).

groups.title: Density
groups.note: Density (omit for the default plot size).

platformNotes.web:

`curved` draws a monotone cubic that never overshoots the data, `dots` marks each datum, and `baseline` + `fade` give the trading-app price idiom (dashed previous close, gain/loss auto tone, gradient fill). components.name: Listbox
components.description: A custom select whose options stay on screen: single or multi-select, an optional detail line under each option, and a checkmark on the chosen items. Reach for it when the options need rich rows; prefer `Select` for a simple short list.

props.name: items
props.description: The options to render, top to bottom.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the option list or multi-select checkbox group. Defaults to "Options".

props.name: multi

props.name: bordered

props.name: small

props.name: large

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dim the list and block selection.

props.name: selected

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: Initial selection for uncontrolled use (a bare listbox selects on press). Falls back to the `selected` flags on `items` when omitted.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fired with the full new selection (an index in single-select, an index array in multi).

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fired with the pressed option's index.

props.name: testID

platformNotes.web:
A custom select whose options stay on screen: single or multi-select, an optional detail line under each option, and a checkmark on the chosen items. Reach for it when the options need rich rows; prefer `Select` for a simple short list.

The list fills the parent it is given; a step of its own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with `start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a Container step sets its measure.

Neither iOS nor Material 3 ships a listbox, so every platform draws the Canvas v4 list, in its own face:
a chosen row sits on the accent's soft wash with a 16px check at its end in the accent ink, in single and multi select alike, and the check's slot is kept on every row so a choice never reflows a label.

The rows are 10px in with a 500 14/18.2px label (13px small) over a 400 12/16.2px detail in the subtle ink, rounded concentric inside a bordered list, which is the `popover` fill behind the `field-border` hairline at the tile corner with a 4px inset. A pressed row takes the `muted` wash, and on the web a row under the pointer takes the hover wash at once.

Single-select exposes a list of selectable options. With `multi`, it exposes a checkbox group: each row owns its label, checked state, and tap target. Give either mode a meaningful `accessibilityLabel`; the fallback is "Options". Arrow keys and Home/End move focus within one tab stop. Single-select follows focus, while multi-select keeps the current selection until Enter or Space toggles the focused row.

components.name: MediaObject
components.description: Image or icon paired with text content. The fundamental building block for list items, notifications, and comment layouts.

props.name: title
props.description: Primary line: the bold heading (e.g. a person's name).

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary line: muted supporting text under the title (e.g. a role or email).

props.name: body
props.description: Optional longer body paragraph rendered below the description.

props.name: meta
props.description: Trailing metadata text pinned to the right (e.g. "2h ago", "admin").

props.name: avatar
props.description: Initials for the leading avatar (e.g. "RC"); rendered as <Avatar>{avatar}</Avatar>.

props.name: src
props.description: Photo for the leading avatar (a URI string or a bundled `require(...)` image); takes precedence over initials.

props.name: icon
props.description: A leading icon glyph rendered in a tinted square box (stands in for an SVG icon).

props.name: bareIcon
props.description: Draw the `icon` node as it is, with no tinted box around it: a lead that is its own mark, such as a numbered `<Badge step>` (the Layout page's "try in this order" list).

props.name: action

platformNotes.web:
The decomposed-metric dashboard card: headline value, tone-aware rate, Sparkline trend, per-category share rows, and a chip footer.

It holds a preformatted headline `value` with its caption, an optional secondary `rate` readout under the headline (toned by `rateSuccess`, `rateWarning`, or `rateDestructive`), an optional trend strip drawn by the kit Sparkline at the header's end with a latest-value caption above it, per-category `breakdown` rows with proportional share meters and Stats-style deltas, and a `chips` footer for recent notable codes. Every section is independently optional, so one layout backs OAuth token issuance, API request volume, sign-up sources, and any metric that needs decomposition plus trend in one card.

`detailed` emphasizes the value without repeating its caption, shows a trend arrow beside the rate and places the share rows under a divider. Its spark values are percentages from zero to one hundred; `rateLabel` supplies the period comparison.

components.name: Navbar
components.description: Topbars with a brand, navigation links, and an action button. Used as the primary app-level navigation.

props.name: brand
props.description: Brand or product name shown at the left, in a semibold face.

props.name: brandContent
props.description: A brand ELEMENT for the left cluster (a logo mark, a workspace switcher). It LEADS the cluster, so passing it beside `brand` renders the mark first and keeps the wordmark beside it; passing it alone makes the mark the whole brand. It takes the left cluster's own gap, so it needs no wrapper.

props.name: brandHref
props.description: Where the brand leads (an app's home, `/`). With it, or with `onBrandPress`, the brand lockup is one link: a real anchor on the web (an `<a href>`, so middle-click and modifier-click open it in a new tab), named by `brand`, with the kit's focus ring.

props.name: onBrandPress
props.description: Called when the brand is pressed; on the web a modifier-click on a `brandHref` stays the browser's.

props.name: brandDivider
props.description: Draw a short vertical separator between the brand and the links (the kit `<Divider vertical inset strong />`), as the hand-off's floating docs pill does. It shows only while both the brand and the links row are on the bar, so a collapsed bar or one without links never ends its brand on a stray rule.

props.name: links
props.description: Ordered navigation link labels rendered in the middle row. Omit it (or pass an empty array) for a bar with no middle nav: neither the links row nor the narrow menu button that stands in for it renders.

props.name: hrefs
props.description: Destinations for `links`, by index (parallel to it). A link with an href renders as a real anchor on the web (an `<a href>`, so middle-click, modifier-click and open-in-new-tab work); natively it is ignored. A plain click still selects the link and calls `onSelect` with the press event, so an app that routes on the client calls `event.preventDefault()` there; a modifier or middle click is left to the browser and selects nothing. Omit it (or an entry) for a link without a destination.

props.name: active
props.description: Index of the active link (CONTROLLED; its label reads in the foreground color). Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultActive
props.description: Initial active link for uncontrolled use (a bare navbar moves the active link on press).

props.name: actions
props.description: Free-form trailing controls for the right cluster: a ghost search button, icon buttons, a notification dropdown, an account menu. They LEAD the cluster, ahead of the built-in `actionLabel` button and `avatar`, and take the cluster's own gap, so they need no wrapper. Keep them few and compact: the bar is a fixed height and the slot is rendered as given at every width.

props.name: actionLabel
props.description: Optional primary action; renders a <Button primary small> on the right.

props.name: onAction
props.description: Called when the action button is pressed.

props.name: avatar
props.description: Optional account initials/name; renders an <Avatar small> on the right.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called when a nav link is pressed, with its index, and the press event when it came from the link itself (not from the narrow menu).

props.name: onMenu
props.description: The app's own navigation menu. When set, the bar leads with a menu button at every width and calls this on press, so the app can open navigation of its own (a Drawer of grouped sections). It replaces the `links` row and its narrow menu: pass one or the other.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Surface (pick one; default is the flush bottom-hairline bar).

props.name: floating
props.description: Surface (pick one; default is the flush bottom-hairline bar).

props.name: bare
props.description: No surface and no hairline: the bar sits clear on what is behind it. Pass it while nothing has scrolled under the bar (the scroll edge) and drop it once content does.

props.name: compact
props.description: The tight bar: 44px with a 5px inset and 2px between items on the web (the docs pill).

props.name: scrolls
props.description: Keep every link at every width: the bar's content row scrolls sideways inside the bar (no scroll indicator) instead of folding the links into the narrow menu button. Pair it with `floating` and `compact` for the hand-off's docs pill.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook.

platformNotes.web:
Topbars with a brand, navigation links, and an action button. Used as the
primary app-level navigation.

The bar measures its own width: at and below the `sm` breakpoint (640) the links
row automatically collapses into a menu button opening a dropdown of the same
links (the active one checkmarked), so links never clip off a phone screen;
`active` and `onSelect` keep their contract in both renderings.
The menu button
leads the bar, ahead of the logo and brand, where Material 3's top app bar puts
its navigation icon.
Pass `scrolls` to keep every link at every width instead: the bar's content row
then pans sideways inside the bar, with no scroll indicator, and the links never
fold into the menu. `onMenu` still replaces the links when both are passed.

On the web the bar is the v4 hand-off's: 56px tall with a 16px gutter, 32px
capsule links in the interface face, the active one (and a hovered one) on the
`secondary` fill. `floating` lifts it as a pill on the stronger hairline with the
md shade.
On iOS and Android the bar keeps the platform's own navigation bar and
top app bar shape.

In glass mode the active link paints a control-layer pane
(iOS keeps its
inactive capsules and carries the brand fill as glass, web and Android carry
their tinted tile),
and the collapsed menu is Dropdown's dense-layer glass card
under the hamburger. Solid mode keeps the skin's own active tile.

Either cluster takes a caller-supplied element beside its built-in parts:
`brandContent` leads the left one with a logo mark (beside or instead of the
`brand` wordmark) and `actions` leads the right one with free-form trailing
controls (a search button, icon buttons), ahead of `actionLabel` and `avatar`.
`links` is optional, so a console topbar with no middle nav renders neither the
links row nor the menu button that stands in for it.

props.name: itemCount

props.name: compact

props.name: defaultPageSize
props.description: Initial rows-per-page value for uncontrolled use (the selector cycles on press).

props.name: pageSizes
props.description: Selectable rows-per-page values; pressing the selector advances through them.

props.name: onPageSizeChange
props.description: Fired with the next rows-per-page value when the selector is pressed.

props.name: small
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the medium size).

props.name: large
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the medium size).

props.name: disabled

props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

platformNotes.web:
Page-of-N navigation for tables and lists.

Neither iOS nor Android has a numbered pagination control, so every platform shows the
same pager:
rounded hairline cells at 28, 34 or 40 (small, default, large), the page
numbers in 13px mono numerals, and the current page in the accent fill with a soft glow
beneath it. Previous and Next carry a chevron and a "Prev" / "Next" label beside the
numbers (the chevron alone at the small size and in the compact row), the truncation gap
is a quiet text ellipsis (…), and the rows-per-page trigger sits on the field edge. A resting page
or arrow takes the hover wash at once; a disabled pager dims as one, and in an enabled
pager the arrow at either end dims on its own.

In glass mode the current page is a brand-tinted control-layer puck behind its number;
the other pages and the hairline arrows paint no surface, so they stay bare. Beyond
seven pages a page change also shifts the window (an ellipsis moves, a number appears or
drops out). Solid mode keeps the accent fill.

components.name: PhoneInput
components.description: A phone number field: the Input's box with a country segment at its start (the chosen country and a caret, which open a list of countries with their names and dial codes) and that country's dial code inline before the number. On the web the segment is a small chip inside the field naming the country by its ISO code, and the dial code and the number are set in the mono face, and in the country list each row is a 16px flag 10px from the name with the dial code a 12px mono note at its end; on iOS and Android it is the country's flag.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: If true, focuses the input on componentDidMount. The default value is false.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Provides an initial value that will change when the user starts typing. Useful for simple use-cases where you don't want to deal with listening to events and updating the value prop to keep the controlled state in sync.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Limits the maximum number of characters that can be entered. Use this instead of implementing the logic in JS to avoid flicker.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input is blurred Note: If you are trying to find the last value of TextInput, you can use the `onEndEditing` event, which is fired upon completion of editing.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input is focused

props.name: onSubmitEditing
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's submit button is pressed.

props.name: onKeyPress
props.description: Callback that is called when a key is pressed. This will be called with `{ nativeEvent: { key: keyValue } }` where keyValue is 'Enter' or 'Backspace' for respective keys and the typed-in character otherwise including ' ' for space. Fires before onChange callbacks. Note: on Android only the inputs from soft keyboard are handled, not the hardware keyboard inputs.

props.name: returnKeyType
props.description: enum('default', 'go', 'google', 'join', 'next', 'route', 'search', 'send', 'yahoo', 'done', 'emergency-call') Determines how the return key should look.

props.name: testID
props.description: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests

props.name: value
props.description: The national number typed so far (controlled). Omit and use `defaultValue` for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onChangeText
props.description: Called with the new number on each keystroke.

props.name: countries
props.description: The countries the segment offers, in the order shown. Defaults to the kit's curated `PHONE_COUNTRIES` list; pass a full, localized, or reordered list.

props.name: country
props.description: The selected country's ISO alpha-2 code (controlled). Omit and use `defaultCountry`.

props.name: defaultCountry
props.description: Initial country code for uncontrolled use. Defaults to "US" when the list has it, else the first row.

props.name: onCountryChange
props.description: Called with the chosen country's code when a row is picked (both modes).

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder shown while the number is empty.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's persistent label, rendered above the box on every platform (a grouped field never floats its label). It is the number field's programmatic name, and Field delegates its label into it.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field as required: a destructive "*" after the label (decorative, never in the accessible name), and the number field announced as required, through aria-required on the web and with the word in its name ("Phone number, required") on iOS and Android.

props.name: invalid

platformNotes.web:
A phone number field: the Input's box with a country segment at its start (the
chosen country and a caret, which open a list of countries with their names and
dial codes) and that country's dial code inline before the number. On the web the
segment is a small chip inside the field naming the country by its ISO code, and
the dial code and the number are set in the mono face, and in the country list each
row is a 16px flag 10px from the name with the dial code a 12px mono note at its end;
on iOS and Android it is the
country's flag.

The number and the country are each controlled (`value` / `country`) or
self-managed (`defaultValue` / `defaultCountry`), the segment defaults to the
kit's curated `PHONE_COUNTRIES` list (pass `countries` for a full or localized
one), and the number field asks for the phone keypad. Pass `label` (and
`required`) to name it; `error` paints the whole box, segment included, and
Field delegates its label, required mark and error into it. The required star is
decorative: a screen reader hears the number field as required,
from
`aria-required` on the web and from its name ("Phone number, required") on iOS and
Android.
On iOS the field is
drawn to the iOS input-field reference: the white box, the flag and gray caret
segment with its state-coloured divider, the dial code in the placeholder gray.

In glass mode the country list is a dense-layer glass card under the box; the
box, its segment and its number stay in place. A pick commits the country and
returns focus to the number at once, and a field that becomes disabled or
read-only while the list is open closes it. Solid mode paints the skin's own list.

components.name: Popover
components.description: Floating panel with a title, supporting text, rich content such as form fields, and a single follow-up action, anchored to its trigger. Pass children to host custom content in the panel body, between the description and the action.

props.name: anchorRef
props.description: An existing trigger to anchor against; omits the built-in trigger and wrapper.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Explicit name for a panel with custom content.

props.name: compact
props.description: Compact web application panel with an outside hairline and scrolling content.

props.name: comfortable
props.description: Roomier compact-panel content inset.

props.name: anchored
props.description: Keep the card anchored on narrow windows instead of adapting to a sheet.

props.name: alignEnd
props.description: Align the trailing edge of the card to its trigger.

props.name: panelWidth
props.description: Floating card width, clamped inside the overlay outlet.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Maximum height of the floating card; its compact contents scroll within it.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Label for the trigger button.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading shown at the top of the floating card.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting line beneath the title.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom panel content (an input, a form row, any node), rendered in the card body between the description and the action row. Composes with the data-driven props.

props.name: actionLabel
props.description: When set, renders a primary action button at the bottom of the card.

props.name: top
props.description: Anchor the card ABOVE the trigger (it flips below when the room above is short). Placement axis: `top` > `bottom`.

props.name: bottom
props.description: Anchor the card BELOW the trigger, the default (it flips above when the room below is short).

props.name: inline
props.description: Static mode: render the card on its own with no trigger button (an always-visible inline panel). When set, the card is always shown and `open` is ignored. With `top` or `bottom` it points its beak at what it belongs to (below it with `top`, above it with `bottom`), from the end edge with `alignEnd`.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled (the trigger toggles it).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fired when the open state changes.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook.

platformNotes.web:
Floating panel with a title, supporting text, rich content such as form fields, and a single follow-up action, anchored to its trigger. Pass children to host custom content in the panel body, between the description and the action.

On the web and Android the panel is the v4 card:
280 wide at the menu corner, the field
hairline and the large shadow, a 15px display heading over its 14px description in the
muted ink, and in solid mode a small diamond beak on the edge facing its trigger.
iOS
keeps the iPad popover, a rounder borderless card with a tapered beak toward its
trigger.

The triggered card opens below its button by default and above it with `top`; either
way it flips to the other side when its own lacks room, and the beak follows the
side it took. At phone width a triggered card that can close is presented as a sheet
on the bottom edge of the window, over the tab bar and a dimming scrim that glass on the
web also blurs,
its content kept clear of the home indicator: Dark Factory's sheet on the web, the iOS sheet on iPhone and
the Material 3 bottom sheet on Android.

In glass mode the triggered card is a functional-layer glass panel beside its
button, and the sheet a dense-layer one, legible over its scrim; focus enters once the
card's placement has committed, and the `inline` card is a static in-flow panel. Solid
mode paints the skin's own panel.

An existing control can own the trigger: pass its `anchorRef` and drive `open`
with `onOpenChange`. The popover then adds no trigger or layout wrapper. Name
custom content with `accessibilityLabel`. `compact` uses the original Argus panel
inset and outside hairline on web, with scrolling contents; `comfortable` gives
its filter panel more room. `panelWidth` and `maxHeight` bound the overlay.
`anchored` keeps a floating card at narrow widths, and `alignEnd` follows the
trigger’s trailing edge.

components.name: Pressable
components.description: The touchable primitive: wraps content, fires `onPress`, and exposes the press state to its style for feedback.

props.name: hovered
props.description: Every kit control in the subtree renders as if a pointer hovered it.

props.name: focused
props.description: Every kit control in the subtree renders its keyboard focus (the focus ring, or the field's own focused look).

props.name: pressed
props.description: Every kit control in the subtree renders as if it were held down.

props.name: children
props.description: The subtree that resolves the pinned states.

platformNotes.web:
The touchable primitive: wraps content, fires `onPress`, and exposes the press state to its style for feedback.

The kit's interactive components (Button, plus the tappable Card, Stats, GridList, MediaObject, and StackedList rows) cover the common cases and keep branding consistent, so prefer them; Pressable stays for full flexibility when you need a custom interaction the kit doesn't provide. Its style prop accepts a function of the press state, `({ pressed }) => style`, so you can show press feedback with no extra wrapper; style it with tokens to stay on-brand.

Pass `focusable={false}` for a surface only a pointer should reach, such as a row whose keyboard path is a button inside it: it still presses, and it leaves the tab order on the web too, where react-native-web's own Pressable would keep it a tab stop. A Pressable with the `link` role presses on Enter (and not on Space), as a link does, on the web too: react-native-web's own Pressable leaves that key to the browser, which activates only a link that has an `href`.

components.name: Progress
components.description: Determinate and indeterminate progress bars: a rounded bar that reports how far a task has gotten, or that work is underway.

props.name: value
props.description: Completion as a 0..1 fraction (clamped). Ignored when `indeterminate`. Defaults to 0.

props.name: segments
props.description: A fixed number of discrete dashes, filled by the same fractional value.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Indeterminate mode: ignore `value` and animate a sliding bar (a spinner on iOS).

props.name: children
props.description: Optional title line rendered ABOVE the bar. Supplying it (with or without a `description`/`showValue`) builds the stacked header inside the control, so the caller never hand-composes a Row/Column + Typography around the bar. This is the "components own their label anatomy" contract, mirroring Checkbox/Radio/Switch's `description` slot.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional muted secondary line rendered under the title.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Render the percent (derived from `value`) as a right-aligned readout on the title line. Indeterminate has no measurable value, so this renders nothing then.

props.name: status
props.description: A short status word on the title line, in the percent readout's place and type ("indeterminate", "strong", "paused"): what the bar means right now, where `description` is a sentence under the title. It shows while indeterminate too, and when both are passed the status wins the readout slot over `showValue`.

props.name: warning
props.description: Tone axis (the active fill color; pick one, default is the call-to-action fill). `warning` paints the bar in the warning color, `danger` in the destructive color, for a metric over a soft threshold or a hard limit (a WIP meter over its cap); the track stays neutral. Pair with copy: the tone adds no accessible value.

props.name: danger
props.description: Tone axis (the active fill color; pick one, default is the call-to-action fill). `warning` paints the bar in the warning color, `danger` in the destructive color, for a metric over a soft threshold or a hard limit (a WIP meter over its cap); the track stays neutral. Pair with copy: the tone adds no accessible value.

platformNotes.web:
Determinate and indeterminate progress bars: a rounded bar that reports how far a task has gotten, or that work is underway.

The bar fills the parent it is given; a step of its own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with `start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a Container step sets its measure.

Name the task with string `children`, or pass `accessibilityLabel` when the visible title is omitted or contains rich content.

`segments` displays a fixed number of discrete 13×5 dashes with three pixels
between them. It uses the same 0–1 `value`, intent fill and accessible percentage.
Indeterminate wins over discrete segments; a labelled segmented meter retains its header.

components.name: ProgressRing
components.description: A full-circle completion ring, the Gauge's sibling: a muted track ring, a tone-colored value arc revealed clockwise from 12 o'clock with rounded caps, the whole-percent readout centered inside, and an optional label below the graphic. The same 0-100 value contract, tone axis, and rounding rules as Gauge, in the circular anatomy that reads as "completion" rather than "level".

props.description: The value to display, 0-100.

props.name: label
props.description: A short caption beneath the number (e.g. "Complete").

props.name: primary
props.description: Tone of the value arc (pick one; default primary). Precedence when several are passed: success > warning > destructive (first match wins).

props.name: success
props.description: Tone of the value arc (pick one; default primary). Precedence when several are passed: success > warning > destructive (first match wins).

props.description: Set the label under the ring, centred, instead of beside it (a row of rings, each named underneath).

components.name: QRCode
components.description: Encodes a string as a scannable QR code. Built on react-native-svg, so it renders the same on iOS, Android, and the web. The code stays a fixed dark-on-white card so any camera can read it, whatever the app theme.

props.description: The string to encode: a URL, plain text, a token, etc.

props.name: small
props.description: A compact 96px code.

props.name: large
props.description: A large 200px code.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Spoken equivalent for screen readers. A QR code is camera-only content, so without a label assistive tech announces nothing. Defaults to `QR code encoding ${value}`; pass a generic label (e.g. "QR code") when surfacing the raw value is undesirable.

components.name: RadialBarChart

props.name: label

props.description: Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats).
