components.name: Radio
components.description: Single-pick selection: stacked, inline, card-style.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected option's value (CONTROLLED). Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial selected value for uncontrolled use (a bare group selects on press).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fired with the newly selected option's value.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable every radio in the group.

props.name: row
props.description: Lay the options out in a wrapping row instead of the default column. iOS keeps its checkmark list vertical (a list has no row form); `card` options still sit in a row there.

props.name: equal
props.description: With `row`: the options share the row equally and never wrap, a tile picker's even columns (card tiles 10 apart, plain options 20).

props.name: inlineLabel
props.description: With `row` and a `label`: the label sits at the start of the row, before the options and centred on them, in the 500 13 px muted ink (a short setting's inline choice: "Digest ( ) Daily (o) Weekly"), instead of as a heading above. The `description` is not shown inline.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's name, rendered as a heading above the options. It also becomes the radiogroup's accessible name, so a screen reader announces what the set of options is about before reading them. The group owns this label anatomy; never hand-compose a heading Text beside a bare group.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional muted supporting line rendered under the label.

props.name: children
props.description: The `<Radio value="…">` options that make up the group.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the group container.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook.

props.name: value
props.description: This option's value within a RadioGroup. When the radio sits inside a `<RadioGroup>`, its checked state and selection are driven by the group matching this value; ignored for a standalone radio.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether this control is the selected option (controlled; standalone use).

props.name: selected
props.description: Alias for `checked`, for callers that think in terms of "selected".

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fired on press with the next checked value (always true for a radio). Web keyboard activation supports Space on release and Enter; RadioGroup also handles arrows.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the pressable row.

props.name: children
props.description: Label text (the option's title) shown beside the control.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional muted secondary line rendered under the label, for the common title-plus-description option (a plan picker, a settings choice). Supplying it builds the stacked title/description layout inside the control, so the caller never hand-composes a Row + Column + two Typography nodes per option.

props.name: card
props.description: Render the whole control as a selectable option CARD: the mark (the ring, or the trailing check on iOS) plus the title and description sit inside Card chrome (bordered, padded), and the ENTIRE card is the tap target. When this radio is the chosen option, the card takes Card's own `selected` treatment (a primary border and a soft primary tint), so the whole tile reads as chosen, not just the mark. Pairs with `description` for a plan/tier picker, and is still group-wired through `value` inside a `<RadioGroup>`.

props.name: meta
props.description: A trailing detail on the title's line (a version, a price, a status pill): a string is set in the small mono meta type in the subtle ink, a node (a `Badge`) as it is. The title takes the row, so in a full-width option the detail sits at its end; in a `row` group's hugging option it follows the title.

props.name: icon
props.description: A `card` tile's icon (a kit `Icon` with no tone of its own): the tile stacks the icon and the mark on one line above the title and description. The icon takes the accent text ink while the option is chosen and the subtle ink otherwise. Ignored without `card`.

props.name: small
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the 18px control on the web).

props.name: large
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the 18px control on the web).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dim the control and block presses.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the interactive radio row, preserving group navigation. Typed as a React Native View. On web, React Native Web exposes its DOM host; focus() and blur() move browser focus. Native host behavior depends on the platform and React Native version. Calling focus() does not activate the control or call accessibility focus APIs.

groups.title: Size
groups.note: Size (pick one; default is the 18px control on the web).

platformNotes.web:
Single-pick selection: stacked, inline, card-style.

One job, a platform's own control: iOS has no radio button, so there a single choice is a checkmark list, the inline picker of a grouped form. Each option's label leads and the chosen option carries a trailing check, and a RadioGroup's options form one inset-grouped section with a hairline between two rows. The web and Android keep the ring, and the role is `radio` on every platform: on the web an 18 px ring (16 `small`, 22 `large`) whose edge thickens in the accent around a hollow center when chosen, on Android Material 3's 20dp ring around an accent dot.
In glass mode the ring keeps its solid look on every platform: a ring is a small mark inside content, not a surface, so it draws with no pane and no rim. A `card` option is a content-layer pane, as a selectable Card is.
On iOS the list stays vertical when the group asks for a `row` (a list has no row form), and `card` options stay tiles that mark the choice with the same trailing check.

Pass `ref` to access the interactive radio row, preserving group navigation. Use `useRef<ComponentRef<typeof Radio>>(null)` from React, or `useRef<View>(null)` with React Native's `View` type. Object and callback refs are supported and detach on unmount. Calling `ref.current?.focus()` or `.blur()` delegates to the host without activating the control. Browser focus is supported; native focus depends on the platform and React Native version, and is separate from accessibility focus.

On the web, Space activates the focused control on key release, and Enter also activates it. Holding Space does not repeat the change. Moving focus away, disabling the control, or composing text cancels a pending Space press. RadioGroup arrow keys continue to move focus and selection.

components.name: Reveal
components.description: An entrance for page content: what it wraps starts slightly offset and transparent, then travels into place and fades in when it reaches the viewport. It fires once and stays, so content that has arrived never leaves again.

props.name: children
props.description: The Reveals to stagger. Each direct child receives the next ordinal in document order, so a mapped list arrives one item after another with no per-item props.

props.name: fromBelow
props.description: Rise into place from below. The default.

props.name: fromAbove
props.description: Descend into place from above.

props.name: fromLeft
props.description: Slide in from the left. Physical, and does not mirror under RTL (see above).

props.name: fromRight
props.description: Slide in from the right. Physical, and does not mirror under RTL (see above).

props.name: pronounced
props.description: Travel further before settling, for a hero or a section header. Omit for the default, shorter travel.

props.name: brisk
props.description: Arrive faster, for dense sets where the eye should not wait. Omit for the default duration.

props.name: deepInView
props.description: Wait until the element is properly inside the viewport before starting, instead of firing as it enters.

props.name: children
props.description: The content to reveal.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition ONLY: how this wrapper sits in its parent (a `minWidth` of 0 so a grid child may shrink below its content, a `height` of 100% so cards in a row stay even, a flex share). It is NOT a restyle hook: the entrance itself is chosen entirely with the boolean props above, and the revealed content styles itself. A wrapper that cannot be told how to sit in its parent forces callers to add a second wrapper around it, which is worse.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the wrapper.

groups.title: Direction
groups.note: Direction (pick one; the content travels FROM there to its resting place). Precedence when more than one is passed: fromBelow, fromAbove, fromLeft, fromRight. Pass none for the default, which is fromBelow.

platformNotes.web:
An entrance for page content: what it wraps starts slightly offset and transparent, then travels into place and fades in when it reaches the viewport. It fires once and stays, so content that has arrived never leaves again.

Direction chooses the axis it travels from, with `fromBelow` the default and `fromAbove`, `fromLeft`, `fromRight` the alternatives (that is also the precedence order if more than one is passed). `pronounced` travels further, `brisk` arrives faster, and `deepInView` holds the entrance until the element is properly inside the viewport instead of firing as it enters.

Stagger is structural rather than numeric: wrap a set in `RevealGroup` and each child arrives after the one before it, so no call site ever computes a delay. `RevealGroup` renders no box of its own, so it can sit between a grid and the items the grid lays out.

The trigger is measured against the window rather than the nearest scrolling parent, so content sitting inside a short inner scroller can arrive before that scroller has been scrolled to it; reveal on the page scroll, which is what this is for. Under Reduce Motion the content renders its final frame immediately, with no measuring and no timers, and the stagger is skipped along with the motion.

components.name: Row & Column
components.description: The layout primitives. `Row` lays children out horizontally, `Column` vertically. Both own arrangement through semantic boolean axes, a gap scale (`flush` / `tight` / `snug` / `cozy` / `relaxed` / `loose`), main-axis distribution (`center`, `between`, …), cross-axis alignment (`alignCenter`, `baseline`, …), and `wrap` / `fill` / `grow` / `shrink`, so a call site never hand-rolls `flexDirection`, `gap`, or `alignItems`.

props.name: rowsPanel
props.description: A wrapped or stacked row's vertical gap of 28, apart from its main gap: the hand-off's section hero (`gap:28px 40px`), whose halves sit 40 apart beside each other and 28 apart once stacked.

props.name: insetIdentity
props.description: Application identity header inset.

props.name: insetActions
props.description: Application action footer inset.

props.name: insetTheme
props.description: Theme controls inset.

props.name: insetStatus
props.description: Status band inset.

props.name: insetTabs
props.description: Navigation close controls inset.

props.name: apart
props.description: The step between side-by-side panels of one composition (32), the hand-off's widest grid gap.

props.name: ample
props.description: The step between a section page's hero and the body under it, and between the hero's halves (40): the hand-off's section pages (`gap:28px 40px` on the hero, `margin-bottom:40px` under it).

props.name: broad
props.description: The gap between the two halves of a page-wide split (48): the hand-off's hero grid.

props.name: chapter
props.description: The widest gap step (64): the space between a page's chapters, the major sections of a long docs page (a component detail page's Playground, Props and Examples), wider than `page` so each chapter reads as its own block. Wins over every other gap step.

props.description: Orthogonal modifiers (stack freely).

props.name: shrink
props.description: Let this box shrink below its own content width when the line runs out of room (`flexShrink: 1`), so a long text child wraps instead of overflowing. React Native gives every box `flexShrink: 0`, which is the opposite of the web's flex default: inside a Row, a Column holding a sentence keeps its MAX-CONTENT width and spills past the row's edge, where the nearest clipping ancestor cuts it mid-word. `shrink` is the opt-in that hands the row's width back to the text. Reach for it on the copy in a heading-beside-actions row, a label beside a control, any Row child whose width should follow the row rather than its own longest line. It is not `fill`. `fill` (flex: 1) also zeroes the flex BASIS, so in a `wrap` row every child then fits on one line and the actions stop wrapping below the copy; `shrink` leaves the basis at the content size, so the row still breaks where it did and only the over-wide child gives way. Redundant alongside `fill`, which already shrinks.

props.name: stacks
props.description: Responsive (Row only): render as a Column when the row's own CONTAINER is at or below `stackBreakpoint` (default `sm` = 640). Container-measured with a viewport seed for the first frame, so a Row inside a narrow desktop column stacks too, not just on phones. When stacked, the Row IS the Column with the same props: gap, justify, align, and padding apply to the new axes, the default `stretch` cross-axis makes children full width, and `wrap` is inert. Ignored (with a DEV warning) on Column: a Column that must become a Row is a Row that stacks.

props.name: stackBreakpoint
props.description: The breakpoint at and below which `stacks` flips to a column (default `"sm"`). Only meaningful with `stacks` (DEV warns without it).

props.name: span
props.description: Width in twelfths of the parent Row (Bootstrap `.col-n`): `span={6}` is half the row, `span={4}` a third, `span={12}` the full width. The Row measures its own width and gives this box a px cell, gaps included in the arithmetic, so two `span={6}` children plus the gap between them fill the row exactly. Spans over twelve wrap onto the next line. A Row with `stacks` ignores spans once it has stacked (every child is then full width). Only meaningful on a direct child of a Row (DEV warns elsewhere); in a Column, a width is a Container step. A child without a span, `fill`, or `grow` hugs its content (`.col-auto`): a fill component inside it collapses, so give it one of those.

props.name: weight
props.description: A share of the parent Row's free width, CSS grid's `minmax(0, Nfr)`: siblings with `weight={1.7}` and `weight={1}` split the row 1.7 to 1 after the gap, whatever their content, and neither holds a content floor. It is the split a ratio of twelfths cannot name (the Canvas v4 component page's anatomy is 1.7 to 1, where `span` gives 7 to 5). A positive number; it replaces `fill` and `grow` on the same box, and a box takes a `span` or a `weight`, not both. Only meaningful on a direct child of a Row (DEV warns elsewhere); once a `stacks` Row has stacked, the box is the whole line and the weight is ignored.

props.name: indent
props.description: Indent the whole stack by one control gutter (24: a control box plus the row gap), so a nested option group lines up under its parent control's label instead of its box. For nesting checkboxes/radios under a "select all" parent.

props.name: padTight
props.description: Padding scale (pick one; omit for none).

props.name: pad
props.description: Padding scale (pick one; omit for none).

props.name: padLoose
props.description: Padding scale (pick one; omit for none).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Layout containers are the exception to the no-sizing rule: for sizing and composition only (a `maxWidth` on a shell, a `flex` inside an app frame), never for styling or spacing. Gap, margin, padding, and flex layout come from the props above, and the codegen guardrail rejects those keys in `style`. Prefer a Container step or a `span` where one fits.

platformNotes.web:
The layout primitives. `Row` lays children out horizontally, `Column`
vertically. Both own arrangement through semantic boolean axes, a gap scale
(`flush` / `tight` / `snug` / `cozy` / `relaxed` / `loose`), main-axis
distribution (`center`, `between`, …), cross-axis alignment (`alignCenter`,
`baseline`, …), and `wrap` / `fill` / `grow` / `shrink`, so a call site never
hand-rolls `flexDirection`, `gap`, or `alignItems`.

The Argus reference adds intermediate spacing steps without rounding its layout:
`fine` 3, `dense` 5, `compact` 6, `close` 7, `nested` 9, `comfortable` 10,
`balanced` 11, `roomy` 14, `airy` 18, `spacious` 20, `generous` 22,
`section` 26, `panel` 28, `page` 30, `apart` 32 (the space between the side-by-side
panels of one composition), `ample` 40 (between a section page's hero and the body under
it, and between the hero's halves) and `broad` 48 (between the two halves of a page-wide split). Existing named steps keep their values.
Larger active steps take precedence.

`ample` (40) is the step between a section page's hero and the body under it, and between
the hero's halves (the Canvas v4 section pages). `chapter` (64) is the widest step: the
space between a page's chapters, the major sections of a long page (a component detail
page's Playground, Props and Examples). It wins over every other gap step, so the
precedence runs `chapter` > `broad` > `ample` > `apart` > `page` > `panel` > `section` >
`loose` and on down the scale to `flush`. Row, Column and Grid all take them.

`rowsTight`, `rowsComfortable`, `rowsSnug`, `rowsCozy`, `rowsSection` and `rowsPanel` set a
wrapped or stacked row's vertical gap to 4, 10, 8, 12, 26 and 28 independently of its main
gap (a stacked `Row stacks` lays its children down that vertical gap, so a hero whose
halves sit 40 apart beside each other and 28 apart stacked is `ample rowsPanel`). Application inset
roles preserve identity headers (24 top/horizontal, 18 bottom), action footers
(16 vertical, 24 horizontal), theme controls (14 top, 26 horizontal), status bands
(10 vertical, 28 horizontal), and navigation close controls (12 top/horizontal):
`insetIdentity`, `insetActions`, `insetTheme`, `insetStatus`, and `insetTabs`.

components.name: RowMenu
components.description: Vertical action menu items and navigation links.

props.name: items
props.description: The menu rows, top to bottom.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled (the trigger toggles it).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fired when the open state changes.

props.name: links
props.description: Render rows as navigation links rather than action buttons.

props.name: inline
props.description: The menu drawn in place, with no ⋯ trigger and no overlay: the action rows in the menu's own panel, filling the width the parent gives it. With `links` it is a grouped link list instead: hairline-split rows, each ending in its `badge` or `meta` and a chevron. `open`, `onOpenChange` and `triggerLabel` do nothing here.

props.name: sectionLabel
props.description: Show a muted section label heading the menu.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fired with the selected item and its index when a row is pressed.

props.name: triggerLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the icon-only ⋯ trigger. Defaults to "More options".

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

platformNotes.web:
Vertical action menu items and navigation links.

On the web the ··· trigger is a 32px square on the field hairline, washed while its
menu is open or under the pointer, and it opens a card menu 220 wide: rows 34 tall
with a muted leading glyph beside the label, and a destructive row in red.
iOS and
Android keep their platform context menus in the theme's colours.

In glass mode the menu is a dense-layer glass card beside its glyph; a row's
callback fires the moment it is pressed. Solid mode paints the skin's own menu.
Board's card menus are RowMenus and behave the same.

components.name: ScrollView
components.description: A scrollable container for content larger than its bounds: vertical by default, `horizontal` for a row.

props.name: contentContainerStyle
props.description: These styles will be applied to the scroll view content container which wraps all of the child views. Example: return ( <ScrollView contentContainerStyle={styles.contentContainer}> </ScrollView> ); ... const styles = StyleSheet.create({ contentContainer: { paddingVertical: 20 } });

props.name: innerViewRef
props.description: A ref to the inner View element of the ScrollView. This should be used instead of calling `getInnerViewRef`.

props.name: scrollViewRef
props.description: A ref to the Native ScrollView component. This ref can be used to call all of ScrollView's public methods, in addition to native methods like measure, measureLayout, etc.

props.name: decelerationRate
props.description: A floating-point number that determines how quickly the scroll view decelerates after the user lifts their finger. You may also use string shortcuts `"normal"` and `"fast"` which match the underlying iOS settings for `UIScrollViewDecelerationRateNormal` and `UIScrollViewDecelerationRateFast` respectively. - `'normal'`: 0.998 on iOS, 0.985 on Android (the default) - `'fast'`: 0.99 on iOS, 0.9 on Android

props.name: horizontal
props.description: When true the scroll view's children are arranged horizontally in a row instead of vertically in a column. The default value is false.

props.name: invertStickyHeaders
props.description: If sticky headers should stick at the bottom instead of the top of the ScrollView. This is usually used with inverted ScrollViews.

props.name: keyboardDismissMode
props.description: Determines whether the keyboard gets dismissed in response to a drag. - 'none' (the default) drags do not dismiss the keyboard. - 'onDrag' the keyboard is dismissed when a drag begins. - 'interactive' the keyboard is dismissed interactively with the drag and moves in synchrony with the touch; dragging upwards cancels the dismissal.

props.name: keyboardShouldPersistTaps
props.description: Determines when the keyboard should stay visible after a tap. - 'never' (the default), tapping outside of the focused text input when the keyboard is up dismisses the keyboard. When this happens, children won't receive the tap. - 'always', the keyboard will not dismiss automatically, and the scroll view will not catch taps, but children of the scroll view can catch taps. - 'handled', the keyboard will not dismiss automatically when the tap was handled by a children, (or captured by an ancestor). - false, deprecated, use 'never' instead - true, deprecated, use 'always' instead

props.name: onContentSizeChange
props.description: Called when scrollable content view of the ScrollView changes. Handler function is passed the content width and content height as parameters: (contentWidth, contentHeight) It's implemented using onLayout handler attached to the content container which this ScrollView renders.

props.name: onScroll
props.description: Fires at most once per frame during scrolling.

props.name: onScrollBeginDrag
props.description: Fires if a user initiates a scroll gesture.

props.name: onScrollEndDrag
props.description: Fires when a user has finished scrolling.

props.name: onMomentumScrollEnd
props.description: Fires when scroll view has finished moving

props.name: onMomentumScrollBegin
props.description: Fires when scroll view has begun moving

props.name: pagingEnabled
props.description: When true the scroll view stops on multiples of the scroll view's size when scrolling. This can be used for horizontal pagination. The default value is false.

props.name: scrollEnabled
props.description: When false, the content does not scroll. The default value is true

props.name: removeClippedSubviews
props.description: Experimental: When true offscreen child views (whose `overflow` value is `hidden`) are removed from their native backing superview when offscreen. This can improve scrolling performance on long lists. The default value is false.

props.name: showsHorizontalScrollIndicator
props.description: When true, shows a horizontal scroll indicator.

props.name: showsVerticalScrollIndicator
props.description: When true, shows a vertical scroll indicator.

props.name: stickyHeaderHiddenOnScroll
props.description: When true, Sticky header is hidden when scrolling down, and dock at the top when scrolling up.

props.name: style
props.description: Style

props.name: refreshControl
props.description: A RefreshControl component, used to provide pull-to-refresh functionality for the ScrollView.

props.name: snapToInterval
props.description: When set, causes the scroll view to stop at multiples of the value of `snapToInterval`. This can be used for paginating through children that have lengths smaller than the scroll view. Used in combination with `snapToAlignment` and `decelerationRate="fast"`. Overrides less configurable `pagingEnabled` prop.

props.name: snapToOffsets
props.description: When set, causes the scroll view to stop at the defined offsets. This can be used for paginating through variously sized children that have lengths smaller than the scroll view. Typically used in combination with `decelerationRate="fast"`. Overrides less configurable `pagingEnabled` and `snapToInterval` props.

props.name: snapToStart
props.description: Use in conjunction with `snapToOffsets`. By default, the beginning of the list counts as a snap offset. Set `snapToStart` to false to disable this behavior and allow the list to scroll freely between its start and the first `snapToOffsets` offset. The default value is true.

props.name: snapToEnd
props.description: Use in conjunction with `snapToOffsets`. By default, the end of the list counts as a snap offset. Set `snapToEnd` to false to disable this behavior and allow the list to scroll freely between its end and the last `snapToOffsets` offset. The default value is true.

props.name: stickyHeaderIndices
props.description: An array of child indices determining which children get docked to the top of the screen when scrolling. For example passing `stickyHeaderIndices={[0]}` will cause the first child to be fixed to the top of the scroll view. This property is not supported in conjunction with `horizontal={true}`.

props.name: disableIntervalMomentum
props.description: When true, the scroll view stops on the next index (in relation to scroll position at release) regardless of how fast the gesture is. This can be used for horizontal pagination when the page is less than the width of the ScrollView. The default value is false.

props.name: disableScrollViewPanResponder
props.description: When true, the default JS pan responder on the ScrollView is disabled, and full control over touches inside the ScrollView is left to its child components. This is particularly useful if `snapToInterval` is enabled, since it does not follow typical touch patterns. Do not use this on regular ScrollView use cases without `snapToInterval` as it may cause unexpected touches to occur while scrolling. The default value is false.

props.name: StickyHeaderComponent
props.description: A React Component that will be used to render sticky headers, should be used together with stickyHeaderIndices. You may need to set this component if your sticky header uses custom transforms, for example, when you want your list to have an animated and hidable header. If component have not been provided, the default ScrollViewStickyHeader component will be used.

props.name: hitSlop
props.description: This defines how far a touch event can start away from the view. Typical interface guidelines recommend touch targets that are at least 30 - 40 points/density-independent pixels. If a Touchable view has a height of 20 the touchable height can be extended to 40 with hitSlop={{top: 10, bottom: 10, left: 0, right: 0}} NOTE The touch area never extends past the parent view bounds and the Z-index of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch hits two overlapping views.

props.name: id
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing
props.description: Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior. The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value. This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background). Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default. If you do need to enable this property for an animation, consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame). If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once, saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU.

props.name: onLayout
props.description: Invoked on mount and layout changes with {nativeEvent: { layout: {x, y, width, height}}}.

props.name: pointerEvents
props.description: In the absence of auto property, none is much like CSS's none value. box-none is as if you had applied the CSS class: .box-none { pointer-events: none; } .box-none * { pointer-events: all; } box-only is the equivalent of .box-only { pointer-events: all; } .box-only * { pointer-events: none; } But since pointerEvents does not affect layout/appearance, and we are already deviating from the spec by adding additional modes, we opt to not include pointerEvents on style. On some platforms, we would need to implement it as a className anyways. Using style or not is an implementation detail of the platform.

props.name: testID
props.description: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.

props.name: nativeID
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: collapsable
props.description: Views that are only used to layout their children or otherwise don't draw anything may be automatically removed from the native hierarchy as an optimization. Set this property to false to disable this optimization and ensure that this View exists in the native view hierarchy.

props.name: collapsableChildren
props.description: Setting to false prevents direct children of the view from being removed from the native view hierarchy, similar to the effect of setting `collapsable={false}` on each child.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback that is called when the view is blurred. Note: This will only be called if the view is focusable.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback that is called when the view is focused. Note: This will only be called if the view is focusable.

props.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
props.description: Whether this view should render itself (and all of its children) into a single hardware texture on the GPU. On Android, this is useful for animations and interactions that only modify opacity, rotation, translation, and/or scale: in those cases, the view doesn't have to be redrawn and display lists don't need to be re-executed. The texture can just be re-used and re-composited with different parameters. The downside is that this can use up limited video memory, so this prop should be set back to false at the end of the interaction/animation.

props.name: focusable
props.description: Whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description: Indicates whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/tabindex for more details. Supports the following values: - 0 (View is focusable) - -1 (View is not focusable)

props.name: shouldRasterizeIOS
props.description: Whether this view should be rendered as a bitmap before compositing. On iOS, this is useful for animations and interactions that do not modify this component's dimensions nor its children; for example, when translating the position of a static view, rasterization allows the renderer to reuse a cached bitmap of a static view and quickly composite it during each frame. Rasterization incurs an off-screen drawing pass and the bitmap consumes memory. Test and measure when using this property.

props.name: isTVSelectable
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* When set to true, this view will be focusable and navigable using the Apple TV remote.

props.name: hasTVPreferredFocus
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be set to true to force the Apple TV focus engine to move focus to this view.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceX
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceY
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxTiltAngle
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 0.05.

props.name: tvParallaxMagnification
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 1.0.

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponder
props.description: Does this view want to become responder on the start of a touch?

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponder
props.description: Called for every touch move on the View when it is not the responder: does this view want to "claim" touch responsiveness?

props.name: onResponderEnd
props.description: If the View returns true and attempts to become the responder, one of the following will happen:

props.name: onResponderGrant
props.description: The View is now responding for touch events. This is the time to highlight and show the user what is happening

props.name: onResponderReject
props.description: Something else is the responder right now and will not release it

props.name: onResponderMove
props.description: The user is moving their finger

props.name: onResponderRelease
props.description: Fired at the end of the touch, ie "touchUp"

props.name: onResponderTerminationRequest
props.description: Something else wants to become responder. Should this view release the responder? Returning true allows release

props.name: onResponderTerminate
props.description: The responder has been taken from the View. Might be taken by other views after a call to onResponderTerminationRequest, or might be taken by the OS without asking (happens with control center/ notification center on iOS)

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description: onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern, where the deepest node is called first. That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers. This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable. However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder. This can be handled by using the capture phase. Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component, it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture. So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start, it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description: onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern, where the deepest node is called first. That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers. This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable. However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder. This can be handled by using the capture phase. Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component, it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture. So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start, it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: accessible
props.description: When true, indicates that the view is an accessibility element. By default, all the touchable elements are accessible.

props.name: accessibilityActions
props.type: readonly Readonly<{ name: AccessibilityActionName | string; label?: string | undefined; }>[] | undefined
props.description: Provides an array of custom actions available for accessibility.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Overrides the text that's read by the screen reader when the user interacts with the element. By default, the label is constructed by traversing all the children and accumulating all the Text nodes separated by space.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Alias for accessibilityLabel https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#accessibilitylabel https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34424

props.name: accessibilityRole
props.description: Accessibility Role tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the type of element that is focused on.

props.name: accessibilityState
props.description: Accessibility State tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the state of the element currently focused on.

props.name: aria-busy
props.description: alias for accessibilityState see https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitystate

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: An accessibility hint helps users understand what will happen when they perform an action on the accessibility element when that result is not obvious from the accessibility label.

props.name: accessibilityValue
props.description: Represents the current value of a component. It can be a textual description of a component's value, or for range-based components, such as sliders and progress bars, it contains range information (minimum, current, and maximum).

props.name: onAccessibilityAction
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs an accessibility custom action.

props.name: importantForAccessibility
props.description: [Android] Controlling if a view fires accessibility events and if it is reported to accessibility services.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description: A value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within this accessibility element are hidden.

props.name: role
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services to treat UI component like a specific role.

props.name: accessibilityLabelledBy
props.description: Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props, the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props, the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: accessibilityLiveRegion
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: aria-live
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: screenReaderFocusable
props.description: Enables the view to be screen reader focusable, not keyboard focusable.

props.name: accessibilityElementsHidden
props.description: A Boolean value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within this accessibility element are hidden to the screen reader.

props.name: accessibilityViewIsModal
props.description: A Boolean value indicating whether VoiceOver should ignore the elements within views that are siblings of the receiver.

props.name: onAccessibilityEscape
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the escape gesture (scrub with two fingers).

props.name: onAccessibilityTap
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs accessibility tap gesture.

props.name: onMagicTap
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the magic tap gesture.

props.name: accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors
props.description: https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityignoresinvertcolorsios

props.name: accessibilityLanguage
props.description: By using the accessibilityLanguage property, the screen reader will understand which language to use while reading the element's label, value and hint. The provided string value must follow the BCP 47 specification (https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47). https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylanguage-ios

props.name: accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer
props.description: A Boolean value that indicates whether or not to show the item in the large content viewer. Available on iOS 13.0+ https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityshowslargecontentviewer

props.name: accessibilityLargeContentTitle
props.description: When `accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer` is set, this string will be used as title for the large content viewer. https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylargecontenttitle

props.name: accessibilityRespondsToUserInteraction
props.description: Blocks the user from interacting with the component through keyboard while still allowing screen reader to interact with it if this View is still accessible.

props.name: alwaysBounceHorizontal
props.description: When true the scroll view bounces horizontally when it reaches the end even if the content is smaller than the scroll view itself. The default value is true when `horizontal={true}` and false otherwise.

props.name: alwaysBounceVertical
props.description: When true the scroll view bounces vertically when it reaches the end even if the content is smaller than the scroll view itself. The default value is false when `horizontal={true}` and true otherwise.

props.name: automaticallyAdjustContentInsets
props.description: Controls whether iOS should automatically adjust the content inset for scroll views that are placed behind a navigation bar or tab bar/ toolbar. The default value is true.

props.name: automaticallyAdjustKeyboardInsets
props.description: Controls whether the ScrollView should automatically adjust its contentInset and scrollViewInsets when the Keyboard changes its size. The default value is false.

props.name: automaticallyAdjustsScrollIndicatorInsets
props.description: Controls whether iOS should automatically adjust the scroll indicator insets. The default value is true. Available on iOS 13 and later.

props.name: bounces
props.description: When true the scroll view bounces when it reaches the end of the content if the content is larger than the scroll view along the axis of the scroll direction. When false it disables all bouncing even if the `alwaysBounce*` props are true. The default value is true.

props.name: bouncesZoom
props.description: When true gestures can drive zoom past min/max and the zoom will animate to the min/max value at gesture end otherwise the zoom will not exceed the limits.

props.name: canCancelContentTouches
props.description: When false once tracking starts won't try to drag if the touch moves. The default value is true.

props.name: centerContent
props.description: When true the scroll view automatically centers the content when the content is smaller than the scroll view bounds; when the content is larger than the scroll view this property has no effect. The default value is false.

props.name: contentInset
props.description: The amount by which the scroll view content is inset from the edges of the scroll view. Defaults to {0, 0, 0, 0}.

props.name: contentOffset
props.description: Used to manually set the starting scroll offset. The default value is {x: 0, y: 0}

props.name: contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior
props.description: This property specifies how the safe area insets are used to modify the content area of the scroll view. The default value of this property is "never".

props.name: directionalLockEnabled
props.description: When true the ScrollView will try to lock to only vertical or horizontal scrolling while dragging. The default value is false.

props.name: indicatorStyle
props.description: The style of the scroll indicators. - default (the default), same as black. - black, scroll indicator is black. This style is good against a white content background. - white, scroll indicator is white. This style is good against a black content background.

props.name: maintainVisibleContentPosition
props.type: { autoscrollToTopThreshold?: number | null | undefined; minIndexForVisible: number; } | null | undefined
props.description: When set, the scroll view will adjust the scroll position so that the first child that is currently visible and at or beyond minIndexForVisible will not change position. This is useful for lists that are loading content in both directions, e.g. a chat thread, where new messages coming in might otherwise cause the scroll position to jump. A value of 0 is common, but other values such as 1 can be used to skip loading spinners or other content that should not maintain position. The optional autoscrollToTopThreshold can be used to make the content automatically scroll to the top after making the adjustment if the user was within the threshold of the top before the adjustment was made. This is also useful for chat-like applications where you want to see new messages scroll into place, but not if the user has scrolled up a ways and it would be disruptive to scroll a bunch. Caveat 1: Reordering elements in the scrollview with this enabled will probably cause jumpiness and jank. It can be fixed, but there are currently no plans to do so. For now, don't re-order the content of any ScrollViews or Lists that use this feature. Caveat 2: This uses contentOffset and frame.origin in native code to compute visibility. Occlusion, transforms, and other complexity won't be taken into account as to whether content is "visible" or not.

props.name: maximumZoomScale
props.description: The maximum allowed zoom scale. The default value is 1.0.

props.name: minimumZoomScale
props.description: The minimum allowed zoom scale. The default value is 1.0.

props.name: onScrollAnimationEnd
props.description: Called when a scrolling animation ends.

props.name: pinchGestureEnabled
props.description: When true, ScrollView allows use of pinch gestures to zoom in and out. The default value is true.

props.name: scrollEventThrottle
props.description: Limits how often scroll events will be fired while scrolling, specified as a time interval in ms. This may be useful when expensive work is performed in response to scrolling. Values <= `16` will disable throttling, regardless of the refresh rate of the device.

props.name: scrollIndicatorInsets
props.description: The amount by which the scroll view indicators are inset from the edges of the scroll view. This should normally be set to the same value as the contentInset. Defaults to {0, 0, 0, 0}.

props.name: scrollToOverflowEnabled
props.description: When true, the scroll view can be programmatically scrolled beyond its content size. The default value is false.

props.name: scrollsToTop
props.description: When true the scroll view scrolls to top when the status bar is tapped. The default value is true.

props.name: snapToAlignment
props.description: When `snapToInterval` is set, `snapToAlignment` will define the relationship of the snapping to the scroll view. - `start` (the default) will align the snap at the left (horizontal) or top (vertical) - `center` will align the snap in the center - `end` will align the snap at the right (horizontal) or bottom (vertical)

props.name: onScrollToTop
props.description: Fires when the scroll view scrolls to top after the status bar has been tapped

props.name: zoomScale
props.description: The current scale of the scroll view content. The default value is 1.0.

props.name: endFillColor
props.description: Sometimes a scrollview takes up more space than its content fills. When this is the case, this prop will fill the rest of the scrollview with a color to avoid setting a background and creating unnecessary overdraw. This is an advanced optimization that is not needed in the general case.

props.name: scrollPerfTag
props.description: Tag used to log scroll performance on this scroll view. Will force momentum events to be turned on (see sendMomentumEvents). This doesn't do anything out of the box and you need to implement a custom native FpsListener for it to be useful.

props.name: overScrollMode
props.description: Used to override default value of overScroll mode. Possible values: - 'auto' - Default value, allow a user to over-scroll this view only if the content is large enough to meaningfully scroll. - 'always' - Always allow a user to over-scroll this view. - 'never' - Never allow a user to over-scroll this view.

props.name: nestedScrollEnabled
props.description: Enables nested scrolling for Android API level 21+. Nested scrolling is supported by default on iOS.

props.name: fadingEdgeLength
props.type: number | { start: number; end: number; } | undefined
props.description: Controls the fading effect at the edges of the scroll content. A value greater than 0 will apply the fading effect, indicating more content is available to scroll. You can specify a single number to apply the same fading length to both edges. Alternatively, use an object with `start` and `end` properties to set different fading lengths for the start and end of the scroll content. The default value is 0.

props.name: persistentScrollbar
props.description: Causes the scrollbars not to turn transparent when they are not in use. The default value is false.

props.name: scrollsChildToFocus
props.description: When false, the ScrollView will not automatically scroll to a focused child when the child requests focus. This can be useful when you want to control the scroll position programmatically. The default value is true.

props.name: ref
props.description: Allows getting a ref to the component instance. Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null` (or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).

platformNotes.web:
A scrollable container for content larger than its bounds: vertical by default, `horizontal` for a row.

Unlike a plain View, a ScrollView lets its children exceed its size and scroll. Style the frame with `style` and the inner content with `contentContainerStyle`. In Chromium and Firefox a scroller with nothing focusable inside it is a keyboard stop of its own, so arrow keys can scroll it; the browser draws its focus ring in the theme's `ring` colour, 2 px off the frame, like every kit control.

components.name: Select
components.description: A single-choice dropdown field: a trigger showing the chosen value that opens a panel of options, styled to match Canvas inputs.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selection; omit for uncontrolled use. Empty shows the placeholder. With plain string options this is the option itself; with `SelectOption` objects it is the option's `value`, and the trigger shows its `label`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial selection for uncontrolled use (a bare <Select options/> picks on its own).

props.name: options
props.description: The selectable options: bare strings, or `{ value, label }` objects when the stored value differs from the text shown for it.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's persistent label. Its placement is platform-adaptive: iOS and web render it ABOVE the trigger; Android renders the Material 3 in-container FLOATING label (centered like a placeholder at rest, floating to the top once the menu opens or a value is selected). The label names the field for a11y.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible purpose for the trigger and option list. Overrides the visible label for assistive technology; otherwise the label or placeholder names them.

props.name: inline
props.description: Places the `label` as a LEADING cluster INSIDE the trigger row (a toolbar-style labeled select) instead of the persistent above/floating placement. Takes effect only alongside `label`. The inline label still names the trigger (accessibilityLabel / aria-labelledby) and shares its tap target, since it lives inside the trigger Pressable. Pairs with `fit` for a content-hugging toolbar cluster.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field as required and announces "required" with the trigger name. A visible label also gets a decorative destructive "*".

props.name: icon
props.description: Renders a leading globe glyph inside the trigger, indented so the value clears it.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Prompt shown in the trigger when no value is selected.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state of the option list; omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fired when the open state changes (trigger press, select), in both modes.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the control and blocks interaction.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the chosen option's value when a row is pressed (both modes).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the trigger pressable.

props.name: dense
props.description: Use the compact content-sized web field with a drawn disclosure chevron.

props.name: eyebrow
props.description: Use the compact application eyebrow above a web field.

props.name: soft
props.description: Use the brand field fill instead of the card fill.

props.name: plainOptions
props.description: Text-only options: selected ink and a pointer wash, without a check gutter.

props.name: steadyPress
props.description: Keep the resting fill and opacity during a press.

props.name: combobox
props.description: Announce a selection field as a combobox rather than a menu button.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Width of the floating menu, clamped within the overlay outlet.

props.name: small
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the medium field, matching Input's h-9).

props.name: large
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the medium field, matching Input's h-9).

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the interactive trigger, preserving overlay measurement. Typed as a React Native View. On web, React Native Web exposes its DOM host; focus() and blur() move browser focus. Native host behavior depends on the platform and React Native version. Calling focus() does not activate the control or call accessibility focus APIs.

platformNotes.web:
A single-choice dropdown field: a trigger showing the chosen value that opens a
panel of options, styled to match Canvas inputs.

Pass `label` (and `required`) to name the field:
iOS and web render the label
above the trigger, while Android floats the Material 3 in-container label once
the menu opens or a value is selected. On Android the trigger grows with the
user's text size, and a label longer than the trigger truncates on one line clear
of the chevron while the trigger's accessible name stays the whole label.
The trigger fills the parent it is given;
a step of its own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with `start` to pin it to the leading edge) or
a Container step sets its measure.

In glass mode the option panel is a dense-layer glass card under the trigger (or
above it when it fits there); the trigger stays in place with its value and
chevron, and the chosen value and expanded state commit immediately. Solid mode
paints the skin's own panel.

The label also names the option list. Use `accessibilityLabel` to provide an explicit purpose when the visible label or placeholder is insufficient; it overrides both accessible names. A required field announces "required" with the button name and marks the option list as required. The selected value never replaces the field's purpose.

Pass `ref` to access the interactive trigger, preserving overlay measurement. Use `useRef<ComponentRef<typeof Select>>(null)` from React, or `useRef<View>(null)` with React Native's `View` type. Object and callback refs are supported and detach on unmount. Calling `ref.current?.focus()` or `.blur()` delegates to the host without activating the control. Browser focus is supported; native focus depends on the platform and React Native version, and is separate from accessibility focus.

On web, the trigger is the Canvas v4 field: 40 pixels tall (32 small, 48 large)
on the sunken fill behind the `field-border` hairline, a 400 14-pixel value (13
small) and a 16-pixel chevron that turns over while the list is open. The pointer
darkens the edge to the subtle ink, and keyboard focus or the open list rings it in
the accent with a 4-pixel halo. The list is a card 6 pixels under the trigger with
a 4-pixel inset, 34-pixel rows, the chosen row on the `muted` wash with a trailing
check in the accent ink.
iOS keeps the pop-up button (a 44-point field with the
up-and-down chevrons) and its menu, which marks the chosen row with a leading check;
Android keeps the Material 3 exposed dropdown, whose menu marks the chosen row with
its state layer alone.

Use `dense eyebrow soft` for the compact application field on web: a 32-pixel
trigger with a 600 13-pixel value under a tracked uppercase eyebrow label at the
kit’s 10-pixel reading floor, and 30-pixel rows. `plainOptions` removes the check
and marks the chosen row with its wash alone; pointer hover uses the brand wash. `steadyPress` keeps the resting fill and
opacity while pressed. `menuWidth` bounds the floating menu independently of the
field. `combobox` exposes the selection-field role. Native skins keep their
platform field anatomy and minimum touch targets.

the accent with a 4-pixel halo. The list is a card 6 pixels under the trigger with
a 4-pixel inset, 34-pixel rows, the chosen row on the `muted` wash with a trailing
check in the accent ink.
Android keeps the Material 3 exposed dropdown, whose menu marks the chosen row with its state layer alone.

Use `dense eyebrow soft` for the compact application field on web: a 32-pixel
trigger with a 600 13-pixel value under a tracked uppercase eyebrow label at the
kit’s 10-pixel reading floor, and 30-pixel rows. `plainOptions` removes the check
and marks the chosen row with its wash alone; pointer hover uses the brand wash. `steadyPress` keeps the resting fill and
opacity while pressed. `menuWidth` bounds the floating menu independently of the

components.name: Sidebar
components.description: App navigation rail with collapsible sections and active highlighting. The sidebar on the left of this page is a thin adapter over this very `Sidebar` component: it feeds the docs' nav tree in and gets the same collapse, accordion, and active-highlight behavior back.

props.name: sections
props.description: Titled sections of nav rows. Use this or the flat `items` array.

props.name: items
props.description: Flat list of nav rows, wrapped into a single untitled section.

props.name: active
props.description: The active row (CONTROLLED), by id, by label, or by flat index across all rows. Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultActive
props.description: Initial active row for uncontrolled use (a bare sidebar moves the highlight on press).

props.name: onSelect
props.type: ((item: SidebarItem, index: number, event: GestureResponderEvent) => void) | undefined
props.description: Fired with the selected row and its flat index across all sections.

props.name: compact
props.description: Density (pick one; default is the comfortable row).

props.name: bordered
props.description: A rounded card inside the field hairline.

props.name: floating
props.description: A rounded card lifted on the medium shadow (the bordered card natively).

props.name: embedded
props.description: Navigation groups embedded in an app-owned rail: no frame, fill or width of its own and no scroll body (the host rail scrolls); the `header` and `footer` slots stack above and below the groups as plain blocks.

props.name: markers
props.description: Trailing marker dots: the accent on the active row, the field hairline on a row of the current place (an item's `marked`, or every row of a `current` section).

props.name: collapsed
props.description: Collapsed to the mini icon-rail (CONTROLLED). Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultCollapsed
props.description: Initial collapsed state for uncontrolled use (default expanded).

props.name: collapsible
props.description: Show the collapse/expand toggle in the header slot.

props.name: onToggleCollapse
props.description: Fired when the user taps the collapse/expand toggle.

props.name: openSections
props.description: Open collapsible sections (CONTROLLED), by section id/title. A single key by default, an array when `independentSections`. Pair with `onOpenSectionsChange`.

props.name: defaultOpenSections
props.description: Initial open sections for uncontrolled use.

props.name: onOpenSectionsChange
props.description: Fired with the next open sections whenever a section header toggles.

props.name: independentSections
props.description: Allow more than one collapsible section open at once (default: one-open-at-a-time).

props.name: responsive
props.description: Opt in to the responsive rail->drawer behavior. Off by default: a bare sidebar is the inline rail at every width, byte-identical to before.

props.name: drawer
props.description: Always the drill-down drawer, at every width, never the inline rail: for an app shell whose only entry to the site tree is its own hamburger (a top app bar). Takes the same `open` / `onOpenChange` wiring as `responsive`, and wins over it.

props.name: open
props.description: The narrow drawer's open state (CONTROLLED). The consumer wires its hamburger to this.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state for the uncontrolled narrow drawer (default closed).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fired when the narrow drawer opens or closes (scrim tap, back, or a leaf selection).

props.name: drawerBreakpoint
props.description: The width at and below which `responsive` switches to the drawer (default `lg` = 1024).

props.name: drawerWidth
props.description: The narrow drawer panel width in px (default 288).

props.name: drawerContentInsetBottom
props.description: Extra bottom padding for the drawer's scrolling content, so its last rows clear persistent chrome painting over the drawer (e.g. a native bottom tab bar on Android).

props.name: drawerRight
props.description: Slide the drawer in from the end (right) edge instead of the start (left).

props.name: drawerTop
props.description: Drop the drawer down from the top edge (a top sheet).

props.name: drawerBottom
props.description: Raise the drawer up from the bottom edge (a bottom sheet).

props.name: header
props.description: Optional top slot (a brand lockup / logo). A render function receives the collapsed state so it can show a compact mark in the rail. When `header` or `footer` is set, the panel becomes a pinned header + scrolling body (+ footer).

props.name: footer
props.description: Optional bottom slot (pinned below the scrolling sections). A render function receives the collapsed state so it can show a compact (icon-only) footer in the rail.

props.name: account
props.description: The signed-in account, drawn as a filled card pinned to the foot of the column: a small avatar beside the name and a detail line in the third ink. The collapsed rail keeps the avatar alone. It sits under the groups (above a `footer` slot), and in the drawer under the drill-down.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: The name of the sidebar's navigation landmark, a short statement of what it navigates ("Workspace", "Controls components"). A sidebar is a navigation landmark on every platform, and a page holding two navigation landmarks needs a distinct name on each, so a landmark list can tell them apart. In the narrow `responsive` drawer it names the drawer. Omit it and the landmark stays unnamed, as before.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook.

groups.title: Density
groups.note: Density (pick one; default is the comfortable row).

groups.title: Frame
groups.note: Frame (pick one; default is the flush right-bordered column). `bordered` wins over `floating`.

groups.title: Collapse axis
groups.note: Collapse axis (the mini icon-rail).

groups.title: Accordion open-state
groups.note: Accordion open-state (for `collapsible` sections; mirrors Accordion's value API).

groups.title: Responsive drawer axis
groups.note: Responsive drawer axis: at and below `drawerBreakpoint` the sidebar renders as a start-edge (left, RTL-aware) DRILL-DOWN Drawer instead of the inline rail, opened by a consumer-owned hamburger. The rail is unchanged above the breakpoint.

groups.note: Responsive drawer EDGE axis: which side the drawer slides from (default = the start/left edge). First match wins; pass none for the default left. Only applies in drawer mode.

platformNotes.web:
App navigation rail with collapsible sections and active highlighting. The sidebar on the left of this page is a thin adapter over this very `Sidebar` component: it feeds the docs' nav tree in and gets the same collapse, accordion, and active-highlight behavior back.

In glass mode the active row paints a control-layer pane behind its icon, label
and badge; the drill-down drawer keeps its own row treatment. Solid mode keeps
the skin's own row fill.

On the web a hovered row's wash (the palette's translucent `hover`) fades in over
150 ms and back out when the pointer leaves, in the rail and the drill-down alike;
the pressed and active fills still switch at once, and Reduce Motion makes the wash
instant.

Add `responsive` to make it adapt across breakpoints: it stays the accordion rail on desktop, and at and below the `lg` breakpoint (1024px) it becomes a start-edge (left, RTL-aware) **navigation drawer** that drills through the same `sections` one level at a time (tap a group to slide in to its rows, back to return). Drive the drawer's open state with `open` / `onOpenChange` from your own hamburger button; the `header` and `footer` slots pin above and below the drill-down, just as in the rail. The drawer slides from the start (left) edge by default; `drawerRight`, `drawerTop`, and `drawerBottom` change which edge it slides in from. (This page's own left nav does exactly this: an accordion rail here, a drill-down drawer on a phone.)

Pass `drawer` instead when the shell's hamburger is the only way into the tree at every width (a top app bar on a phone and a tablet alike): the sidebar is then the drill-down drawer at every width and never the inline rail, with the same `open` / `onOpenChange` wiring. `drawer` wins over `responsive`.

On the web the sidebar takes the Canvas v4 rail: a 232px column on the sunken page
tone, rows 36px tall at a 9px corner (30px at 8 with `compact`, the docs rail's
density), 500 13px labels in the secondary ink, the active row on the accent's soft
wash in the accent's text ink, and a mono uppercase eyebrow over each titled group.
iOS and Android keep their platform rows (the HIG capsule, the Material 3 pill) in the
v4 colors.

`markers` gives each row a trailing dot: the accent on the active row, and the field
hairline on a row of the reader's current place, either one item with `marked: true`
or every row of a section with `current: true`. A `current` section also sets its
eyebrow in the accent's text ink and its resting rows in the foreground ink, and a
section's `count` sits at the far end of its heading.

`embedded` renders the navigation groups inside an app-owned rail: it inherits the
rail's frame, fill, width and scroll, stacks its groups 16px apart, and renders the
`header` and `footer` slots as plain blocks above and below them, so a filter field or
a heading row fits there. A framed sidebar's header grows past its 56px floor when its
content is taller.

A sidebar is a navigation landmark on every platform. Name it with `accessibilityLabel`,
a short statement of what it navigates such as "Workspace", so a screen reader's
landmark list can tell it apart; a page that holds more than one navigation landmark (a
sidebar beside the app's top navigation, or two sidebars) needs a distinct name on each.
In the narrow `responsive` drawer the same name labels the drawer.

components.name: Slider
components.description: Drag (or tap) along a track to pick a value in a range; the keyboard and screen readers step it too. Controlled by `value`, bounded by `min` / `max`, and snapped to `step`.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value; omit for uncontrolled use. The thumb sits at this value (clamped to [min, max]).

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value for uncontrolled use (a bare <Slider/> drags out of the box). Default `min`.

props.name: min
props.description: Lower bound of the range. Default 0.

props.name: max
props.description: Upper bound of the range. Default 100.

props.name: step
props.description: Snap increment. Default 1. Set to a fraction for finer control.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fired with the next (clamped, snapped) value as the thumb is dragged or the track tapped (both modes).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the slider container.

props.name: children
props.description: The title line, rendered ABOVE the track (a slider's label sits above the rail, not beside it). Supplying it builds the component-owned header so the caller never hand-composes a Column + Typography above a bare slider, and the visible title also names the control for assistive tech (see `accessibilityLabel`).

props.name: description
props.description: Optional muted secondary line rendered under the title, for a hint or unit note.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Render the live current value (the same value the thumb sits at) as a trailing readout on the title line, right-aligned. With no title it still renders the value as a standalone trailing readout above the track. The number tracks the drag in real time and uses tabular figures so it does not jitter.

props.name: percent
props.description: The value is a percentage: the `showValue` readout prints it with a percent sign ("62%") and assistive tech hears it so. Pair with the default 0 to 100 range.

props.name: scale
props.description: A scale under the track: the minimum, the middle and the maximum, spread across the track's width in the small mono meta type, 8 px below the rail.

props.name: small
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the standard track + thumb).

props.name: large
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the standard track + thumb).

props.name: disabled
props.description: State.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the slider (e.g. "Volume").

props.name: style
props.description: Extra style on the slider container, applied last.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the interactive adjustable track, including when a header is shown. Typed as a React Native View. On web, React Native Web exposes its DOM host; focus() and blur() move browser focus. Native host behavior depends on the platform and React Native version. Calling focus() does not activate the control or call accessibility focus APIs.

platformNotes.web:
Drag (or tap) along a track to pick a value in a range; the keyboard and screen readers step it too. Controlled by `value`, bounded by `min` / `max`, and snapped to `step`.

Like the other input-like controls, a slider fills the parent it is given; a step of its own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with `start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a Container step sets its measure.

Pass `ref` to access the interactive adjustable track, including when a header is shown. Use `useRef<ComponentRef<typeof Slider>>(null)` from React, or `useRef<View>(null)` with React Native's `View` type. Object and callback refs are supported and detach on unmount. Calling `ref.current?.focus()` or `.blur()` delegates to the host without activating the control. Browser focus is supported; native focus depends on the platform and React Native version, and is separate from accessibility focus.

Name the setting with string `children`, or pass `accessibilityLabel` when the visible title is omitted or contains rich content.

Use `useRef<ComponentRef<typeof Slider>>(null)` from React, or `useRef<View>(null)` with React Native's `View` type. Object and callback refs are supported and detach on unmount. Calling `ref.current?.focus()` or `.blur()` delegates to the host without activating the control. Browser focus is supported; native focus depends on the platform and React Native version, and is separate from accessibility focus.

Name the setting with string `children`, or pass `accessibilityLabel` when the visible title is omitted or contains rich content.

props.name: label

props.name: hideLegend
props.description: Hide the legend (the labelled dots below the bar).

props.name: detailed
props.description: A two-column legend with separate right-aligned share readouts.

props.name: legendSegments

props.name: track
props.description: Paint the unfilled remainder as a muted rail, so a bar whose segments sum to zero still reads as a bar rather than as blank space. A composition of nothing (an empty queue, a metric at zero) is a real state to draw, and without the rail it draws as an absence.

components.name: StackedList
components.description: Vertical lists with avatar, two-line items, and trailing metadata. Used for contacts, activity feeds, and data previews.

props.name: items
props.description: Rows to render.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional header title; shown above the rows, separated by a rule. It also names the list for assistive tech ("Team, list, 12 items").

props.name: label
props.description: The list's accessible name when it has no `title` (a `title` names the list, and wins when both are set). A screen reader announces it with the list. A `title` that is not a string names the list on the web only, and `label` then names it on iOS and Android. A `virtualized` list needs a name: on the web its scroller is a keyboard stop while the rows overflow, and Chromium names an unnamed stop from the text of every row it has rendered.

props.name: action
props.description: Trailing header content (e.g. an action button); only shown with a title. Takes precedence over `addAction` when both are supplied.

props.name: addAction
props.description: Convenience header action: renders a small outlined button with a leading plus icon and this label (e.g. "Add"). Only shown with a title and when `action` is not set. Serializable, so the playground can drive it.

props.name: rowMenu
props.description: Appends a trailing ghost overflow ("...") action-menu button to every row. Press is reported through `onPressItemMenu`.

props.name: onPressItem
props.description: Press handler for a row, by index. Only used in the `clickable` variant.

props.name: onPressItemMenu
props.description: Press handler for a row's overflow menu, by index. Used with `rowMenu`.

props.name: clickable
props.description: Variant (pick one; default is the plain two-line list).

props.name: card
props.description: Variant (pick one; default is the plain two-line list).

props.name: flush
props.description: Divider modifier: rows are ruled by default; `flush` removes the hairlines.

props.name: virtualized
props.description: Render the rows through a windowed `FlatList` instead of mounting every row up front, for large lists. Give the list a bounded height (via `style`, e.g. `{ maxHeight: 400 }`) so it can scroll; without one it warns and renders eagerly anyway. Default (omitted) mounts all rows, unchanged. Ignored (with a dev warning) when `reorderable` is set: windowing unmounts off-screen rows, which would leave them undraggable and unmeasurable mid-drag. On the web, while the rows overflow, the windowed list is a keyboard tab stop the keyboard can scroll, and the list's frame draws the focus ring while it has keyboard focus.

props.name: reorderable
props.description: Make the rows reorderable: each row gains a leading drag grip (keyboard- and screen-reader-operable: Space grabs, the arrow keys move, Space drops, Escape cancels) and the list becomes one drop zone. The order stays CONTROLLED by the consumer's `items` array: a drop only reports the move through `onReorder`, never reorders internally.

props.name: onReorder
props.description: Fired on drop with the computed move (row id, from/to index, new neighbors).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Variant
groups.note: Variant (pick one; default is the plain two-line list).

groups.title: Divider modifier
groups.note: Divider modifier: rows are ruled by default; `flush` removes the hairlines.

Rows can carry a per-item `trailing` slot for an inline control, and

screen-reader-operable) that reports each drop through `onReorder` while the
order stays controlled by your `items` array.

The rows are a list, as in Tailwind UI, and each row is one of its items: a
screen reader announces the list with its number of rows and moves through it
row by row. A clickable row's button sits inside its item. The header `title`
names the list; a list without a title takes its name from `label`.

own. On the web, while those rows overflow, that list is a keyboard tab stop
