any), the keyboard can scroll it, and while it has keyboard focus the list's
card, or a plain list's frame, draws the theme's focus ring. Only the rows near
its viewport are mounted, and each says where it sits in the whole list, so a
screen reader still counts every row. Give a windowed list a `title` or a
`label`: focused, a list with no name is named in Chromium from the text of
every row it has rendered, so the kit warns in development when it has neither.

components.name: Stats
components.description: Single value, grouped row, with sparkline, with comparison. Used for dashboards and overview pages.

props.name: items
props.description: The metrics to render, in order.

props.name: plain
props.description: Borderless metric stacks on a shared surface, for nesting inside a card.

props.name: compact
props.description: Dense value-first tile for a navigation rail: a 12px inset and a 20px headline.

props.name: large
props.description: Value-first dashboard tile with a 36px headline.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional heading shown above the metrics (mainly for the plain surface).

props.name: framed
props.description: Draw every metric's strip on a muted track, in one bounded band. For a ROW of metrics, where the strips are read against each other. Without it each strip draws only its marks, so a metric with a quiet series shows a near-empty band beside one with a full bar and the row's densities range from blank to solid with nothing tying them together; the eye lands on the fullest tile rather than scanning the row. The track gives every strip the same frame whatever its data, so a flat series reads as a chart sitting at zero and the fill is the only thing that varies.

props.name: onPressItem
props.description: Make each metric a tappable target (drill into the underlying detail). When set, every metric renders as a Pressable with a button role and a pressed affordance, so a tappable stat needs no hand-rolled Pressable.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Surface
groups.note: Surface (pick one; default is bordered cards).

platformNotes.web:
Single value, grouped row, with sparkline, with comparison. Used for dashboards and overview pages.

Under the value each tile can draw one strip: its trend (`spark`) or its composition (`share`). Both reserve the same height, so a row that mixes them keeps one card height and no tile is left half empty. `framed` puts every strip on a muted track, which is what makes a ROW of them scan evenly.

The metrics sit edge to edge inside one bordered surface, a hairline between each: a 16px
inset, a 13px label, a 28px figure and a 12px delta led by its direction arrow. `framed`
separates them into tiles 12px apart. A trend draws as a small line beside the figure and
a composition as a thin bar over its legend. `compact` renders value-first rail tiles with
a 12px inset and 20px figures; `large` renders 36px dashboard headlines; compact wins if
both are set. Each item may include a muted `description`.

components.name: Stepper
components.description: Increment, decrement, or type a number in a bounded range. A − button, an editable numeric center field, and a + button, controlled by `value` and clamped to `min` / `max` by `step`. This is the ± numeric control (the iOS UIStepper idiom); for a multi-step progress indicator see Steps.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled numeric value (clamped to [min, max] for display); omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value for uncontrolled use (a bare <Stepper /> steps out of the box). Default `min`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fired with the next clamped value when buttons, adjustment keys, or direct entry change it (both modes).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the group container.

props.name: min
props.description: Lower bound. Default 0. The − button disables when value <= min.

props.name: max
props.description: Upper bound. Default Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. The + button disables when value >= max.

props.name: step
props.description: Increment/decrement amount for the ± buttons and adjustment keys. Default 1.

props.name: label
props.description: The control's persistent, component-owned label. When set it renders as a VISIBLE title ABOVE the ± control (mirroring Input's above-field placement, per-OS type from the skin) and becomes the group's programmatic name (wired via accessibilityLabel + aria-labelledby). When omitted, the control keeps the invisible "Number" accessible-name fallback and renders no visible label, so a bare `<Stepper />` looks exactly as before.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional muted secondary line rendered under the label (parity with Input). Takes effect only alongside `label`.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the control required: appends a destructive "*" to the label (decorative, never in the accessible name) and announces the control as required, through aria-required on the web's numeric field and with the word in its name ("Quantity, required") on iOS and Android. The star takes effect only alongside `label`.

props.name: suffix
props.description: A unit or note beside the control, 16 px after it on the same line ("× 4px", "items"): a string is set in the 400 13 px subtle ink, a node as it is. Unlike `description`, it reads as part of the value's line.

props.name: small
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the medium control). Precedence: large > small.

props.name: large
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the medium control). Precedence: large > small.

props.name: disabled
props.description: State.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the underlying React Native host. Supports object refs and callback refs; native methods follow the platform's behavior.

groups.title: Size
groups.note: Size (pick one; default is the medium control). Precedence: large > small.

components.name: Steps
components.description: Multi-step progress indicators: horizontal, vertical, with progress.

props.name: steps
props.description: Ordered steps to render. Each is a label with an optional one-line note.

props.name: current
props.description: Index of the active step (CONTROLLED). Earlier steps read completed, later ones muted. Omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultCurrent
props.description: Initial active step for uncontrolled use (pressing a step, with `onStepPress`, moves it).

props.name: vertical
props.description: Layout (pick one; default is horizontal). Precedence: progress, segmented, vertical.

props.name: compact
props.description: A short vertical list with 22px markers and no connector lines, for a workflow sidebar.

props.name: segmented
props.description: Equal segments in a row: each step a 4 px bar (the accent once reached, glowing on the current step) over its label and, from its `description`, a status line inked by the step's state (the success ink once done, the accent's text ink on the current step).

props.name: progress
props.description: Render a labeled percentage progress bar instead of discrete steps.

props.name: stacks
props.description: Responsive (horizontal layout only): render the EXISTING vertical layout when the component's own CONTAINER is at or below `stackBreakpoint` (default `sm` = 640). Container-measured with a viewport seed, mirroring Row `stacks`. `vertical` and `progress` are unaffected (a progress bar is already fluid).

props.name: stackBreakpoint
props.description: The breakpoint at and below which `stacks` goes vertical (default `"sm"`). Only meaningful with `stacks`.

props.name: value
props.description: Progress mode only: filled fraction, 0-100 (clamped). Defaults to 0.

props.name: label
props.description: Progress mode only: caption shown left of the percentage.

props.name: onStepPress
props.description: When set, each step circle is pressable, reporting the step index.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Layout
groups.note: Layout (pick one; default is horizontal). Precedence: progress, segmented, vertical.

platformNotes.web: Multi-step progress indicators: horizontal, vertical, with progress.
platformNotes.ios: Multi-step progress indicators: horizontal, vertical, with progress.

props.name: color
props.description: The fill: any React Native color string. Pass a theme token, not a literal.

props.name: violet
props.description: Palette picker (pick one): the sample becomes the 16 px hue disc of that accent palette, a radio named for it (a size boolean sizes the disc to that sample edge: `small` is 32 px). Precedence is ThemeProvider's: cyan, mint, rose, amber, violet.

props.name: cyan
props.description: Palette picker (pick one): the sample becomes the 16 px hue disc of that accent palette, a radio named for it (a size boolean sizes the disc to that sample edge: `small` is 32 px). Precedence is ThemeProvider's: cyan, mint, rose, amber, violet.

props.name: mint
props.description: Palette picker (pick one): the sample becomes the 16 px hue disc of that accent palette, a radio named for it (a size boolean sizes the disc to that sample edge: `small` is 32 px). Precedence is ThemeProvider's: cyan, mint, rose, amber, violet.

props.name: rose
props.description: Palette picker (pick one): the sample becomes the 16 px hue disc of that accent palette, a radio named for it (a size boolean sizes the disc to that sample edge: `small` is 32 px). Precedence is ThemeProvider's: cyan, mint, rose, amber, violet.

props.name: amber
props.description: Palette picker (pick one): the sample becomes the 16 px hue disc of that accent palette, a radio named for it (a size boolean sizes the disc to that sample edge: `small` is 32 px). Precedence is ThemeProvider's: cyan, mint, rose, amber, violet.

props.name: selected
props.description: The sample is the chosen one: draws the selection ring (a 2 px gap in the page color, then a 2 px band). On a plain sample the band is the accent and the name says "selected"; on a palette picker it is the one in force and the radio is checked.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Palette picker: pick this palette.

props.name: children
props.description: The sample's name (the token name). Swatch owns this label column.

props.name: value
props.description: Primary mono line under the name: what the name resolves to (a hex, a custom-property name, a ramp step).

props.name: detail
props.description: Secondary mono line under the value, for a second notation of the same color (an oklch value, a legacy alias).

props.name: tiny
props.description: The 20 px disc of a token chip (`<Chip token icon={<Swatch tiny ring circle />}>`).

props.name: circle
props.description: Circle instead of the default rounded square. Keeps the 1:1 footprint, so it wins over `block`'s stretch.

props.name: ring
props.description: Draws the token chip's hairline INSIDE the sample, a 1 px inset ring in the field border, in place of the resting hairline edge; a selected sample keeps its selection ring outside it.

props.name: inline
props.description: Put the label column beside the block instead of under it.

props.name: block
props.description: Stretch the block to the parent's width; the size then reads as its height (the full-width ramp bar).

props.name: tile
props.description: The labelled colour tile: the parent's width, 64 px tall (40 `small`), its name set inside the fill on one line (ellipsized where it outgrows the tile) at an 8 px inset in the 11 px mono face, at the foot (centred `small`). `ink` paints the name; the value lines are read into the accessible name only.

props.name: bar
props.description: A colour bar: the parent's width, 26 px tall at the swatch bar corner (a neutral role's sample).

props.name: steps
props.description: One bar of colour steps in place of `color`, flush and clipped at the ramp corner at the size's height (`block small` is the 32 px accent ramp); `segmented` stands them apart.

props.name: segmented
props.description: `steps` as separate segments: a 28 px bar, 4 apart, the step corner inside and the bar corner at its ends.

props.name: fluid
props.description: The chip's edge is the parent's width, held 1:1 (a spectrum's discs filling their cells).

props.name: glow
props.description: The fill's own ambient light under the chip (`0 12px 30px -8px`, the fill at .6).

props.name: centered
props.description: The label column centred under the chip, 10 px below it.

props.name: bare
props.description: No resting edge: the sample sits on its fill alone (a saturated fill that needs no hairline).

props.name: compact
props.description: The mono lockup: the name 500 12 px and the value 400 10 px in the code face, each on one line (ellipsized where it outgrows a narrow column), 6 px apart and 6 px under the chip; a `block` chip is 56 px tall.

props.name: ink
props.description: The `tile` name's ink, a theme token like `color` (default the foreground).

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name override. By default the sample names itself from its own name, value, and detail (falling back to the color string), so pass this only when the name is a node rather than text and there is nothing to read.

props.name: decorative
props.description: The sample is decoration beside text that already names it (a theme choice's disc before its label): hidden from assistive tech, so the text carries the name once. Pass it in place of `accessibilityLabel`.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: For layout composition only (not styling): the fill, radius, and size come from props.

groups.title: Palette picker
groups.note: Palette picker (pick one): the sample becomes the 16 px hue disc of that accent palette, a radio named for it (a size boolean sizes the disc to that sample edge: `small` is 32 px). Precedence is ThemeProvider's: cyan, mint, rose, amber, violet.

groups.title: Size
groups.note: Size (pick one; default 48). Sets the block's edge, or its height when `block`. Precedence: `tiny` > `small` > `large`.

groups.title: Form
groups.note: Form (pick one; default the rounded square). Precedence: `tile` > `bar` > `circle`; a `steps` list wins over all three.

platformNotes.web:
A color sample: a filled rounded block with the token's name and value beneath
it, the anatomy a design-system color sheet repeats down a page. Swatch owns the
whole lockup, so a sheet never sets a bare block next to a hand-built text
column and drifts row to row.

Pass a live theme token as `color` and the sample follows the active scheme; a
hairline edge keeps a white or near-black sample visible on the surface behind
it. The chip is 48px at a 12px corner (32 `small`, 72 `large`, and 20 `tiny`,
the disc of a token Chip), the name a 13px line and the value lines 11px mono
in the subtle ink; the lockup also comes as a `circle`, `inline` (the label
beside the block), or as a `block` (a full-width ramp bar). `ring` draws the
edge as a 1px inset ring in the field border instead of the hairline, the token
chip's swatch. `selected` marks the chosen sample with the selection ring, a
2px gap in the page color and then a 2px accent band, and adds "selected" to
its accessible name. `decorative` hides a sample from assistive tech when text
beside it already names it (a theme choice's disc before its label), so the
name is read once.

A palette picker takes one of the kit's five accent palettes, `violet`, `cyan`,
`mint`, `rose` or `amber` (ThemeProvider's precedence: cyan, mint, rose, amber,
violet), with `selected` and `onPress`. It is a 16px disc of the palette's hue,
the same in both schemes, and a radio named for its palette ("Violet"). The
palette in force wears the selection ring, a 2px gap in the card color and then
a 2px muted-foreground band; the others draw none. On the web a hovered disc
grows to 1.25 times its size. A size boolean sizes the disc to that sample edge
(`small` is a 32px disc, the size a form's hue choice takes). Put the pickers in
a `radiogroup` so the set reads as one choice. A plain sample still uses `color`.

The section page's samples come as forms and lockups of the same component. `tile` is
the labelled colour tile, the parent's width and 64 px tall (40 `small`), its name set
inside the fill on one line (ellipsized where it outgrows the tile, its accessible name
whole) in the 11 px code face at an 8 px inset, at the foot (centred `small`),
in the `ink` it is given. `bar` is a colour bar, the parent's width at 26 px and a 7 px
corner. `steps` takes a list of colours in place of `color` and draws one bar of them,
flush and clipped at a 10 px corner at the size's height; `segmented` stands them 4 px
apart in a 28 px bar, each at a 3 px corner but for the bar's two outer ends at 7. The
form precedence is `tile` > `bar` > `circle`, and a `steps` list wins over all three.
`fluid` makes the chip's edge the parent's width, held 1:1; `glow` lays the fill's own
light under the chip; `centered` centres the label column 10 px under the chip; `bare`
drops the resting edge from a fill that needs none; and `compact` is the mono lockup, the
name 500 12 px and the value 400 10 px in the code face, each on one line (ellipsized in a
narrow column), 6 px apart and 6 px under a 56 px `block`.

components.name: Switch
components.description: On / off switch, isolated or grouped in a settings list.

props.name: checked
props.description: Controlled on/off state; omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Initial state for uncontrolled use (a bare <Switch /> is interactive).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fired with the next checked value when the switch is toggled (both modes). Web keyboard activation supports Space on release and Enter.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Alias of onChange, for parity with RN's value-style callbacks.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the pressable row.

props.name: small
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the standard track). The web track scales; iOS and Android draw their platform switch, which comes in one size.

props.name: large
props.description: Size (pick one; default is the standard track). The web track scales; iOS and Android draw their platform switch, which comes in one size.

props.name: chip
props.description: A compact bordered capsule with its label after the switch, for a toolbar setting.

props.name: listed
props.description: A row of a settings list: 10 px above and below the row, so a stack of switches reads as a list rather than a form (stack them in a `Column tight`). Pair with `divided` on every row after the first.

props.name: divided
props.description: A hairline above the row in the `border` ink: a settings list's separator from the row before.

props.name: disabled
props.description: State.

props.name: children
props.description: Optional label, rendered to the left of the track.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional muted description line, rendered under the label.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the switch when no visible `children` label is rendered (e.g. a switch embedded in an Action Panel whose label sits in sibling Text). Without it, a label-less switch announces only "switch, on/off".

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the interactive switch row, including its label. Typed as a React Native View. On web, React Native Web exposes its DOM host; focus() and blur() move browser focus. Native host behavior depends on the platform and React Native version. Calling focus() does not activate the control or call accessibility focus APIs.

groups.title: Size
groups.note: Size (pick one; default is the standard track). The web track scales; iOS and Android draw their platform switch, which comes in one size.

platformNotes.web:
On / off switch, isolated or grouped in a settings list.

In glass mode a switch keeps its solid look on every platform: it is a small
mark inside content, not a surface, so its track and knob draw as in solid mode,
with no pane and no rim, a checked track in its solid brand fill. The track, the
label, the description and the hit target never move, and the checked state flips
at once. A disabled switch is inert.

`small` and `large` scale the track on the web.
Pass `chip` for a compact toolbar setting: a 32 px bordered capsule with a 26×16 track, a 10 px knob and the label after the switch. The web thumb follows the reference spring and Reduce Motion; native skins keep their own switch.
On iOS and Android the switch is the
platform's own control, which comes in one size (51x31 on iOS, 52x32 on Android), so
the size props leave it unchanged there.

Pass `ref` to access the interactive switch row, including its label. Use `useRef<ComponentRef<typeof Switch>>(null)` from React, or `useRef<View>(null)` with React Native's `View` type. Object and callback refs are supported and detach on unmount. Calling `ref.current?.focus()` or `.blur()` delegates to the host without activating the control. Browser focus is supported; native focus depends on the platform and React Native version, and is separate from accessibility focus.

On the web, Space activates the focused control on key release, and Enter also activates it. Holding Space does not repeat the change. Moving focus away, disabling the control, or composing text cancels a pending Space press.

components.name: TabBar
components.description: Bottom app navigation: a row of equal-width destinations, each an icon over a short label, with exactly one active. The mobile idiom (the iOS 26 floating tab bar / Material 3 navigation bar), rendered through the glass functional layer.

props.name: active
props.description: The active item's key; omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultActive
props.description: Initial active key for uncontrolled use (defaults to the first item's key).

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the pressed destination's key (both modes).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the tablist row.

props.name: bottomInset
props.description: Safe-area bottom inset, e.g. `insets.bottom`. It is added BELOW the bar's own symmetric vertical padding (not in place of it), so the bar clears the home indicator without making the bottom margin heavier than the top. Defaults to 0 (web desktop / no inset).

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only. Use bottomInset for the safe area.

platformNotes.web:
Bottom app navigation: a row of equal-width destinations, each an icon over a short label, with exactly one active.
The mobile idiom (the iOS 26 floating tab bar / Material 3 navigation bar), rendered through the glass functional layer.

iOS and web share the iOS 26 anatomy: a 62 px capsule that floats above the
content (which scrolls beneath it), inset from the sides, with the safe-area
inset kept under the capsule, and the selected destination washed in the accent
as a capsule covering its whole cell. Android docks the Material 3 bar
full-bleed, 80 tall under a hairline, with its 64 by 32 icon pill. In glass mode
the selection is a control-layer pane on the active destination: the cell
capsule on iOS and web, the icon pill on Android. Solid mode retains the
ordinary platform surface.

components.name: Tabs
components.description: Underline, pill, vertical, with badges.

props.name: tabs
props.description: Triggers, left to right. Strings, or `{ label, badge }` for a count.

props.name: active
props.description: Index of the active trigger; omit for uncontrolled use.

props.name: defaultActive
props.description: Initial active index for uncontrolled use (a bare <Tabs /> switches out of the box).

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the pressed trigger's index (both modes). Matches TabBar and ButtonGroup, which also fire `onSelect` for the active-index change.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the tablist row.

props.name: pills
props.description: Look (pick one; default is the underline look). Precedence when more than one is passed: pills, then vertical, then underline.

props.name: vertical
props.description: Look (pick one; default is the underline look). Precedence when more than one is passed: pills, then vertical, then underline.

props.name: underline
props.description: Look (pick one; default is the underline look). Precedence when more than one is passed: pills, then vertical, then underline.

props.name: block
props.description: Layout: equal full-width triggers vs. leading-aligned hugging triggers.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Layout (the underline and pills rows): a row longer than its container wraps onto further lines inside one track instead of panning in the overflow scroller, so every tab stays on screen at once. The track fills its container and grows taller, its corners concentric with the pills. `block` never overflows and wins; a `responsive` vertical rail honors it once it flattens.

props.name: responsive
props.description: Responsive (vertical look only): render the EXISTING horizontal underline look when the component's own CONTAINER is at or below `sm` (640), where a side rail would starve the panel beside it. Container-measured with a viewport seed. `pills` and `underline` are unaffected.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook.

groups.title: Look
groups.note: Look (pick one; default is the underline look). Precedence when more than one is passed: pills, then vertical, then underline.

groups.title: Layout
groups.note: Layout: equal full-width triggers vs. leading-aligned hugging triggers.

platformNotes.web:

tint with readable foreground ink. Solid mode keeps the complete platform
treatment.

components.name: Text
components.description: Renders text. In React Native every string must live inside a Text element, so you cannot put a bare string in a View. For type scale and tone in app code, reach for `<Typography>` (e.g. `<Typography h3>`, `<Typography body>`, `<Typography tiny muted>`), which owns the kit's roles and colors; use the raw Text primitive for the primitive-level cases it does not cover: `numberOfLines` truncation and nested inline runs.

props.name: allowFontScaling
props.description: Specifies whether fonts should scale to respect Text Size accessibility settings. The default is `true`.

props.name: ellipsizeMode
props.description: This can be one of the following values: - `head` - The line is displayed so that the end fits in the container and the missing text at the beginning of the line is indicated by an ellipsis glyph. e.g., "...wxyz" - `middle` - The line is displayed so that the beginning and end fit in the container and the missing text in the middle is indicated by an ellipsis glyph. "ab...yz" - `tail` - The line is displayed so that the beginning fits in the container and the missing text at the end of the line is indicated by an ellipsis glyph. e.g., "abcd..." - `clip` - Lines are not drawn past the edge of the text container. The default is `tail`. `numberOfLines` must be set in conjunction with this prop. > `clip` is working only for iOS

props.name: id
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: lineBreakMode
props.description: Line Break mode. Works only with numberOfLines. clip is working only for iOS

props.name: numberOfLines
props.description: Used to truncate the text with an ellipsis after computing the text layout, including line wrapping, such that the total number of lines does not exceed this number. This prop is commonly used with `ellipsizeMode`.

props.name: onLayout
props.description: Invoked on mount and layout changes with {nativeEvent: { layout: {x, y, width, height}}}.

props.name: onTextLayout
props.description: Invoked on Text layout

props.name: onPress
props.description: This function is called on press. Text intrinsically supports press handling with a default highlight state (which can be disabled with suppressHighlighting).

props.name: onLongPress
props.description: This function is called on long press. e.g., `onLongPress={this.increaseSize}>`

props.name: testID
props.description: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.

props.name: nativeID
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: maxFontSizeMultiplier
props.description: Specifies largest possible scale a font can reach when allowFontScaling is enabled. props.name: dynamicTypeRamp

props.name: suppressHighlighting

props.name: lineBreakStrategyIOS

props.name: selectable

props.name: textBreakStrategy

components.name: TextInput
components.description: Single-line (or multiline) text entry. Control it with `value` + `onChangeText`, and style the box with the usual View style props. Common props: `placeholder`, `secureTextEntry` (passwords), `keyboardType`, and `multiline`.

props.name: systemFocus
props.description: Keep the platform’s system focus appearance instead of the themed ring.

props.name: allowFontScaling
props.description: Specifies whether fonts should scale to respect Text Size accessibility settings. The default is `true`.

props.name: autoCapitalize
props.description: Can tell TextInput to automatically capitalize certain characters. characters: all characters, words: first letter of each word sentences: first letter of each sentence (default) none: don't auto capitalize anything https://reactnative.dev/docs/textinput#autocapitalize

props.name: autoComplete

props.name: autoCorrect

props.name: autoFocus

props.name: blurOnSubmit
props.description: If `true`, the text field will blur when submitted. The default value is true for single-line fields and false for multiline fields. Note that for multiline fields, setting `blurOnSubmit` to `true` means that pressing return will blur the field and trigger the `onSubmitEditing` event instead of inserting a newline into the field.

props.name: submitBehavior
props.description: When the return key is pressed, For single line inputs: - `'newline`' defaults to `'blurAndSubmit'` - `undefined` defaults to `'blurAndSubmit'` For multiline inputs: - `'newline'` adds a newline - `undefined` defaults to `'newline'` For both single line and multiline inputs: - `'submit'` will only send a submit event and not blur the input - `'blurAndSubmit`' will both blur the input and send a submit event

props.name: contextMenuHidden

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Provides an initial value that will change when the user starts typing. Useful for simple use-cases where you don't want to deal with listening to events and updating the value prop to keep the controlled state in sync.

props.description: If false, text is not editable. The default value is true.

The following values work across platforms: - default - numeric - email-address - phone-pad The following values work on iOS: - ascii-capable - numbers-and-punctuation - url - number-pad - name-phone-pad - decimal-pad - twitter - web-search The following values work on Android: - visible-password

props.description: Works like the inputmode attribute in HTML, it determines which keyboard to open, e.g. numeric and has precedence over keyboardType.

props.name: maxLength

props.name: multiline
props.description: If true, the text input can be multiple lines. The default value is false.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input is blurred Note: If you are trying to find the last value of TextInput, you can use the `onEndEditing` event, which is fired upon completion of editing.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's text changes.

props.name: onChangeText
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's text changes. Changed text is passed as an argument to the callback handler.

props.name: onContentSizeChange
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's content size changes. This will be called with `{ nativeEvent: { contentSize: { width, height } } }`. Only called for multiline text inputs.

props.name: onEndEditing

props.name: onSelectionChange

props.name: onSubmitEditing

props.name: onScroll
props.description: Invoked on content scroll with `{ nativeEvent: { contentOffset: { x, y } } }`. May also contain other properties from ScrollEvent but on Android contentSize is not provided for performance reasons.

props.name: onKeyPress
props.description: Callback that is called when a key is pressed. This will be called with `{ nativeEvent: { key: keyValue } }` where keyValue is 'Enter' or 'Backspace' for respective keys and the typed-in character otherwise including ' ' for space. Fires before onChange callbacks. Note: on Android only the inputs from soft keyboard are handled, not the hardware keyboard inputs.

props.name: selectTextOnFocus
props.description: If true, all text will automatically be selected on focus

props.name: selection
props.type: { start: number; end?: number | undefined; } | undefined
props.description: The start and end of the text input's selection. Set start and end to the same value to position the cursor.

props.name: selectionColor

props.name: inputAccessoryViewButtonLabel

props.name: value
props.description: The value to show for the text input. TextInput is a controlled component, which means the native value will be forced to match this value prop if provided. For most uses this works great, but in some cases this may cause flickering - one common cause is preventing edits by keeping value the same. In addition to simply setting the same value, either set editable={false}, or set/update maxLength to prevent unwanted edits without flicker.

props.name: maxFontSizeMultiplier
props.description: Specifies largest possible scale a font can reach when allowFontScaling is enabled. Possible values: - null/undefined (default): inherit from the parent node or the global default (0) - 0: no max, ignore parent/global default - >= 1: sets the maxFontSizeMultiplier of this node to this value

props.name: hitSlop
props.description: This defines how far a touch event can start away from the view. Typical interface guidelines recommend touch targets that are at least 30 - 40 points/density-independent pixels. If a Touchable view has a height of 20 the touchable height can be extended to 40 with hitSlop={{top: 10, bottom: 10, left: 0, right: 0}} NOTE The touch area never extends past the parent view bounds and the Z-index of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch hits two overlapping views.

props.name: id
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing
props.description: Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior. The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value. This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background). Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default. If you do need to enable this property for an animation, consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame). If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once, saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU.

props.name: onLayout
props.description: Invoked on mount and layout changes with {nativeEvent: { layout: {x, y, width, height}}}.

props.name: pointerEvents
props.description: In the absence of auto property, none is much like CSS's none value. box-none is as if you had applied the CSS class: .box-none { pointer-events: none; } .box-none * { pointer-events: all; } box-only is the equivalent of .box-only { pointer-events: all; } .box-only * { pointer-events: none; } But since pointerEvents does not affect layout/appearance, and we are already deviating from the spec by adding additional modes, we opt to not include pointerEvents on style. On some platforms, we would need to implement it as a className anyways. Using style or not is an implementation detail of the platform.

props.name: removeClippedSubviews
props.description: This is a special performance property exposed by RCTView and is useful for scrolling content when there are many subviews, most of which are offscreen. For this property to be effective, it must be applied to a view that contains many subviews that extend outside its bound. The subviews must also have overflow: hidden, as should the containing view (or one of its superviews).

props.name: nativeID
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: collapsable
props.description: Views that are only used to layout their children or otherwise don't draw anything may be automatically removed from the native hierarchy as an optimization. Set this property to false to disable this optimization and ensure that this View exists in the native view hierarchy.

props.name: collapsableChildren
props.description: Setting to false prevents direct children of the view from being removed from the native view hierarchy, similar to the effect of setting `collapsable={false}` on each child.

props.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
props.description: Whether this view should render itself (and all of its children) into a single hardware texture on the GPU. On Android, this is useful for animations and interactions that only modify opacity, rotation, translation, and/or scale: in those cases, the view doesn't have to be redrawn and display lists don't need to be re-executed. The texture can just be re-used and re-composited with different parameters. The downside is that this can use up limited video memory, so this prop should be set back to false at the end of the interaction/animation.

props.description: Whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description: Indicates whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/tabindex for more details. Supports the following values: - 0 (View is focusable) - -1 (View is not focusable)

props.description: Whether this view should be rendered as a bitmap before compositing. On iOS, this is useful for animations and interactions that do not modify this component's dimensions nor its children; for example, when translating the position of a static view, rasterization allows the renderer to reuse a cached bitmap of a static view and quickly composite it during each frame. Rasterization incurs an off-screen drawing pass and the bitmap consumes memory. Test and measure when using this property.

props.description: *(Apple TV only)* When set to true, this view will be focusable and navigable using the Apple TV remote.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceX
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceY
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxTiltAngle
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 0.05.

props.name: tvParallaxMagnification
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 1.0.

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponder
props.description: Does this view want to become responder on the start of a touch?

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponder
props.description: Called for every touch move on the View when it is not the responder: does this view want to "claim" touch responsiveness?

props.name: onResponderEnd
props.description: If the View returns true and attempts to become the responder, one of the following will happen:

props.name: onResponderGrant
props.description: The View is now responding for touch events. This is the time to highlight and show the user what is happening

props.name: onResponderReject
props.description: Something else is the responder right now and will not release it

props.name: onResponderMove
props.description: The user is moving their finger

props.name: onResponderRelease
props.description: Fired at the end of the touch, ie "touchUp"

props.name: onResponderTerminationRequest
props.description: Something else wants to become responder. Should this view release the responder? Returning true allows release

props.name: onResponderTerminate
props.description: The responder has been taken from the View. Might be taken by other views after a call to onResponderTerminationRequest, or might be taken by the OS without asking (happens with control center/ notification center on iOS)

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description: onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern, where the deepest node is called first. That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers. This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable. However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder. This can be handled by using the capture phase. Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component, it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture. So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start, it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description: onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern, where the deepest node is called first. That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers. This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable. However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder. This can be handled by using the capture phase. Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component, it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture. So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start, it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.description: By using the accessibilityLanguage property, the screen reader will understand which language to use while reading the element's label, value and hint. props.name: accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer
props.description: A Boolean value that indicates whether or not to show the item in the large content viewer. Available on iOS 13.0+ https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityshowslargecontentviewer

props.name: accessibilityLargeContentTitle
props.description: When `accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer` is set, this string will be used as title for the large content viewer. https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylargecontenttitle

props.name: accessibilityRespondsToUserInteraction
props.description: Blocks the user from interacting with the component through keyboard while still allowing screen reader to interact with it if this View is still accessible.

props.name: disableKeyboardShortcuts
props.description: If true, the keyboard shortcuts (undo/redo and copy buttons) are disabled. The default value is false.

props.name: clearButtonMode
props.description: enum('never', 'while-editing', 'unless-editing', 'always') When the clear button should appear on the right side of the text view

props.name: clearTextOnFocus
props.description: If true, clears the text field automatically when editing begins

props.name: dataDetectorTypes
props.description: Determines the types of data converted to clickable URLs in the text input. Only valid if `multiline={true}` and `editable={false}`. By default no data types are detected. You can provide one type or an array of many types. Possible values for `dataDetectorTypes` are: - `'phoneNumber'` - `'link'` - `'address'` - `'calendarEvent'` - `'none'` - `'all'`

props.name: enablesReturnKeyAutomatically
props.description: If true, the keyboard disables the return key when there is no text and automatically enables it when there is text. The default value is false.

props.name: keyboardAppearance
props.description: Determines the color of the keyboard.

props.name: passwordRules
props.description: Provide rules for your password. For example, say you want to require a password with at least eight characters consisting of a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, at least one number, and at most two consecutive characters. "required: upper; required: lower; required: digit; max-consecutive: 2; minlength: 8;"

props.name: rejectResponderTermination
props.description: If `true`, allows TextInput to pass touch events to the parent component. This allows components to be swipeable from the TextInput on iOS, as is the case on Android by default. If `false`, TextInput always asks to handle the input (except when disabled).

props.name: selectionState

props.name: spellCheck

props.description: Placeholder shown while the field is empty.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's persistent label. Its placement is platform-adaptive: iOS and web render it ABOVE the field; Android renders the Material 3 in-container FLOATING label — a MULTILINE float pinned to the first text line at rest, floating to the top once the field is focused or filled. The label names the field for a11y.

props.name: systemFocus
props.description: Preserve the platform system focus outline.

props.name: dense
props.description: Dense paragraph-entry metrics matching the application field family.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Prevent edits while retaining focus and the resting appearance.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field as required: appends a destructive "*" to the label (decorative, never in the accessible name) and announces the field as required, through aria-required on the web and with the word in its name ("Bio, required") on iOS and Android. The star and the spoken word take effect only alongside `label`.

props.name: rows
props.description: Visible rows the field sizes to (4 when omitted). Sets the min height (rows times the skin's line plus the field's padding); the field still grows with content past this floor.

props.name: showCount
props.description: Show a live character-count line inside the field's own anatomy: an end-aligned muted caption under the control reading "N / max" (just "N" when no `maxLength` is set), where N is the current text length. When on, `maxLength` becomes a SOFT cap rather than a hard one: it is NOT forwarded to the native TextInput (a hard cap silently drops the extra keystroke, so the overage could never be seen), the user can type past it, and once N exceeds `maxLength` the count turns destructive AND the field enters its error state automatically (red border/underline). Leave `showCount` off to keep `maxLength` as a hard input cap.

props.name: error

platformNotes.web:
Multi-line input, with character count, with toolbar.

Pass `label` (and `required`) to name the field:
iOS and web render the label
above the control, while Android floats the Material 3 in-container label at the
top of the multiline box, making room for itself at the user's text size and
truncating on one line when it is longer than the box while the field's
accessible name stays the whole label.
The required star is decorative: a screen
reader hears the field as required,
from `aria-required` on the web and from its
name ("Bio, required") on iOS and Android.
The box fills the parent it is given; a step of its
own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with `start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a Container
step sets its measure.

The box is the single-line Input's on each platform. On the web it is the sunken
well with a 1 px hairline that steps to the subtle ink on hover, takes the `ring`
edge and a 4 px accent halo on focus and the `destructive` edge on error, with a
400 value on a 1.55 line; the count is an 11 px mono caption ("12 / 280").
iOS keeps
its 8 pt `card` box with the error wash and a tabular count ("12/280").
Android uses
the same opaque muted surface as the other filled fields, and its count sits at the
end of the supporting-text row.
Its label uses `primary-text` when focused and
`destructive-text` on error. The over-limit character count also uses
`destructive-text` on every platform. Without `rows` the field starts four rows tall.

Inside an overlay, Escape follows the overlay's cancellation policy. A supplied
`onKeyPress` runs first and can call `preventDefault()` to handle Escape locally.
Cancelling an IME candidate keeps the overlay open.

`dense` preserves application paragraph fields with 13/19.5 semibold values,
the dense field inset and explicit visible rows. `eyebrow` supplies the matching
web label. `accessibilityLabel` overrides the visible label’s accessible name;
`readOnly` prevents edits without dimming or removing the field from focus.
`systemFocus` keeps the platform system focus outline.

`embedded` renders a bare editor inside a parent-owned field surface and focus frame, as used by Chat. It implies `flush` and removes the independent backing and focus outline; the parent must provide a visible focus treatment.

components.name: Toast
components.description: A transient notification card. Render a `<Toast>` directly, or drive them imperatively: mount a `<ToastProvider>` near your app root and call `toast(...)` from the `useToast()` hook to enqueue auto-dismissing toasts that stack over the app.

props.name: brief
props.description: A single-line notification pill without extra chrome.

props.name: message
props.description: The headline line (required).

props.name: description
props.description: A secondary line under the message.

props.name: action
props.description: A trailing action button (e.g. Undo).

props.name: success
props.description: Green success intent (icon + tint).

props.name: destructive
props.description: Red danger intent (icon + tint). This is the name the intent axis uses across the kit (Button, AlertDialog, and every chart) and the one the design hand-off uses.

props.name: warning
props.description: Amber warning intent (icon + tint).

props.name: info
props.description: Brand-tinted informational intent (icon + tint).

props.name: icon
props.description: Override the auto intent icon; pass any node, or omit to use the intent glyph.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: When provided, render a trailing dismiss (x) that calls this.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook.

platformNotes.web:
A transient notification card. Render a `<Toast>` directly, or drive them imperatively: mount a `<ToastProvider>` near your app root and call `toast(...)` from the `useToast()` hook to enqueue auto-dismissing toasts that stack over the app.

On the web and iOS the toast is a floating card:
the overlay panel at the card corner, up to 380px wide, with the intent glyph in its status color (the accent's sparkle on a neutral toast), a medium message over a muted description, and the action in the accent. A `brief` toast hugs its one line.
Android keeps the Material 3 snackbar on the inverse fill.

For a single brief notification, use `<ToastProvider single brief safeArea duration={2800}
bottomInset={28} horizontalInset={20}>`. New messages replace the current toast and
restart its lifetime. `safeArea` includes the device safe area. `brief` retains a
single line without the dismiss
control; Android retains its snackbar skin.

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: Small floating helper text on hover or focus.

props.name: children
props.description: An arbitrary element for the tip to hang off: an existing Button, Chip, or any other control that already owns its own press and accessible name. The highest-precedence trigger: children win over `iconTrigger`, `textTrigger`, and the default Button. The child renders as-is and stays the single interactive, labelled element; the root view Tooltip wraps it in takes no accessibility role and no tab stop, listens only for hover and focus, and never claims the press, so a Button child keeps its `onPress` and the tip does not toggle on tap.

props.name: label
props.description: The tip text shown in the bubble.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The element the tip describes. By default rendered as a text `<Button outline small>`; set `iconTrigger` for a ghost icon button, `textTrigger` to hang the tip off an inline pressable word, or pass `children` to wrap an element you already have. Ignored when `children` is passed.

props.name: iconTrigger
props.description: Render the trigger as a ghost icon button (a settings glyph) instead of the text Button. When set, `trigger` (the label string) is ignored. Ignored when `children` is passed, which takes precedence.

props.name: textTrigger
props.description: Render the `trigger` string as a pressable inline word (an underlined hover-text affordance) rather than the default text Button, so the tip can hang off a run of body copy. Orthogonal to placement (top/left/right/bottom). Ignored when `children` or `iconTrigger` is set, both of which take precedence.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled visibility. Omit for uncontrolled: the tip shows while the trigger is hovered or focused, and a tap toggles it (the touch analogue of hover) on the built-in triggers. An element trigger (`children`) has no tap toggle (the child keeps its own press), and native platforms never fire hover, so `open` is the native and touch path for that trigger.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fired when the bubble is shown/hidden.

props.name: top
props.description: Placement (pick one; default is top).

props.name: bottom
props.description: Placement (pick one; default is top).

props.name: left
props.description: Placement (pick one; default is top).

props.name: right
props.description: Placement (pick one; default is top).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: The tip text shown in the bubble
Fired when the bubble is shown/hidden
Placement
groups.note: Placement (pick one; default is top).

platformNotes.web:
Small floating helper text on hover or focus.

The bubble floats over the page: it is drawn in the overlay layer of the nearest
`OverlayProvider`, placed against its trigger, and changes no layout, so a tip on a
table row's action never grows the cell. It centers on the trigger at the side you
pick, flips to the opposite side when the visible area has no room there, and slides
to stay inside it. Moving the pointer from the trigger onto the bubble keeps it up.
With no `OverlayProvider` mounted it still floats, on an absolute anchor beside the
trigger, but an ancestor that clips its content can then cut it off.

The bubble inverts against the page (dark in the light scheme, light in the dark one)
and sets its text in Dark Factory's label type;
iOS, which has no tooltip, shows the
same bubble, and Android keeps the Material 3 plain tooltip.

The trigger is a boolean axis of its own, resolved first match wins:

- `children`, an element you already have (an icon `Button`, a `Chip`, any
  control that owns its own press and accessible name). The child renders as-is
  and the tip hangs off it through a wrapper that only LISTENS: no accessibility
  role, no tab stop, and no press of its own, so the child stays the single
  interactive, labelled element, keeps its `onPress`, and the tip never toggles
  on tap. Hover and focus on the child both raise it.
- `iconTrigger`, a ghost icon button carrying a settings glyph.
- `textTrigger`, the `trigger` string as a pressable inline word.
- Otherwise the default: the `trigger` string as an outline Button.

Hover and focus are pointer-and-keyboard affordances. Touch pointers are
skipped,
and iOS and Android never fire hover at all.
On touch the built-in
triggers toggle the tip on tap (tap again to close it; a tip is never modal, so a
tap elsewhere goes to the page). A long press is not taken: it belongs to the
platform and to the control. An element trigger has no tap toggle either, because
that press belongs to the child, so on native and on touch the controlled `open`
prop is the way to show its tip: drive it from whatever the platform does offer (a
long press the child handles, a selected row, an inline help toggle). Keyboard
focus, including a hardware keyboard on a tablet, raises the tip on every platform.

Escape hides an open tip and leaves focus where it is (WCAG 1.4.13: hover and focus
content is dismissable without moving the pointer or focus). It goes through the kit's
one Escape owner, so a tip inside a Dialog or Popover closes first and the next Escape
reaches its host; a closed tip takes no Escape at all. A controlled tip reports the
close through `onOpenChange(false)`.
On iOS the same close answers the accessibility
escape (the VoiceOver two-finger scrub, and Escape on a hardware keyboard under Full
Keyboard Access).
Android delivers no Escape key to a view, and its back gesture is
never taken for a tip, so there the tip closes with focus or the controlled `open`.

components.name: Treemap
components.description: Squarified value tiles: each datum becomes a ramp-colored rectangle whose area is proportional to its value, packed largest-first with near-square aspect ratios, with the label and formatted value rendered inside only when the tile fits them.

props.name: data
props.description: The tiles, laid out largest first by the squarified algorithm.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional heading shown above the tiles.

props.name: compact
props.description: Density (omit for the default 240 plot height; compact is 160).

props.name: partitioned
props.description: Slice successive values along alternating axes, keeping the data order.

props.name: outlined
props.description: Show pale series washes with colored outlines and large readable values.

props.name: plain
props.description: Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats).

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats tile values and the flag (data formatting, not styling).

props.name: selected
props.description: Press-to-inspect: the selected tile index (controlled). Pass null for none.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: Press-to-inspect: the initially selected tile (uncontrolled).

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Fired when a press selects a tile (or clears it with null).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Density
groups.note: Density (omit for the default 240 plot height; compact is 160).

platformNotes.web:
