components.name: Typography
components.description: Type scale classes for headings, body text, and helper styles.

props.name: terminal
props.description: Use the system terminal face while retaining the selected reading role and size.

props.name: section
props.description: A section heading owning its count, metadata and trailing actions.

props.name: subheading
props.description: Exact Argus reading roles; these preserve the original dense web type.

props.name: hue
props.description: Hue-keyed stage text; deep in light schemes, pastel in dark.

props.name: inverseHint
props.description: De-emphasized white ink over branded surfaces.

props.name: onTextLayout
props.description: The text's laid-out lines, as React Native reports them (each line's `y`, `height`, `ascender` and `descender`, so its baseline is `y + height - descender`): for drawing something on the text's own lines, such as an illustration over a word. Fired by the native platforms; the web does not report it.

props.name: level
props.description: The heading level assistive tech hears, independent of the visual role: a heading role exposes its own level (display and h1 at 1, h2 to h5 at 2 to 5) unless this overrides it, so `<Typography h3 level={2}>` draws the h3 size and is announced as a level-2 heading (a real `<h2>` on the web). On a non-heading role it makes the text a heading at that level. Semantics only: it never changes the look. `href` still wins (a link is not a heading).

props.name: hero
props.description: The hand-off's hero headline: the display face sized by the window, `clamp(56px, 7.2vw, 112px)` at a .94 line and -.045em tracking (56 px on a phone, 103.68 at a 1440 window, 112 from 1556 up). One per page, its lead line. A level-1 heading.

props.name: pageTitle
props.description: The hand-off's page title (a component page's name): the display face sized by the window, `clamp(40px, 5vw, 64px)` at a 1.0 line and -.04em tracking. A level-1 heading.

props.name: sectionTitle
props.description: A page section's heading (a component page's Playground, Variants...): the display face, 500 28/1.1, -.02em. A level-2 heading.

props.name: cardTitle
props.description: A feature card's title: the display face, 500 22/1.15, -.02em. A level-3 heading.

props.name: panelTitle
props.description: A panel's or dialog's title: the display face, 500 20/1.2, -.02em.

props.name: tagline
props.description: The one-line tagline under a section's title: the display face, 400 22/1.3, -.015em, in the foreground ink.

props.name: pageLead
props.description: A page's summary under its title: 400 18/1.55 in the secondary ink.

props.name: sectionLead
props.description: A section's introductory paragraph: 400 17/1.55 in the secondary ink.

props.name: cardBody
props.description: A feature card's description: 400 14/1.55 in the secondary ink.

props.name: sectionNote
props.description: The note under a page section's heading: 400 14/1.5 in the secondary ink.

props.name: pageBody
props.description: A page's body paragraph (a component page's usage line): 400 15/1.6 in the secondary ink, held to an 80ch measure.

props.name: pageNote
props.description: A page's note paragraph (a component page's overview and docs notes): 400 14/1.6 in the secondary ink, held to an 80ch measure.

props.name: pageLabel
props.description: A page's label (a panel's "Props", a rail's group header, a table's header cell, a previous/next eyebrow): 500 11/1 tracked .08em in caps, in the subtle ink. Pass `mono` for the mono face, as the other page roles do. Not the `eyebrow`, which is the type table's accent-ink label tracked .1em.

props.name: knobLabel
props.description: A knob panel's label row (a knob's name, and the type hint beside it with `muted`, the third ink): 500 12/1 in the secondary ink. Pass `mono` for the mono face, as the hand-off's page does.

props.name: guideTitle
props.description: A guidance card's title: 600 16/1.3 in the interface face. A level-3 heading.

props.name: guideBody
props.description: A guidance card's paragraph: 400 13.5/1.6 in the secondary ink.

props.name: pagerName
props.description: A pager card's name (the previous or next page under its label): the display face, 500 18 on the face's own 22 line, in the foreground ink.

props.name: specMeta
props.description: A reference sheet's meta cell (a props table's type or default): 400 12/1.55 in the foreground ink. Pass `mono` for the mono face and `subtle` or `muted` for the ink, as the sheet's cells take them.

props.name: specText
props.description: A reference sheet's text cell (a props table's description, an inherited-props note): 400 13/1.55 in the secondary ink.

props.name: pagerLabel
props.description: A pager card's label (Previous, Next): the page label's 500 11 tracked .08em in caps and subtle ink on the face's own 14 line (the hand-off sets no ratio there). Pass `mono` for the mono face, as the page label takes it.

props.name: legendLabel
props.description: A legend row's label (an anatomy part's name beside its numbered disc): 500 14 on the face's own 18 line, in the foreground ink.

props.name: tileCaption
props.description: A specimen tile's caption strip (a size or state name under its well): 500 12 on the face's own 16 line, in the secondary ink. Pass `mono` for the mono face.

props.name: variantTitle
props.description: A variant card's title (an example's label over its note and snippet): 500 14/1.3 in the interface face and the foreground ink.

props.name: linkName
props.description: A link tile's name (a related component beside its arrow): 600 14 on the face's own 18 line, in the foreground ink.

props.name: subsectionTitle
props.description: A page section's own sub-heading (the "Related components" title over its tiles): 600 16 on the face's own 20 line in the interface face. A level-3 heading.

props.name: cardNote
props.description: A section card's foot caption, or a note inside the card: 400 12/1.6 (19.2) in the subtle ink. Pass `mono` for the mono face, as the hand-off sets it.

props.name: codeLabel
props.description: A code name on its own line (a variant row's label, a token's name): 400 12 on the mono face's 16 line, in the secondary ink. Pass `mono` for the mono face.

props.name: inlineNote
props.description: A short note beside a specimen: 400 12 on the interface face's 15 line, in the subtle ink.

props.name: tileTitle
props.description: A tile's title: the display face, 500 15/1.3 (19.5), in the foreground ink.

props.name: gridLabel
props.description: A grid widget's label: 500 10 mono tracked .08em in caps on a 13 line, in the subtle ink.

props.name: tick
props.description: A scale's tick label: 500 10 mono on a 13 line, in the secondary ink.

props.name: rowLabel
props.description: A stat row's label: 500 11/1 mono tracked .06em in caps, in the subtle ink.

props.name: rowValue
props.description: A stat row's value beside its label: the display face, 500 22/1, -.02em, in the foreground ink.

props.name: headlineValue
props.description: A card's headline figure: the display face, 500 26/1, -.02em, in the foreground ink.

props.name: bigNumber
props.description: A card's big number: the display face, 500 40/1, -.03em, in the foreground ink.

props.name: unit
props.description: The unit after a figure: 400 16 on the interface face's 20 line, in the subtle ink. Nest it inside the figure's Typography so it shares the figure's baseline (`<Typography bigNumber>107<Typography unit> components</Typography></Typography>`).

props.name: paneTitle
props.description: A pane's title: the display face, 500 16/1.2, -.01em, in the foreground ink. Pass `level` to announce it as a heading.

props.name: sampleLabel
props.description: A sample's caption (a hue number, a series name): 400 11 on the mono face's 14 line, in the subtle ink. Pass `mono`.

props.name: sampleMeta
props.description: A sample's meta line (a hex value, a size): 400 10 on the mono face's 13 line, in the subtle ink. Pass `mono`.

props.name: base
props.description: The 14 px body in the foreground ink: 400 14 on the interface face's 18 line (a description list's value).

props.name: inline
props.description: With `code`: the prose code chip, a word of code inside a sentence. Regular weight at .88 of the surrounding reading role's size (pass that role beside it, `lead`, `small`, `pageBody`, `pageNote`, `pageLead` or `sectionLead`; body when none), the chip's own small corner, 1 by 5 padding, the surface fill and a hairline rim. Natively a Text nested in a Text draws the fill and horizontal padding only. Without `code` it does nothing.

props.name: subtle
props.description: Tone (pick one; orthogonal to role). When omitted, the role's own color is used.

props.name: primary
props.description: Tone (pick one; orthogonal to role). When omitted, the role's own color is used.

props.name: destructive
props.description: Tone (pick one; orthogonal to role). When omitted, the role's own color is used.

props.name: success
props.description: Tone (pick one; orthogonal to role). When omitted, the role's own color is used.

props.name: warning
props.description: Tone (pick one; orthogonal to role). When omitted, the role's own color is used.

props.name: cyan
props.description: The fixed cyan series hue (the hand-off's `--cyan`, `chart-2`) as an ink, whatever the palette, solved to 4.5:1 on the scheme's surfaces.

props.name: mint
props.description: The fixed mint series hue (the hand-off's `--mint`, `chart-3`) as an ink, whatever the palette, solved like `cyan`.

props.name: regular
props.description: Weight (pick one; orthogonal to role). When omitted, the role's own weight is used.

props.name: medium
props.description: Weight (pick one; orthogonal to role). When omitted, the role's own weight is used.

props.name: semibold
props.description: Weight (pick one; orthogonal to role). When omitted, the role's own weight is used.

props.name: bold
props.description: Weight (pick one; orthogonal to role). When omitted, the role's own weight is used.

props.name: tightLeading
props.description: Leading (orthogonal to role). Pulls the line box in to 1.25x the font size for a STACKED LOCKUP, where two lines read as one unit (a wordmark over its tagline, a title over its subtitle) and the roles reading leading would leave dead air between them. Only ever tightens, so it is safe on every role. Omit for prose: the role's own line height is the reading value.

props.name: natural
props.description: Leading: the face's own normal line at the role's size, the line the hand-off's text takes where it sets a size with no ratio (JetBrains Mono 10, 11 and 12 px on 13, 14 and 16; Instrument Sans 12, 13 and 14 on 15, 16 and 18; Bricolage Grotesque 14 and 15 on 17 and 18). The face is the one the text is set in (`mono`, a display role, or the interface face). A size off the measured table (10 to 28 px) keeps the role's line.

props.name: underline
props.description: Decoration (orthogonal to role / tone / weight). Underlines the text so an inline text link reads as a link, replacing the banned raw `textDecorationLine` style shim. Combines freely with every role, tone, and weight; omit for undecorated text.

props.name: italic
props.description: Slant (orthogonal to role / tone / weight / decoration). Sets the text in the face's italic, for a word set off in prose or the italic mark of a formatting toolbar. Omit for upright text.

props.name: tabular
props.description: Numerals (orthogonal to role / tone / weight). Tabular figures: every digit the same width, for numbers read down a column or updated in place (a table's figures, a live metric, a counter), so the column lines up and a changing value holds still. Never for prose, which keeps the face's own proportional figures.

props.name: href
props.description: Renders this text as a REAL inline link on the web: react-native-web gives the root element a browser link with this destination, so middle-click, cmd-click, and open-in-new-tab work and assistive tech hears a link. Native platforms have no browser links and ignore it, so pair `href` with an `onPress` running the same navigation through the host's router. Combine with `underline` for the conventional link look. When a heading role and `href` are both set, the link role wins.

props.name: hrefAttrs
props.type: { target?: "_blank" | "_self"; rel?: string; download?: boolean | string; } | undefined
props.description: Attributes forwarded with `href` on the web: `target`, `rel`, `download`.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Press handler; the native navigation path for `href` (fires on web too).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: For layout/positioning composition only (margins handled by Row/Column). Not a styling escape hatch: size, color, and weight come from the props above.

groups.title: Role
groups.note: Role (pick one; default is the plain body style). First-match precedence.

groups.title: Tone
groups.note: Tone (pick one; orthogonal to role). When omitted, the role's own color is used.

groups.title: Weight
groups.note: Weight (pick one; orthogonal to role). When omitted, the role's own weight is used.

platformNotes.web:
Type scale classes for headings, body text, and helper styles.

`terminal` selects the system terminal face while retaining the reading role, size, weight, and ink: pair it with `tiny`, `caption`, `small`, or a heading. The web uses the system monospace stack beginning with `ui-monospace`, SFMono-Regular, and Menlo; native platforms use Menlo or their monospace alias. Existing `mono` and code typography keep their current behavior.

Argus reading roles include `subheading`, `label`, `micro`, `tag`, `eyebrow`,
`eyebrowLg`, `stageLabel`, `statValue`, `metricValue`, and `formValue`. These extend
Typography itself. Semantic leading and tracking props preserve the reference's
fractional web metrics; for example `labelLeading` is the compact label line box
and `wideTracking` its uppercase eyebrow tracking. `extraBold` selects the 800 face.
The owner's exact-reference directive preserves the existing 9.5px eyebrows.

`foreground`, `inverse`, `action`, `actionForeground`, and `info` name the ink;
`hue` gives a stage its theme-aware identity text. `inverseHint`, `inverseSubtle`,
`inverseMuted`, `inverseSoft`, and `inverseFaint` express the reference's hierarchy
on branded surfaces. `numberOfLines` truncates a reading block, and accessible
labels and roles stay with the text. Existing roles and defaults keep working.

`section` lets a heading own its `count`, muted `description` and trailing `actions`.
They wrap along a shared baseline, preserving dense section anatomy. Pair it with
`h5 bold labelLeading` or `subheading bold labelLeading`; the latter uses the compact
metadata metrics. Actions move to the far edge and wrap below on narrow surfaces.

`level={1..6}` sets the heading level assistive tech hears without changing the
look. A heading role exposes its own level (`hero`, `pageTitle`, `display` and `h1` at 1, `sectionTitle` at 2, `cardTitle` at 3, `h2` to `h5` at
2 to 5, a `section` heading 6), so `<Typography h3 level={2}>` draws the h3 size
and is announced as a level-2 heading: a real `<h2>` on the web, the header trait
natively. On a non-heading role `level` makes the text a heading at that level.
`href` still wins: a link is never a heading. The level is a number because it is
the document outline, not a style (the same reason Row's `span` is one); the look
stays on the boolean role axis.

`hero` and `pageTitle` are the two fluid headlines, sized by the window rather than a
fixed step: `hero` is the landing headline (56 to 112 px at 7.2 percent of the window,
a .94 line, tracked -.045em) and `pageTitle` a page's own title (40 to 64 px at 5
percent, a 1.0 line, tracked -.04em). Both are medium-weight display face.

The page roles are the hand-off pages' own titles and leads, outside its type table:
`sectionTitle` (a page section's heading, display 500 28/1.1), `cardTitle` (a feature
card's title, display 500 22/1.15), `panelTitle` (a panel's title, display 500 20/1.2),
`tagline` (the line under a section's title, display 400 22/1.3), `pageLead` (a page's
summary, 18/1.55, held to the hand-off's 72ch measure), `sectionLead` (a section's introduction, 17/1.55), `cardBody` (a feature
card's description, 14/1.55), `sectionNote` (the note under a section's heading,
14/1.5), `pageBody` (a page's body paragraph, 15/1.6) and `pageNote` (a page's note paragraph,
14/1.6), the last six in the secondary ink and the last two held to an 80ch measure.
Four more are the component page's own: `pageLabel` (a panel's "Props", a rail's group
header, a table's header cell, a previous/next eyebrow: 500 11/1 tracked .08em in caps, in
the subtle ink; pass `mono` for the mono face, as the hand-off's page does), `knobLabel` (a
knob panel's label row, a knob's name and its type hint: 500 12/1 in the secondary ink, the
hint beside it in the `muted` tone, the third ink; pass `mono` for the mono face), `guideTitle` (a
guidance card's title, 600 16/1.3 in the interface face, a level-3 heading) and `guideBody`
(a guidance card's paragraph, 400 13.5/1.6 in the secondary ink). `pageLabel` is not the
`eyebrow`: that is the type table's accent-ink label tracked .1em. `pagerName` is the
previous or next card's name under its label: the display face, 500 18 on the face's own 22
line (the hand-off sets no ratio), in the foreground ink. Two are the reference sheet's cells
(the component page's props table): `specMeta` (a type or default cell, 400 12/1.55; pass
`mono` for the mono face and `subtle` or `muted` for the ink, as the sheet's cells take
them) and `specText` (a description cell or an inherited-props note, 400 13/1.55 in the
secondary ink).
line the same way: `pagerLabel` (the previous or next card's label over its name, the page
label's 500 11 tracked .08em in caps and subtle ink on a 14 line; pass `mono`), `legendLabel`
(a legend row's label beside its numbered disc, 500 14 on an 18 line in the foreground ink)
and `tileCaption` (a specimen tile's caption strip, 500 12 on a 16 line in the secondary ink;
pass `mono`). Three more are the component page's Variants and Tokens sections: `variantTitle`
(a variant card's title over its note and snippet, 500 14/1.3 in the foreground ink),
`linkName` (a link tile's name beside its arrow, 600 14 on the face's own 18 line in the
foreground ink) and `subsectionTitle` (a section's own sub-heading over a grid of tiles,
600 16 on the face's own 20 line in the interface face, a level-3 heading).

The section pages' card roles are the hand-off's section cards' own text, one role per
value set however many pages set it: `cardNote` (a card's foot caption or an in-card note,
400 12/1.6 in the subtle ink; pass `mono`), `codeLabel` (a code name on its own line, a
variant row's label or a token's name, 400 12 on a 16 line in the secondary ink; pass
`mono`), `inlineNote` (a note beside a specimen, 400 12 on a 15 line in the subtle ink),
`tileTitle` (a tile's title, display 500 15/1.3), `paneTitle` (a pane's title, display 500
16/1.2 tracked -.01em; pass `level` to announce it), `gridLabel` (a grid widget's label, 500
10 mono tracked .08em in caps on a 13 line, subtle ink), `tick` (a scale's tick label, 500 10
mono on a 13 line, secondary ink), `rowLabel` (a stat row's label, 500 11/1 mono tracked
.06em in caps, subtle ink), `rowValue` (the value beside it, display 500 22/1 tracked
-.02em), `headlineValue` (a card's headline figure, display 500 26/1 tracked -.02em),
`bigNumber` (a card's big number, display 500 40/1 tracked -.03em), `unit` (the unit after a
figure, 400 16 on a 20 line in the subtle ink, nested in the figure's Typography so it shares
its baseline), `sampleLabel` and `sampleMeta` (a sample's caption and meta line, 400 11 on 14
and 400 10 on 13 in the subtle ink; pass `mono`) and `base` (the 14 px body in the
foreground ink, 400 14 on an 18 line). The figures and titles rank with the titles, the
labels with the page label, and the notes, samples, unit and base with the reading roles.

`natural` sets the text on its face's own normal line at the role's size, the line the
hand-off's text takes where it sets a size with no ratio: JetBrains Mono 10, 11 and 12 px on
13, 14 and 16, Instrument Sans 12, 13 and 14 on 15, 16 and 18, Bricolage Grotesque 14 and
15 on 17 and 18 (measured in Chromium on the faces, 10 to 28 px). The face is the one the
text is set in: `mono`, a display role, or the interface face. It sits on the leading axis
after the fixed ratios and before `tightLeading`.

`cyan` and `mint` are two inks on the tone axis that name a fixed series hue whatever the
palette (the hand-off's `--cyan` and `--mint`, the `chart-2` and `chart-3` tokens), each
solved to 4.5:1 on the scheme's surfaces. Tone precedence: `destructive`, `warning`,
`success`, `cyan`, `mint`, `primary`, `subtle`, `muted`.

`code` is the standalone code pill (regular 13px mono on the muted fill, a 6 radius and 2
by 6 padding). `code inline` is the prose code chip, a word of code inside a sentence: the
hand-off's inline `<code>`, regular weight at .88 of the surrounding reading role's size
(pass that role beside it, `lead`, `small`, `pageBody`, `pageNote`, `pageLead` or
`sectionLead`; body when none), a 5 radius, 1 by 5 padding, the surface fill and a 1px
hairline rim. The chip keeps its regular weight inside a strong run, as the hand-off
applies bold and code independently. Under glass the fill is the same ink tint the pill
takes. Natively a Text nested in a Text has no border and no vertical box, so there the
chip draws its fill and horizontal padding only; `inline` without `code` does nothing.

components.name: UptimeBar
components.description: The statuspage strip: per-period status pills (operational, degraded, down, unknown) with a summary caption and edge labels.

props.name: periods
props.description: The periods to render, oldest first; each becomes one pill.

props.name: label
props.description: What the strip measures (e.g. "API"); shown in the header and leading the accessible name.

props.name: caption
props.description: A summary at the header's right (e.g. "99.98% uptime").

props.name: startLabel
props.description: Caption under the strip's left (oldest) edge (e.g. "90 days ago").

props.name: endLabel
props.description: Caption under the strip's right (latest) edge (e.g. "Today").

props.name: midLabel
props.description: Caption centred under the strip, between the edge captions (e.g. "1 incident · 2 degraded days").

props.name: compact
props.description: Density (omit for the default pill height).

props.name: detailed
props.description: Display header and taller history marks for a status overview.

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Density
groups.note: Density (omit for the default pill height).

platformNotes.web:
The statuspage strip: per-period status pills (operational, degraded, down, unknown) with a summary caption and edge labels.

The pills run in a single row, oldest on the left, colored operational green, degraded amber, down red, or unknown muted (precedence down > degraded > unknown; an unmarked period is operational). An optional `caption` summarizes the strip above it, and `startLabel`/`endLabel` caption the physical edges below. The strip is a time axis, so it keeps left-to-right ordering in every locale, and its accessible name tallies every status.

`detailed` uses a display header, taller history marks and neutral unknown periods. Hovering a period expands it with an overshooting transition; Reduced Motion keeps it still.

components.name: Video
components.description: Plays a clip with an optional poster: tap to play inline, or full transport controls (the platform's own on iOS and Android, the kit's bar on the web), with boolean fit, `autoplay`, `loop` and `muted` props.

props.name: source
props.description: The clip: a remote `{ uri }`, or a bundled asset from `require(...)`.

props.name: poster
props.description: A still shown until the clip's first frame is on screen: a remote `{ uri }` or a bundled asset.

props.name: contain
props.description: Fit: show the whole picture, letterboxed on black. The default (pick one).

props.name: cover
props.description: Fit: fill the frame, cropping the overflow (pick one).

props.name: stretch
props.description: Fit: fill the frame by distorting the aspect ratio (pick one).

props.name: autoplay
props.description: Start playing as soon as the clip is ready, unless the system asks to reduce motion. Browsers autoplay only muted clips, so pair it with `muted` on the web.

props.name: loop
props.description: Play again from the start at the end.

props.name: muted
props.description: Play without sound.

props.name: controls
props.description: Transport controls: the platform's own player controls on iOS and Android, the kit's control bar on the web.

props.name: aspectRatio
props.description: Width over height of the clip; the frame fills its parent's width at this ratio (default 16 / 9).

props.name: radius
props.description: Corner radius from the kit's radius scale (pick one): none, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl, full.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: The clip's accessible name, used in the names of its controls (default "video").

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.description: Called when playback starts or stops.

props.name: onEnd
props.description: Called when the clip plays to its end (each time round, when looping).

props.name: testID
props.description: E2E hook forwarded to the frame.

props.name: style
props.description: Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds.

groups.title: Fit
groups.note: Fit (pick one; default `contain`). How the picture fills the frame; first match wins.

platformNotes.web:
Plays a clip with an optional poster: tap to play inline, or full transport controls
(the platform's own on iOS and Android, the kit's bar on the web),
with boolean fit, `autoplay`, `loop` and `muted` props.

Give it a `source` (a `{ uri }`, or a bundled asset from `require`), an optional `poster` shown until the clip's first frame is on screen, and the clip's `aspectRatio` (width over height, 16 / 9 by default): the frame fills its parent's width at that ratio and letterboxes the picture on black, inside the v4 hand-off's frame: a 14 px corner on a hairline (`radius` picks a step of the kit's scale instead). Without `controls` it is an inline player: the whole picture is one play and pause control, a play emblem sits over the paused picture, and a spinner shows while the clip loads. With `controls` each platform shows transport its own way:
iOS and Android hand the frame to their own player controls, and the web draws
the kit's control bar under the picture, with play and pause, the elapsed time, a seek slider, the length, mute, and full screen.

`autoplay` starts a clip once it is ready unless the system asks to reduce motion; browsers autoplay only `muted` clips, and this site's own policy blocks autoplay, so the examples here play on tap. Name every clip with `accessibilityLabel`: its controls are announced as "Play", "Pause", "Seek" and "Mute" followed by that name. Playback runs through the optional `expo-video` peer; without it the frame keeps its size and poster in a labeled frame.

components.name: View
components.description: The layout primitive: a flex container that runs identically on iOS, Android, and the web. A View is a column by default.

props.name: hitSlop
props.description: This defines how far a touch event can start away from the view. Typical interface guidelines recommend touch targets that are at least 30 - 40 points/density-independent pixels. If a Touchable view has a height of 20 the touchable height can be extended to 40 with hitSlop={{top: 10, bottom: 10, left: 0, right: 0}} NOTE The touch area never extends past the parent view bounds and the Z-index of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch hits two overlapping views.

props.name: id
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing
props.description: Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior. The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value. This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background). Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default. If you do need to enable this property for an animation, consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame). If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once, saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU.

props.name: onLayout
props.description: Invoked on mount and layout changes with {nativeEvent: { layout: {x, y, width, height}}}.

props.name: pointerEvents
props.description: In the absence of auto property, none is much like CSS's none value. box-none is as if you had applied the CSS class: .box-none { pointer-events: none; } .box-none * { pointer-events: all; } box-only is the equivalent of .box-only { pointer-events: all; } .box-only * { pointer-events: none; } But since pointerEvents does not affect layout/appearance, and we are already deviating from the spec by adding additional modes, we opt to not include pointerEvents on style. On some platforms, we would need to implement it as a className anyways. Using style or not is an implementation detail of the platform.

props.name: removeClippedSubviews
props.description: This is a special performance property exposed by RCTView and is useful for scrolling content when there are many subviews, most of which are offscreen. For this property to be effective, it must be applied to a view that contains many subviews that extend outside its bound. The subviews must also have overflow: hidden, as should the containing view (or one of its superviews).

props.name: testID
props.description: Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.

props.name: nativeID
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: collapsable
props.description: Views that are only used to layout their children or otherwise don't draw anything may be automatically removed from the native hierarchy as an optimization. Set this property to false to disable this optimization and ensure that this View exists in the native view hierarchy.

props.name: collapsableChildren
props.description: Setting to false prevents direct children of the view from being removed from the native view hierarchy, similar to the effect of setting `collapsable={false}` on each child.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback that is called when the view is blurred. Note: This will only be called if the view is focusable.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback that is called when the view is focused. Note: This will only be called if the view is focusable.

props.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
props.description: Whether this view should render itself (and all of its children) into a single hardware texture on the GPU. On Android, this is useful for animations and interactions that only modify opacity, rotation, translation, and/or scale: in those cases, the view doesn't have to be redrawn and display lists don't need to be re-executed. The texture can just be re-used and re-composited with different parameters. The downside is that this can use up limited video memory, so this prop should be set back to false at the end of the interaction/animation.

props.name: focusable
props.description: Whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description: Indicates whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/tabindex for more details. Supports the following values: - 0 (View is focusable) - -1 (View is not focusable)

props.name: shouldRasterizeIOS
props.description: Whether this view should be rendered as a bitmap before compositing. On iOS, this is useful for animations and interactions that do not modify this component's dimensions nor its children; for example, when translating the position of a static view, rasterization allows the renderer to reuse a cached bitmap of a static view and quickly composite it during each frame. Rasterization incurs an off-screen drawing pass and the bitmap consumes memory. Test and measure when using this property.

props.name: isTVSelectable
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* When set to true, this view will be focusable and navigable using the Apple TV remote.

props.name: hasTVPreferredFocus
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be set to true to force the Apple TV focus engine to move focus to this view.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceX
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceY
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxTiltAngle
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 0.05.

props.name: tvParallaxMagnification
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus. Defaults to 1.0.

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponder
props.description: Does this view want to become responder on the start of a touch?

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponder
props.description: Called for every touch move on the View when it is not the responder: does this view want to "claim" touch responsiveness?

props.name: onResponderEnd
props.description: If the View returns true and attempts to become the responder, one of the following will happen:

props.name: onResponderGrant
props.description: The View is now responding for touch events. This is the time to highlight and show the user what is happening

props.name: onResponderReject
props.description: Something else is the responder right now and will not release it

props.name: onResponderMove
props.description: The user is moving their finger

props.name: onResponderRelease
props.description: Fired at the end of the touch, ie "touchUp"

props.name: onResponderTerminationRequest
props.description: Something else wants to become responder. Should this view release the responder? Returning true allows release

props.name: onResponderTerminate
props.description: The responder has been taken from the View. Might be taken by other views after a call to onResponderTerminationRequest, or might be taken by the OS without asking (happens with control center/ notification center on iOS)

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description: onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern, where the deepest node is called first. That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers. This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable. However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder. This can be handled by using the capture phase. Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component, it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture. So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start, it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description: onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern, where the deepest node is called first. That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers. This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable. However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder. This can be handled by using the capture phase. Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component, it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture. So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start, it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: accessible
props.description: When true, indicates that the view is an accessibility element. By default, all the touchable elements are accessible.

props.name: accessibilityActions
props.type: readonly Readonly<{ name: AccessibilityActionName | string; label?: string | undefined; }>[] | undefined
props.description: Provides an array of custom actions available for accessibility.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Overrides the text that's read by the screen reader when the user interacts with the element. By default, the label is constructed by traversing all the children and accumulating all the Text nodes separated by space.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Alias for accessibilityLabel https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#accessibilitylabel https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34424

props.name: accessibilityRole
props.description: Accessibility Role tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the type of element that is focused on.

props.name: accessibilityState
props.description: Accessibility State tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the state of the element currently focused on.

props.name: aria-busy
props.description: alias for accessibilityState see https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitystate

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: An accessibility hint helps users understand what will happen when they perform an action on the accessibility element when that result is not obvious from the accessibility label.

props.name: accessibilityValue
props.description: Represents the current value of a component. It can be a textual description of a component's value, or for range-based components, such as sliders and progress bars, it contains range information (minimum, current, and maximum).

props.name: onAccessibilityAction
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs an accessibility custom action.

props.name: importantForAccessibility
props.description: [Android] Controlling if a view fires accessibility events and if it is reported to accessibility services.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description: A value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within this accessibility element are hidden.

props.name: role
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services to treat UI component like a specific role.

props.name: accessibilityLabelledBy
props.description: Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props, the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props, the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: accessibilityLiveRegion
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: aria-live
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: screenReaderFocusable
props.description: Enables the view to be screen reader focusable, not keyboard focusable.

props.name: accessibilityElementsHidden
props.description: A Boolean value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within this accessibility element are hidden to the screen reader.

props.name: accessibilityViewIsModal
props.description: A Boolean value indicating whether VoiceOver should ignore the elements within views that are siblings of the receiver.

props.name: onAccessibilityEscape
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the escape gesture (scrub with two fingers).

props.name: onAccessibilityTap
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs accessibility tap gesture.

props.name: onMagicTap
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the magic tap gesture.

props.name: accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors
props.description: https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityignoresinvertcolorsios

props.name: accessibilityLanguage
props.description: By using the accessibilityLanguage property, the screen reader will understand which language to use while reading the element's label, value and hint. The provided string value must follow the BCP 47 specification (https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47). https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylanguage-ios

props.name: accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer
props.description: A Boolean value that indicates whether or not to show the item in the large content viewer. Available on iOS 13.0+ https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityshowslargecontentviewer

props.name: accessibilityLargeContentTitle
props.description: When `accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer` is set, this string will be used as title for the large content viewer. https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylargecontenttitle

props.name: accessibilityRespondsToUserInteraction
props.description: Blocks the user from interacting with the component through keyboard while still allowing screen reader to interact with it if this View is still accessible.

components.name: WaterfallChart

props.name: title

props.name: compact
props.description: Density (omit for the default plot size).

props.name: plain
props.description: Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats).

props.name: hideGrid

props.name: hideAxes
props.description: Furniture visibility.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats tick labels, the flag, and the accessible name.

props.name: selected
props.description: Scrub-to-inspect: the selected step index (controlled). Pass null for none.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: Scrub-to-inspect: the initially selected step (uncontrolled).

props.name: onSelect

props.name: testID

props.name: style

components.name: Wizard
components.description: A modal workflow with a fixed step sidebar, a title and status header, and footer actions around a bounded, scrolling body. The application owns stage content, validation, saving and transitions; Wizard composes the existing Dialog, Steps and Button controls.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled modal visibility.

props.name: title
props.description: Names the modal and its fixed header.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting text below the title.

props.name: steps
props.description: Ordered stages; the application owns their content and transitions.

props.name: current
props.description: Zero-based active stage; earlier stages read as complete.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the close action, Escape or native back requests dismissal.

props.name: panelWidth
props.description: Maximum panel width; defaults to the hand-off's 620px and shrinks to its parent.

props.name: previous
props.type: { label: string; onPress: () => void; disabled?: boolean; } | undefined
props.description: Named previous stage action at the footer's start.

props.name: actions
props.description: Application actions at the footer's end.

props.name: status
props.description: Save/progress status beside the title in the fixed header.

props.name: scrollBody
props.description: Scroll the body (default true). Set false when a child, such as Chat, owns its scroll.

props.name: embedded
props.description: Show the open wizard as a non-modal specimen, for a catalogue or a showcase: it keeps its look, its dialog role and its labelling, but does not take focus, trap Tab, claim `aria-modal`, or close on Escape or native back. It renders in place, in the flow of the page, as Dialog's contained form does, rather than presenting into an OverlayProvider.

props.name: testID
props.description: Prefix for modal, steps, body-scroll and footer test hooks.
